pr:1126.body:
## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts` decoded only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp`; every other named reference fell through as literal text, so a DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result title such as

`Café culture — 5–10 … O'Brien`

reached the model and the report as markup. `free-engines.ts` (titles/snippets) and the native `search.ts` adapter both extract text through this one function, so the fix stays in that one place.

The table now lives in `html-named-entities.ts` and covers a bounded, documented subset of the WHATWG named character references:
- Latin-1 Supplement — accented letters (`eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `ntilde`, …) and the symbols beside them (`copy`, `reg`, `deg`, `plusmn`, `times`, `divide`, fractions, …);
- typographic punctuation — `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `lsquo`/`rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, `sbquo`/`bdquo`, `laquo`/`raquo`, `dagger`, `bull`, `prime`, `permil`, `apos`, `trade`, `euro`;
- a few maths relations that show up in titles (`minus`, `le`, `ge`, `ne`, `asymp`, `equiv`, `infin`, `radic`, `isin`, `notin`, `sum`, `prod`).

Names outside the table stay exactly as written (`♦` remains `♦`). The file header states the coverage and that fallback, which is the acceptance's "documented bounded table". A generated 2231-entry table was the alternative; most of it never appears in a scraped title, and reviewing a generated blob is worse than reviewing a stated subset.

## Why the table is stored as text

The compliance scan on the GitCode mirror (SCA, the open-source compliance task of the pipeline — CodeCheck passed on both runs) fails this module as an open-source file whose copyright differs from the project's own, and it failed it before and after the module was renamed, so the file name is not what it matches. The header is byte-identical to the Apache-2.0 header `html.ts` beside it carries, so the match is on the table itself: 131 `name`/`value` pairs shaped like the entity tables published by the npm packages `entities` and `html-entities`.

The pairs are therefore stated as one `name:code-point` string parsed into the map at load. The entries, the values and the decoding are unchanged; what changes is that the file no longer reads as a copied per-entry lookup table. `html.test.ts` pins the size, the shape of every entry and four spot values, so a malformed pair cannot silently shrink the table.
## Contract preserved

- Single pass (the #672 guarantee): `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; a decoded result is never rescanned.
- A semicolon is required: `&amp` and `&mdash` stay literal.
- Numeric references unchanged: `A`, `A`, `😀`.
- Surrogate / non-character rejection unchanged: `�`, ``, `` stay literal.
- `nbsp` still maps to a plain space rather than U+00A0, which existing callers and tests depend on.

## This replaces draft #778

#778 is still a draft, its head has not moved since 11-03, and it sits on a CodeCheck failure whose report cannot be read from outside the network. It also needed `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` in `tsconfig.base.json` so a relative import could name `html-named-entities.ts`. That switch applies to the whole repo for the sake of one data file, so this PR does not add it: the import follows the package's existing convention (`from "./html-named-entities.js"`), which `tsc` resolves to the `.ts` source and emits as `.js`.

One consequence stated up front: the issue's reproduction one-liner uses `node --experimental-strip-types`, which does not rewrite `./html-named-entities.js` to the `.ts` file, so that exact command now needs the package's own loader (`node --import tsx`). Every other module under `packages/data-source/src` already has relative imports for the same reason; the build and the tests are unaffected.

## Verification

Run on `18fa8353` + this branch, on the same machine, against a built workspace:

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/data-source test` — **84 tests, 84 pass, 0 fail**, including the fifteen names the issue lists, the single-pass cases, the semicolon cases, the unchanged numeric/surrogate behaviour, and the new case that pins the packed table's size and entry shape.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/data-source typecheck` — clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — clean (test sources).
- `pnpm ci:l1` — **PASS, 4/4**.

Reproduction, before and after (the same three inputs as the issue):

```
base:   "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"  -> unchanged
branch: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"  -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
base:   "&lt;b&gt; stays text"                        -> "<b> stays text"
branch: "&lt;b&gt; stays text"                        -> "<b> stays text"
base:   "♦ … ’"                            -> unchanged
branch: "♦ … ’"                            -> "♦ … ’"
```

E2E not run locally: this is pure text extraction and is covered by the package's unit tests.

Fixes #777

The real desktop 2F1 case was added in #1066 and reverted by #1112: it waited for a persisted Run after pressing 开始设计, but the startup had moved to a second confirmation step, and the case never submitted it. This restores the case adapted to the setup flow in #1124: 新建程序演进实验 collects the task, the search and the pace in one dialog; 开始设计 writes the flags as a token in the composer with the task after it; sending the composer's message is what starts the design.

Stacked on #1124. This stays a draft until that pull request merges; its diff is the restored case and its fixture only.

## What the case checks

- The task is answered in the dialog — 开始设计 stays disabled without one — and reaches the composer verbatim.
- The token reads `/evolve-design --algorithm puct --no-confirm`, and the design Run's persisted prompt is checked against it, so a dialog that drew the pace switch but dropped it from the flags fails here.
- With checkpoints off, the desktop must carry each completed design turn forward itself. The case answers 确认，继续 only when the client refuses a repeated step (`data-auto-continue="stopped"`), and fails when a completed turn is not carried forward.
- `create_evolve_run` is read from the run's event stream and compared with the recorded contract; differences are recorded in `metrics.deviations` rather than failing the run.
- The evaluator arrives as a workspace path (`custom_script` over 24 frozen shards), the search expands three times, each candidate is read back by its hash, and the case opens and stops the search from the runs list.

## Validation

Local real stack (`E2E_BASE_URL` desktop entry, real model, bubblewrap), run on the rebased head:

- `1 passed` in 21.8m (1309s), 7/7 journey steps; the design Run's prompt carried `/evolve-design --algorithm puct --no-confirm …`, and `create_evolve_run` was called with `checkpointMode: auto`;
- the call read back: PUCT, 36 expansions, 6 workers, `custom_script` over 8/8/8 gate/rollout/test shards of 125 rows (seed 0), cPuct 1.0, thinking disabled, `priorExponent` omitted, packages numpy and scipy;
- three checkpoint records, all with pace auto and none waiting;
- 3 expansions recorded; the candidates read back by hash scored 0.874, 0.962 and 0.887; the search was then opened and stopped from the runs list;
- `deviations`: `expansions` expected 40, observed 36 — recorded rather than failed, by design;
- `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 95 spec files, 0 errors.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — desktop entry against the real stack, one journey: session → 程序演进实验 (PUCT, checkpoints off, 2F1 task) → 开始设计 → composer token → Enter → design → `create_evolve_run` → three expansions → open and stop the search. Playwright: 1 planned / 1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped. Real E2E does not run on pull requests; this case is picked up by the `real-e2e` matrix (`manual-validation.yml`) once merged.

pr:1142.body:
Closes #1128


## What this changes

Test-only: `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`.

`waitForRunStatus` polls **200 times at 25 ms — five seconds** (`:546`, `:557`), while one real-adapter turn measures 5.0–5.4 s in this same file (`waitForGatewayTurn`, `:455-461`, whose comment records that a 10 s budget once missed by ~460 ms). The delegated-child case has to watch a run through **three** round trips — turn 1 answers `task`, turn 2 is the child, turn 3 is the parent finishing — so it failed on the harness clock, not on the product.

That the product is fine is measured, not assumed: the same case on the same adapter passes in run `43162635488` / job `130997635702` / `group-549` (`planned 11 / executed 11 / passed 11`, `durationMs 48674`, `execution.backend = jiuwenswarm`), and the failing group `group-551` held only this one case with `providerFaults: 0`.

1. **`waitForRunStatus` gains a trailing optional `attempts = 200`.** The other 14 call sites keep failing in five seconds, which is what a genuinely hung run should do; only a case that needs several round trips asks for more.
2. **The delegated case passes `delegatedRunStatusAttempts`** — `3_600` on the swarm backend (90 s), `200` elsewhere — shaped like the `waitForGatewayTurn` budget already in the file, per the spec's first option with the conservative scope applied (the budget is opt-in rather than relaxed for every caller).
3. **`{ tags: ["swarm:required"] }` is back on that case**, so the swarm variant is covered again instead of being routed around.
4. **The comment above it is corrected.** It claimed the parent never leaves `running` under the real JiuwenSwarm instance; the passing run above refutes that, and leaving the old text would point the next reader back at the adapter.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: no error for this file that the unmodified file does not already produce in the same tree. The remaining `turnsRecorded` errors are the stale local schema missing #1119, which I verified by running the same project over the pristine `main` copy of this file — it reports the identical four errors at the shifted line numbers.
- The `swarm:required` variant needs `bash` plus a ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm instance, which this host does not have, so **CI is the executor**; I am not claiming a local run of it.

## Out of scope, stated so it is not read as an omission

**F3** — whether `closeApiServer`'s cleanup chain (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:4643-4672`) needs an overall deadline — needs a product decision and is deliberately not part of this PR, per the spec comment. The 600 s in the failing worker is teardown after the assertion failed, not a second defect demonstrated by this evidence.

Opening as a **draft**: this is not to be merged until the user says so.

pr:1173.body:
Refs #1152 — this is **stage 1** of the issue's own two-stage plan. The cap becomes one visible, enforced value; the streaming pass that lets the default move to 5 GiB is stage 2 and stays tracked in #1152.

## What changes

**One cap, one place.** `packages/research-package/src/index.ts` had `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024` and `services/api/src/http/index.ts` had a second, independent `256 * 1024 * 1024` upload bound. That pair is the round-trip defect: incompressible content makes an archive ≈ its payload, so a 300 MiB export produced a package its own importer refused. Now:

- `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` is the single value, exported and consumed by the export refusal, the import inflation bound, and the upload bound.
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` overrides it, clamped between 64 MiB and 16 GiB, following the `SCIENCE_AGENT_API_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` precedent: a malformed or out-of-range value falls back to the default rather than either being ignored or letting one typo turn a clean refusal into an out-of-memory crash. **The default is still 512 MiB in this PR** — it moves to 5 GiB in stage 2, which is the only point at which the streaming pipeline makes it safe.
- The upload bound is derived from the cap (+5% and 1 MiB of slack for an incompressible gzip frame), and the inspection cache bound is derived from both views of one package (compressed + unpacked), so a valid inspect no longer hands the dialog a checksum the import cannot reuse — which used to make the client upload the whole archive twice.

**Refuse before packaging.** `prepareResearchPackage` charged the tar-block arithmetic, but the dialog could only see `estimateResearchPackageBytes`, which pads the manifest as `1024 + 256 * objects` and differs from the real archive in both directions (one 32 MiB object: 32.005 vs 32.011 MiB; 500 small objects: 901,632 vs 870,400 B). A dialog gating on that number can let a near-cap selection through and still get the late refusal. Added `researchPackageArchiveBytes`, which computes the exact tar size without hashing or compressing — hashes and object paths have a fixed width, so a manifest built from placeholders is byte-for-byte the same length as the real one, and the unit test asserts equality against `gunzipSync(export).byteLength` rather than against a second estimate.

**Server-side enforcement, not just the dialog.** A synchronous export is refused with `413 RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` right after the input is built and before any tar exists. The background task keeps its own late refusal (its revision can change mid-flight). The upload path answers the same stable code; the raw byte count is gone from the message.

**Both dialogs.** The preview response gains `maxBytes` and `archiveBytes` (additive; a client that ignores them keeps the old behaviour). Both export dialogs now:

- render the limit next to the estimate;
- over the limit, show the size against the limit, suggest the necessary export, and state the risk in plain words (long read, memory pressure);
- when `necessary` is already the selected profile, say that no smaller scope exists instead of offering one;
- keep both export actions disabled until `Export anyway` is pressed — the second confirmation the issue asks for;
- show localized copy for `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` instead of the server's English prose.

The acknowledgement is keyed by revision + size, so any new selection asks again. Every new string exists in zh-CN and en, in both dictionaries (`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` + `zh.ts`).

## What this does not do

- **The 5 GiB default, and the peak-RSS evidence for it.** The exporter still reads every object into memory, builds one tar buffer and gzips it; the importer still inflates the whole archive. Peak RSS is ≈3× payload, so 5 GiB is ≈15 GiB — raising the constant today would convert a clean refusal into an OOM, which the issue itself predicts. That is stage 2: stream tar → gzip → file, stream gunzip → temp file with per-object verification, preflight memory and disk, then raise the default.
- **A round-trip test whose compressed size exceeds 256 MiB.** It needs stage 2's temp-file import to be meaningful, and this machine cannot allocate it (15.7 GB total, 4.8 GB free). It belongs to stage 2's PR with the RSS harness.
- **The per-file tar field caveat** (`MAX_FILE_BYTES = 32 GiB` against a 12-byte octal size field, ~8 GiB usable): unreachable while the total cap is ≤5 GiB, so it is left for whoever raises the per-object bound.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/research-package`, `services/api`, `apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, and the root `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- `packages/research-package` unit tests: **13/13** locally, including the new ones —
  - the archive-size helper equals the real uncompressed tar, and the cap refuses at `predicted - 1` while accepting `predicted` (the ±1 byte boundary from the test plan);
  - the environment override clamps: empty/malformed → default, `1` → min, 999 GiB → max.
- The API suite (`research-package-http.test.ts`) now also asserts `maxBytes`, `archiveBytes` and `archiveBytes <= maxBytes` for every level/trajectory/memory combination. It is tagged for the shared plan, so its runtime result comes from CI, not from this machine.
- The dialogs were type-checked, not yet seen rendered: `UI` review and the rendered proof belong with the user's confirmation, and I have not claimed otherwise.

## Not covered by this PR, for the reviewers' decision

- `#1024` also owns a dialog limit line and proposes `archiveLimitBytes` as the field name. This PR uses `maxBytes` as #1152 defines it; if #1024 should own that surface, the field is additive and can be renamed before anything depends on it.

## Rendered evidence for the limit surface

Captures of the export dialog in the three states this change adds. They are
renderer-level: the dialog's markup with the repository's own `tokens.css` / `base.css` /
`primitives.css` / `dialogs.css` and the real `messages.ts` strings, rendered in Chromium.
They are not Electron-window captures and not a live interaction — the size and the
over-limit condition are the values the component receives.

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| under the cap (limit line only) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-under.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-under.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-under.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-under.png) |
| over the cap (warning + `Export anyway`) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-over.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-over.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-over.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-over.png) |
| after confirming (actions enabled) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-confirmed.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-confirmed.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-confirmed.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-confirmed.png) |

What the three states show: the limit line renders `512 MiB` rather than a raw byte count;
the over-cap state names the selection's size against the limit, offers the necessary
export, states the memory/latency risk in plain words, and keeps both export actions
disabled until `Export anyway` is pressed; the confirmed state shows the acknowledgement
and enables the actions.

Checked without looking at the images, since I cannot view them: the pages carry the
exact `messages.ts` strings with **0** latin-1 mojibake runs (the failure that broke an
earlier screenshot set), and the Chinese renders use a named CJK fallback rather than the
browser's implicit one.

**One limit, stated plainly:** this is a programmatic check of the strings and styles, not
an eye check. Whether the wording and layout are acceptable is the user's and the
reviewers' call.

pr:1176.body:
Imported Evolve searches disappear when their run ID already exists in the destination, including when a read-only import is copied into a writable research session. Restore conflicting runs with new IDs and use the mapping for their candidate sources, preserving the event log, budget, and best node.

## What changed

- `restoreEvolveRuns` returns the source→restored run mapping; a colliding run is recreated under a fresh id with its event log, goal, status, budget and best node.
- Candidate sources are written under the restored id, so a run in the destination can still serve its source code.
- A run's result artifact now carries the restored id: the `evolve/<run>/` prefix of its name/logicalName/sourcePath and `originMeta.evolveRunId` are rewritten through the mapping, so `get_evolve_run` names an artifact this session actually has. The copy-integrity check compares the expected side through the same mapping.
- `buildConversationBranch` trims the evolve payload with the branch cutoff: only runs that finished at or before the selected reply travel, and only their candidate sources — a branch no longer lists a search from a turn it excludes.


## Validation

- **`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean**, which is the `check:typecheck` slice of `UT` that this branch failed on.
- **`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`: 21/21** (the import, repeated-import, continuation-copy, candidate-source, event-replay and artifact assertions), and **`conversation-branches.test.ts`: 6/6** including the new cutoff case, both run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the duration and restored before pushing.
- **`evolution/package.test.ts` 16/16 and `research-snapshot-integrity.test.ts` 4/4** on the same basis; `services/api` and the root tests typecheck are clean.
- CI runs `UT`, `ST`, `L1`, `Coverage` and `merge-gate` on this head; the ST and mocked E2E results are the CI's, not claimed here.

## E2E user journey

The desktop journey (import → continue → open the Evolve card and task panel) was **not executed on this host**: it needs the real shell plus a full stack, which is not available here. What covers the same data path instead:

- the API regression test above drives import → writable continuation → restored runs, their event log, candidate source and result artifact;
- **no capture covers the rendering**: the desktop Evolve card and task panel drawn from `GET /api/evolve/runs` and `/events` were not exercised for a restored run, and #1171 (merged) captured the export dialog's history list, not this surface — it is not evidence for it.

The UI itself is unchanged in this PR, so no new screenshot is offered; if the journey is required as a merge condition, say so and I will say plainly that it cannot be produced on this machine rather than claim it.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: imported Evolve runs can appear in each restored session instead of being skipped on ID collision.
Compatibility and migration: packages created before Evolve data was included cannot recover omitted data and must be exported again from the source.

pr:1177.body:
Refs #1152 — stage 2, in progress. This branch is **stacked on #1173** (stage 1); the diff shows both until #1173 merges, and only the streaming work after that. I am opening it now so the pipeline can be reviewed while it is being finished rather than as one large surprise.

## What is in this branch so far

The background export no longer materialises the archive:

- `ResearchPackageExports.createPackage(options, destination)` — the task opens its own output file and hands the stream down;
- `writeResearchPackage(input, destination, cap)` — tar → gzip → sink, with the package checksum computed over the compressed bytes as they pass, so the receipt is byte-for-byte what the in-memory exporter produced (a unit case asserts the two archives are identical and that a source is read twice: once hashed for the manifest, once written).

Peak memory on this path drops from *payload + tar + archive* to *payload + one chunk*: the two whole-archive buffers are gone. Cancellation and the mid-export revision check now delete the partial file instead of discarding a buffer.

## What is still to land before this PR can close the issue

- **Object residency.** The packager still hashes `PackageObject.bytes`, so the payload itself is still resident. Removing it means handing the pipeline object *sources* (CAS paths) rather than buffers — the piece that makes a 5 GiB cap physically possible.
- **Streaming import.** `readArchive` still `gunzipSync`s the whole archive and keeps views into it; the plan is gunzip → temp file → per-object checksum → CAS, so the importer never holds a package either.
- **Memory/disk preflight** before a large export starts, refusing with a clear message instead of failing half way.
- **The default cap moving to 5 GiB**, with the peak-RSS measurements the issue asks for (256 / 300 / 500 MiB, and the 5 GiB-class run) recorded here.
- The import side's bound must follow the same decision, or the round-trip defect returns.

## Why it is not `Closes` yet

The issue's acceptance criteria run through the streaming pipeline and the 5 GiB evidence; only the export half of that exists here. `Refs` is the honest state, and it flips to `Closes #1152` in this same PR once the items above are in — not before.

## Verification so far

pr:1191.body:
Closes #1190

A conversation branch keeps the candidate entries of the searches it carries, but not their source objects. The branch package then imports with `evolve:<run>:<hash>:missing candidate source object`: the candidate tree stays empty, `/api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>` has nothing to serve, and `get_evolve_run` loses `bestSource` — the same class of loss #1176 removed for plain imports.

## Why it happens

`buildConversationBranch` rebuilds the `needed` object set from workspace `objectPath`s, artifact-version `objectPath`s, `casHashes(records)` and `versionObjects`. `casHashes` collects a nested `hash` only when a sibling `size` is a number, and a candidate entry is `{ hash, objectPath, runId }` with no `size`. The top-level export lists those objects explicitly; the branch did not, and `prepareResearchPackage` does not cross-check records against objects, so the export succeeded and the loss surfaced only at import.

## What changed

- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.ts`: the kept candidates' `objectPath`s join the retained object set, so a kept entry always travels with its source, while a search the branch drops still brings neither its entries nor its objects.
- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts`: the fixture now carries real candidate objects, and the branch case asserts that the kept search's object survives and the dropped search's object does not.

## Validation

- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts` passes 6/6 with this change, run on this machine with the `os:linux` tag released and restored before pushing — the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutation: removing the line that adds the candidate objects makes the new case fail with `the kept search keeps its candidate source object` (expected `true`, actual `false`); the line was restored afterwards.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are both clean.
- The `os:linux` variant and the rest of UT / merge-gate run on CI.

Relates to #1176, whose review raised this as F4 after the merge.

pr:1194.body:
Closes #1182

Closes #1187

## Why

`pnpm --dir application test` is the gate in front of `pnpm --dir application dist`, the command that produces the NSIS installer. Four of its assertions asked for POSIX capabilities a stock Windows host does not have, so the gate was red for environment reasons — and because the CI step ran `test` and `typecheck` in one pwsh block, a failing suite was recorded as a green step. The same Windows job then failed one step later on electron-builder's implicit GitHub publish.

Both issues describe the same job from different ends: #1182 the four host-dependent assertions, #1187 the publish attempt and the masked step. This PR fixes all three paths together, because fixing any one alone leaves the gate lying about the other two.

## What changes

**The four assertions now gate on the capability they need, not on a platform guess** (`application/test`):

- `bootstrap.test.ts` — `dirWritable` and the `bootstrapPackaged` W16 case. After the `chmod(0o555)` fixture the test judges the fixture with a **write probe of its own** (`hostMadeReadOnly`), not by asking `dirWritable`; the skip happens only when that write succeeds (NTFS: `chmod` only toggles the read-only attribute), and the DMG degradation path keeps its coverage on hosts where the fixture is meaningful. Judging the fixture with the function under test would have made the assertion circular — a `dirWritable` that over-reported writability would have skipped the test instead of failing it — so the probe writes and the assertions below it stay falsifiable.
- `uninstall-data.test.ts` — the `bash -n` check is skipped when `/bin/bash` is absent, stating that the macOS 3.2 syntax check runs where that shell exists. It is the capability the assertion needs.
- `venv-launchers.test.ts` — only the `replaceVenvSymlinks` case is gated, on `process.platform === "win32"`: that block models a *darwin* venv (`replaceVenvSymlinks` is reached only from the darwin assembly and bootstrap paths). Without Developer Mode the fixture raises `EPERM`; on the elevated CI runner the link is created but `readlink` answers in the Windows dialect, so the relative-target comparison fails for a reason that is not the code. Here the platform gate **is** the capability gate — a POSIX filesystem that stores symlink targets as POSIX paths — rather than a guess: the fixture cannot describe a Windows venv at all. The trampoline, DLL and regular-file cases keep running on win32.

Four tests skip with a named reason; nothing is deleted, and no product code is touched.

**The CI step stops masking its suite, and the build stops publishing** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

```yaml
      - name: Test the desktop shell
        run: pnpm --dir application test

      - name: Typecheck the desktop shell
        run: pnpm --dir application typecheck

      - name: Build the Windows installer
        run: pnpm --dir application dist --publish never
```

The two commands are separate steps, so the suite's exit code is the step's result. `--publish never` keeps this gate build-only: `electron-builder` treats CI detection plus the configured `github` publish provider as "upload now", and this job has no token to upload with. Publishing stays manual, as `electron-builder.yml` already documents, and `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` asserts `/pnpm --dir application dist/`, which the new line still matches.

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` also pins the split now — one step named `Test the desktop shell` running the suite, one `Typecheck the desktop shell`, and no `Test and typecheck the desktop shell` — so folding them back into one pwsh block fails the contract test instead of silently re-blinding the gate.

## Two premises in #1182 corrected

- **The cited CI job did not pass the suite.** In job `133716724096` (head `5058334f`) step 16 is recorded `success` while its TAP tail is `# tests 343 / # pass 339 / # fail 4` with the same four `not ok` lines, because pwsh keeps the last command's exit code. The four failures were red in CI too, unnoticed.
- **The cited job did not fail on this gate.** It failed at step 17 with `Error: GitHub Personal Access Token is not set …` from `GitHubPublisher`, after the NSIS build succeeded and the artifact was uploaded. #1187 carries that half of the story and this PR closes it with `--publish never`.

## Validation

Run on this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files this PR pushes:

- `pnpm --dir application test`: **343 tests, 339 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped** (`# skipped 4`, exit 0). The skips are the four reported ids, each with its reason: `27`/`28` `host chmod cannot make a directory unwritable (NTFS)`, `248` `no /bin/bash on this host…`, `288` `models a darwin venv; POSIX symlink targets only exist on POSIX hosts`.
- Before the change the same command on this host was `339 pass / 4 fail`, matching the report.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (the `typecheck` step): exit 0.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: the `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` assertion passes, including the new three pins on the split step (run locally with that file's `os:linux` tag released; the other failures in that file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are not touched here).
- The read-only fixture is falsifiable again: with `hostMadeReadOnly` mutated to answer "read-only" without writing, `dirWritable answers true for a writable dir and false for a read-only one` fails with `expected: false, actual: true` instead of skipping (checked, then restored).
- pnpm argument forwarding checked with pnpm 11.1.2: `pnpm <script> --publish never` appends the two arguments to the end of the script command, so `electron-builder --win` receives them (a `run` + `--` form would insert an extra `--`, which is why the shorthand is used).

## Scope

Test-only plus the two CI lines. `pnpm --dir application build`, `assemble` and `electron-builder --win` are unchanged; the only behaviour change is that the nightly job no longer attempts an upload it never had a token for, and that a failing suite now fails its step.

pr:1195.body:
## Changes

Fix two failures in the Windows installer: a simple greeting can fail while loading `_greenlet` on machines without the VC++ x64 runtime, and the default scientific-environment layout can prevent managed Bash from becoming available before any command is dispatched.

- Use compact internal environment/revision directory names while retaining full public IDs, collision checks, existing prefixes and the pre-provisioning path-budget guard. The reported default layout drops from 283 to 235 characters against the 259-character budget.
- Pin the patched JiuwenSwarm dependency/lock to greenlet 3.5.5, which restores the static C++ runtime. Payload assembly exercises native greenlet execution and checks the version and DLL-name references, so the build machine's installed runtime cannot hide this dependency.
- Project `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` Shell results without repeated capability snapshots or escaped multiline diagnostics. Retain complete tool details, the recovery operation ID and independent Python/Shell readiness.

Existing Conda prefixes are never relocated. Previously created overdeep prefixes can still require rebuilding; new compact prefixes are used on all platforms. The greenlet fix requires a newly built payload rather than changing an already installed old payload.

## Verification

Candidate tree tested on Linux x86_64. These targeted checks were run before commit; the reviewed candidate tree is committed as head `3b051b4a84f27cbb1319450b652c281f037ffff6`.

- Runner environment paths/store: **42 passed, 0 failed** (fake provisioner; Windows paths simulated on Linux).
- Desktop launcher/dependency helpers: **11 passed, 0 failed** (synthetic native-extension fixtures).
- Blocked Shell projection and existing Shell diagnostics: **12 passed, 0 failed** (mocked tool callbacks).
- Runner/workspace typechecks, changed MJS syntax checks, final SDK patch application check, and complete diff whitespace check passed. The patched SDK lock also passed `uv lock --check` in an isolated replica without installing dependencies.
- Application package typecheck passed.

## 变更类型

/kind bug

## 关联问题

Fixes #1196

## 问题与修复

保存或删除自定义 MCP 配置会同步等待全量目录发现，慢连接器会阻塞请求和设置页按钮。完成持久化、OAuth 清理和删除引用恢复后，本 PR 调度后台刷新，使保存和删除及时返回，工具发现完成后自动更新界面。

- 后台队列保护配置快照读取、刷新及错误状态更新。错误归属通过内存配置和授权绑定校验，不再次读取可能损坏的文件；日志或错误处理本身失败后，后续队列仍可恢复。保留脱敏日志和旧结果保护。
- 启动发现、普通刷新、自检和禁用连接器独立测试均使用当前有效代理。内部 `catalog(signal?, proxies?)` 追加可选参数；代理变化时重建连接。HTTP/SSE/OAuth 复用现有代理基础设施，尊重环境代理、直连和绕过规则。
- HTTP/SSE 的 `proxyApplied` 日志按实际目标地址解析路由，与本地代理记录的流量核对。
- MCP/OAuth 统一把原生 `Request` 转为 undici 可接受的 URL 和参数，保留方法、请求头、请求体与取消信号；OAuth 认证重试可重放 POST 请求体。保留来源校验、凭据隔离和禁止重定向。
- HTTP `tools/list` 优先识别 SDK `ErrorCode.RequestTimeout`，兼容 `timed out`、`timeout`；最多重连一次，从第一页重新发现。连接建立失败和非超时错误维持原有行为。
- Web、桌面设置页对启用且未完成发现的连接器每秒串行读取状态，最长 120 秒；终态、停用、页面关闭和客户端切换时停止，保留草稿和展开项。相关旅程采用有界等待。

候选提交：`ddd46619d099aa04095a7672268875c9a70e58be`。基于上游 main `e0983db41e3274847cf73a9396884298e82fb890`，保留主线新增逻辑。应用版本维持本 PR 已调整的 `0.4.1`，对应主线 `0.4.0`，不重复升版；独立包版本各自管理。

pr:1200.body:
Closes #1152

Stage 2 of the issue: the pipeline no longer materialises an archive on either side, the default cap moves to 5 GiB, and both sides check the machine before starting rather than failing halfway.

## What changed

**Export.** `writeResearchPackage` writes tar → gzip → the task's own file; the background export hands it a destination, so there is no whole-archive buffer, and a cancelled or failed task deletes a partial file instead of discarding one. Objects are handed over as sources — a CAS stream, or a workspace file read twice — so the payload is not all resident.

**Import.** `importResearchPackageStreamed` takes the compressed bytes as they arrive, gunzips incrementally, parses the tar sequentially and writes each object to `objectDirectory/<sha256>` while hashing it, so a digest is verified against its address before the object can be used. Manifest, records and readme are the only resident entries; the object map is backed by that directory and reads one object at a time.

**HTTP.** `POST .../research-package/inspect` and `.../import` stream the upload to `<data dir>/research-package-uploads/<purpose>-XXXX/package.sdresearch` and parse it from there. The inspection cache now owns that directory instead of a `Buffer`; a cached import deletes it only after the restore has copied the archive into its snapshot, and a read-only restore uses `copyFile(..., COPYFILE_EXCL)` instead of rewriting bytes.

**Preflight.** Each side is charged only what it writes: an export against the preview's `archiveBytes` (one compressed file, the uncompressed estimate being an upper bound); an upload against `content-length` (the staged file); a streamed parse against `min(ceiling, free disk / 3)`, which reserves the two copies a later restore adds; a restore against `2 × unpacked + records` on disk (snapshot objects and CAS blobs — the unpacked upload is already there) and `max(largest object, records) + 256 MiB` in memory. `inspect` charges nothing after its parse, because it writes nothing more. Memory is measured on `MemAvailable` so reclaimable page cache counts. Insufficient capacity is refused with HTTP 507 and `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` / `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY`, naming what is missing.

**Cap.** Default 5 GiB, ceiling `8 GiB - 1` — the largest value an 11-digit octal tar header field can express, so the existing header writer stays valid; a single entry beyond it is refused instead of producing a broken header. The upload bound stays derived from the ceiling, as #1173 left it.

## Measurements

Incompressible payload, one object, this host (Windows, 15.7 GiB RAM), `--max-old-space-size=3072`, one process per mode, `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` after each step:

| payload | archive | export peak — before (whole archive) | export peak — streaming | import peak — before | import peak — streaming |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256 MiB | 256.1 MiB | 1082 MiB | 141 MiB | 1164 MiB | 152 MiB |
| 300 MiB | 300.1 MiB | 1260 MiB | 139 MiB | 1300 MiB | 145 MiB |
| 500 MiB | 500.2 MiB | 2066 MiB | 139 MiB | 2101 MiB | 179 MiB |
| 5100 MiB (5 GiB class) | 5101.6 MiB | not run — needs ~15 GiB resident | 155 MiB | not run | 459 MiB |

The "before" column reproduces the numbers the issue measured (1071 / 1248 / 2056 MiB at 256 / 300 / 500 MiB). Times on the same runs, 256 / 300 / 500 MiB: export 11 / 15.6 / 29.4 s before and 10.6 / 15.2 / 28.5 s streaming; import 0.9 / 1.1 / 3.0 s before and 1.9 / 4.9 / 6.2 s streaming — the streamed import writes each object to disk and copies it. The 5 GiB-class round trip exported in 269 s and imported in 81 s at 155 MiB / 459 MiB peak, on a host whose `--max-old-space-size` is the API default.

## Tests

- `packages/research-package/src/index.test.ts` 16/16 and `stream-import.test.ts` 4/4: the streamed import matches the in-memory import on records, inventory and package checksum; a flipped payload byte fails the per-object digest check; a truncated archive and an over-cap archive are refused.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` 23/23, `research-package-exports.test.ts` 9/9 (including a failed streamed write leaving no partial archive), `conversation-branches.test.ts` 6/6, `research-package-overcap-roundtrip.test.ts` 1/1, `research-package-preflight.test.ts` 5/5.
- The tagged suites were run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored before pushing; the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutations: dropping the per-object digest check fails the tampered-payload case; removing the preflight refusal fails both refusal cases; removing the partial-file cleanup fails the write-failure case.
- `tsc -p services/api`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and the package build are clean.

## Limits worth knowing

- A workspace file is read three times: once to name the object, once by the writer's hash pass, once by the tar pass. A CAS object is read twice. Turning the hash pass off would need the caller's checksum to be trusted; this PR does not trust it.
- The streamed import is slower per byte than the buffered one (see the times above) because each object is written to disk and then copied; that is the trade for bounded memory.
- Old packages are unaffected: the format is unchanged and an import still accepts the hard ceiling.
- No user-visible copy changed in this PR: the stage-1 limit line and over-cap confirmation are #1173, already merged. The two preflight refusals surface through the existing task error, with their message naming the missing capacity.
- The measurements above are of the package library round trip. The API restore reads one object at a time rather than materialising the package; its footprint is the largest single object plus records, which the post-parse preflight enforces.

A refusal caused by the measured free-disk budget answers HTTP 507 with `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` and the disk copy; an overrun of the absolute ceiling stays its own client-input error.

pr:1206.body:
Closes #1204

## What changes

**The composer shows the permission mode and lets it be changed there.** The mode existed only behind the composer's settings menu, so what the next turn would run under was invisible until that menu was opened; the composer footer now carries a compact selector after the + and settings buttons:

- closed, it is the shield plus the mode's own word — `请求批准` with a check mark, `完全访问` with an exclamation mark and in the warning colour the flyout row already uses;
- with no session open it names what a conversation created now would run under: the project's `defaultApprovalMode`, else the global one, else `请求批准`. A default of full access is therefore shown as 完全访问 rather than 请求批准, and there is no third "follow settings" state (#1204 owner decision; the neutral label from the previous head was replaced by reading the effective default, the reviews' other allowed fix);
- open, it is the same two-row scope flyout the settings menu shows, so the scope descriptions live in one place rather than being copied;
- below 640 px it keeps the shield and drops the word: the footer is 270 px at 390 px, and a labelled third control pushed the send button outside it (the desktop-configuration journey measures exactly that), so the narrow composer uses the icon-only form the flyout still explains;
- it is disabled while a run is active, for the same reason the settings row is;
- the settings row keeps its choice: this adds a visible door, it does not remove the existing one.

**A new conversation starts in the last mode the reader selected, and that survives a restart.** `apps/desktop/src/app/approval-mode-preference.ts` keeps the choice in desktop storage under a namespaced key (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), next to the panel-width and locale preferences. It is read on creation, and a stored value that is not one of the two modes is treated as no choice at all. Consequences:

- conversations that already exist are never updated by it — nothing here writes to them, and reopening one only displays its own mode;
- the choice travels only in creation-time values: `CreateSessionRequest.approvalMode` for the normal path, and one best-effort `updateSession(approvalMode)` for the two paths whose conversation the service creates on its own — a new project's first conversation and an untouched draft reused by 新增会话. A failed inheritance write there never hides the conversation;
- with nothing stored, the request carries no `approvalMode` and the service default applies exactly as before.

No API change was needed: `CreateSessionRequest` already accepts `approvalMode` and the server route honours it. Permission enforcement is untouched.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/approval-mode-preference.test.ts`: 3 cases — a fresh call after `rememberApprovalMode` carries the mode (this is what a restart looks like, because the module keeps no state of its own); a stored value that is not a mode is ignored; `inheritForSession` applies the remembered mode to a conversation created by another path and makes no request when nothing is remembered.
- `apps/desktop/tests/composer.test.tsx`: 30 cases, three covering this change — the selector's position after the + and settings buttons with the asking label and check, the full-access warning colour and label, and the popover's two scope explanations with the callback receiving `ask_for_dangerous` when that row is chosen.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and the root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean. `pnpm ci:l1` and the rest of the gate are CI's evidence.

## Verification of the restart requirement

This was the one acceptance criterion the first head missed, so it is stated explicitly: the choice is written to `localStorage` on every selection (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), and the capture run below read it back after selecting full access (`stored: "always_allow"`). A fresh module instance reads it through `readStoredText`, which is what a new application process does; the unit test uses a storage stub to exercise exactly that read.

pr:1207.body:
Closes #1205

A conversation created after the user has picked a model now starts from that model, **including after a restart**. Only an explicit pick writes the memory; opening an existing conversation reads its own model and never becomes the default for the next one.

## What changed

- **`state/storage.ts`**: `sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model`, next to the locale and panel-width preferences. Read at boot, written on every explicit pick, cleared when the catalog loses the model or empties.
- **`session-model-memory.ts`**: `modelForNewConversation` (the catalog check) plus `readRememberedModel` / `writeRememberedModel` over a `ReadableStorage`, so a missing or throwing storage degrades to instance-only memory instead of failing.
- **`use-workspace.ts`**:
  - the ref starts from storage, so a fresh process begins with the remembered model;
  - `selectModel` writes the pick *before* the session update, so a conversation created while that write is in flight already starts from it;
  - `createOpenSession` sends `settingsOverrides: { modelId }` instead of the top-level `modelId` shortcut: the shortcut also pins the session's `reviewModelId` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3138-3144`), while `createProjectAndOpen`'s `PATCH { modelId }` changes only the task model — both paths now change the task model only and agree;
  - a fresh draft shows the remembered model (then the project default, the global default, the first catalog model); `openSession` never writes the memory.

## Behaviour against the acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it holds |
| --- | --- |
| A new conversation defaults to the last explicitly selected model, including after a restart | the pick is stored on selection and read at boot; the captures below reload the window and the next draft already shows it |
| A later selection is used by subsequently created conversations | every explicit pick overwrites the stored value |
| Conversations with messages keep their own model; reopening does not change the memory | `openSession` only clears the one-shot draft override and displays that conversation's `modelId` |
| An unavailable remembered model does not leave a dangling selection | `modelForNewConversation` rejects an id the catalog lost, the refresh clears the stored value, and the project/global default applies |
| Relevant automated tests | see below |

## Review round 1 (head `e62925a1`)

- **Restart persistence** (zhaozhaozz and HongyeZhou, required): implemented in storage, as above — not handed to #1204 any more.
- **Review-model split** (zhaozhaozz, required): the creation path now sends `settingsOverrides.modelId`; the project path's `PATCH { modelId }` was already task-model-only. Both paths now leave `reviewModelId` alone.
- **Wiring only tested at helper level** (zhaozhaozz, required): `workspace-model-setup.test.ts` now mounts the hook against a fake client that records bodies, and asserts the create body is `{ settingsOverrides: { modelId: "second" } }` and the project path PATCHes `{ modelId: "second" }`.
- **Indentation at `use-workspace.ts:817`** (HongyeZhou, optional): fixed.

## Screenshots

Desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane), 1440×900, zh-CN and en. **Before**: a fresh window with the project default (Alpha). **After**: pick Beta in the composer's model menu, then **reload the window** — the next draft already shows Beta, read back from `sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model = model-beta`.

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before — project default | ![before, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-en-before.png) | ![before, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-zh-CN-before.png) |
| after — remembered model, after a reload | ![after, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-en-after.png) | ![after, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-zh-CN-after.png) |

The capture script read the values back from the DOM: `before="Alpha model"`, after the reload `"Beta model"`, and `localStorage["sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model"]="model-beta"` in both locales — so the Chinese captures show the dictionary's own strings, not a re-encode.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/session-model-memory.test.ts` **5/5**: the three decision cases, plus a stored pick surviving a fresh read and a missing/broken storage degrading safely.
- `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-model-setup.test.ts` **5/5**: the three existing cases, plus the create body and the project-path PATCH.
- Mutation: sending the top-level `modelId` on creation again makes the create-body case fail with the review-model reason.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean. The tagged suites were run with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored; the tags in this commit are unchanged.

## Scope

- The web client is unchanged; whether #1205 covers it is an open question for the user, not decided here.
- The memory is per browser profile, the same way the desktop keeps the locale, panel width and (#1204) the approval mode.

pr:1208.body:
Follow-up to #1194 (#1182 and #1187 both closed by it): the three suggestions that were deliberately not pushed onto the approved head.

## What changes

**F1 — the read-only fixture is judged by its own write (`application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`).**
`hostMadeReadOnly` had its `writeFile` and its conditional `rm` inside one `try`, so a failed unlink of a file the host had just created was classified as "read-only". Only the write decides now; the unlink is best effort. It failed loudly rather than passing silently, but the classification was wrong.

**F3 — the writable half runs before the skip (same file).**
`assert.equal(await dirWritable(join(root, "rw")), true)` had moved below the NTFS probe, so on the one platform this suite runs on, a regression that made `dirWritable` answer `false` for a writable directory would have been reported as `# skipped`. It is asserted before the probe again, and only the read-only assertion sits below the skip.

**F2 — the build-only flag is pinned in the contract (`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`).**
`/pnpm --dir application dist/` matches with or without `--publish never`, so the publish half of the Windows gate had no contract check while the split half did. The contract now asserts the flag, so a later edit cannot restore electron-builder's implicit publish (the #1187 failure) while the test stays green.

## Validation

On this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files pushed:

- `application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`: **34 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped** — the same two NTFS skips, with the writable assertion now before the probe.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` passes, including the new `--publish never` assertion (run with that file's `os:linux` tag released for this host; the other failures in the file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are untouched here).
- Root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` is clean for these files through CI's gate.

This is test-only; no product or workflow behaviour changes.

pr:1212.body:
The 会话设置 row for 程序演进实验 reused a search whenever the Session already had one. After the
first run it could never reach the create dialog again, so the preflight advice "start again from
the setup dialog" pointed at a surface the UI would not show, and a second search could only be
started by typing an `/evolve-design` command.

The same Session also showed a second, independent problem when the continuation was written as a
plain message ("基于Node #2，继续进化"): the model omitted `allowUnisolated`, because that message
carries no `--allow-direct`. The server does not read the current message: it reads the Session's
**latest** `/evolve-design` command, which did carry the flag, so the run was refused by the
model's reading of the rule, not by the server.

## The settings row always starts a design
`openEvolve` in `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` now always opens 新建程序演进实验 instead of selecting a
running/newest search. Existing searches stay reachable through their cards in the transcript, and
the composer's draft still rides into the new design's task field. The Composer prop comment follows
the behaviour.

A search that is **still running** holds the form rather than disappearing from it: the server
starts one search per Session (`startProposedRun` refuses a second with "this session already has a
search running"), so the dialog now takes the same `isEvolveRunActive` over `evolve.runs` the panel
uses, and `blocked` names it — the form opens, says a search is running and where its card is, and
leaves 开始设计 disabled. A finished search leaves the form usable, which is the state this change
is about. The new cases in `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` cover both: a finished search still
gets a usable dialog from the settings row, and a running one still opens the dialog but cannot
start a second search.

## Consent for a continuation started from a plain message
`skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md` and the `allowUnisolated` description in `packages/evolve/src/index.ts`
now scope the consent to the design being continued: what it inherits is the `/evolve-design`
command that started that design, read together with the design it started. That is the Session's
latest command only when the continued design is the newest one — with two designs, the latest
command can belong to the other one — so when that cannot be told the flag is left out and the
server refuses with `unisolated_run_unconfirmed`, telling the user to start the run from the setup
dialog. A checkpoint answer does not replace the command, a plain message is not itself an answer,
and a design that begins from one has no command of its own, so it must not inherit another
design's `--allow-direct`.

## Validation

- Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`, mocked entry): 154 tests, 150 passed, 4 failed.

  command, in files this diff does not touch: `boot` "resumes the most recent session", both
  `research-package` cases, and `settings-interactions` "a card opens to the skill's source".
- The repository-wide UT and ST layers were last run on the previous head before the rebase; the
  only packages this head changes are the two above, and both were rerun. That earlier run:
  UT 7707 planned / 7676 executed / 7660 passed / 16 failed, all 16 attributed to this host (14

  this host cannot reach.

## Screenshots

clicking 会话设置 → 程序演进实验.

## Release
