pr:1213.body:
The desktop front end had no Reviewer Specialist surface. The service writes a
review for every artifact it audits — a `reviewer_checkpoint` message in the
transcript plus an `ArtifactReviewRun` — and the desktop read neither, so a
Session could be reviewed at the Quick or Deep level with nothing on screen to
say what the review concluded.

## The verdict card

A checkpoint message now draws a card in the conversation, joined to its
reviews by `toolCallId`, so the verdict sits under the turn that produced the
artifact rather than at the end of the Session. One checkpoint can cover
several artifacts and each gets its own section; the header reports the worst
of them.

The colour states what is trustable, not how the run ended:

- **red** — a problem with the artifact: any finding, or delivery checked and
  incomplete;
- **amber** — the verdict cannot be trusted: the review failed, the artifact has
  a newer version, or delivery was never verified;
- **grey** — there was nothing to judge: the checkpoint was skipped, or it
  produced no review;
- **green** — the level ran, raised nothing, and delivery was confirmed — or the
  review was structure-only and never claimed any delivery verdict.

`unverifiedDelivery` is a port of the server's own `reviewUnverifiedDelivery`.
The desktop cannot import the schema's runtime (its barrel reaches a JSON
property import), so the rule is one copy with the server's tests behind it
rather than a second, drifting reading.

Expanding a card shows findings first, then the delivery verdict, then the
checks that ran (the header's "N 项检查" has to have something behind it). A
source service that returned no conclusion is rendered as "来源核验没有得出结论"
and the service's raw error text is not printed: it is not a finding about the
report. A Quick review that only checked citation format says so in a note, so
a green header cannot be read as "the claims were checked". A checkpoint that
produced nothing says why — the server's `skipReason` is mapped to a sentence
that names where to turn it back on — instead of printing the enum.

## The artifact dialog's 审查 tab

The version on screen gets its own tab with the same rows; when the version is
no longer current the verdict is marked as history and a re-run is offered. The
re-run names the checkpoint message the server accepts, which the audit queue
supplies — the dialog never invents a message id.

## The two settings layers

设置 › 专家 carries the system master switch, and the composer's settings menu
carries the Session's automatic review and level. The master switch is read on
Session load and on every reviewer refresh: when it is off the Session switch is
disabled and the menu says why, rather than offering a control that cannot act.

## The desktop E2E layer now gates a PR

The desktop browser suite answers every `/api/**` call from
`apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts`, so it needs neither the Python stack nor
credentials and can run on a pull request. `ci.yml` gains an `e2e-desktop` job
that reuses the lockfile-pinned Playwright install, `merge-gate` waits for it,
and the tier policy requires it on every profile. Documentation-only changes
skip it like every other layer, and the README now says so — the old text said
no workflow ran this suite, which is no longer true.

Wiring the gate flushed out four stale specs (a branch dialog that no longer
quotes the reply, a skill card whose source moved to a badge, two fixture
routes the app now calls); they assert what the app actually does.

The reviewer cases that can be driven through a page mock are ported from the
web journeys `journey-reviewer-result-matrix` and `journey-reviewer-localization`
and the UI half of `journey-reviewer-auto-audit` / `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle`.
Those web specs stay where they are: their other half asserts the service —
the coordinator scheduling an audit, feedback being consumed, records staying
identical across a skip — which runs against the real stack and has no
observable in a page mock.

## Validation

Numbers from this commit (`2f41f8fd`), after rebasing onto `main`:

| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop` unit (`npm test`) | 1193 passed / 0 failed |
| `apps/desktop` typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) | clean |
| Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`) | 171 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped |
| CI self-tests (`node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`) | 149 passed / 0 failed |
| Repo-wide UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | planned 7735, executed 7704, passed 7701, failed 3, skipped 0 |
| Repo-wide ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | planned 63, executed 63, passed 62, failed 1, skipped 0 |
| Repo-wide mocked E2E (`pnpm ci:e2e`) | 188 executed, 184 passed, 4 failed; 8/8 JiuwenSwarm checks except `skills` |

The four repo-wide UT/ST failures do not run on this host as configured, and
each was attributed before touching anything:

- `packages/specialist/src/bundled-references.test.ts` fails only in this
  checkout because it recurses into `.worktrees/`; the same test passes in a
  clean worktree at the same commit.
- `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`'s mutation case reproduces identically on
  a clean `upstream/main` worktree — pre-existing on this host.
- `packages/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` needs `bwrap --disable-userns`;
  this host has bubblewrap 0.6.1, which lacks the flag.
- `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` (ST) fails fetching the pinned
  python-build-standalone release from GitHub; the host cannot reach it.

The mocked-E2E failures were this run's own harness, not the change:

- `journey-compact-process` ×2 — the run had `TMPDIR` pointed at `/var/tmp`,
  which JiuwenSwarm refuses as a local skill-import source (`/var` is on its
  built-in blacklist). No session skill was installed, so `create_skill` never
  fired and the API fell back to its own skill catalog in the prompt — the same
  cause as the failing `skills` check. With `TMPDIR` at its default and the
  batch's data directory reset, both tests pass (2 passed) and all eight
  JiuwenSwarm checks report ok, including `skills`.
- `issue-143-proxy-settings` ×3 — the batch's data directory carried state from
  an earlier run; CI always starts it empty. On a reset directory all three
  pass (3 passed).

No case in the layer fails once the harness is prepared the way CI prepares it;
the numbers above are reported as they were measured, not as a best case.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Two surfaces, both exercised on this commit.

The desktop browser entry (mocked per-page API; no backend), 171 cases: a
confirmed delivery is green; a review that never verified delivery is amber;
structure-only is green because it never claimed delivery; an incomplete
delivery is red; a stale verdict says it is history and offers a re-run; the
eight-checkpoint Quick/Deep outcome matrix including the two skip reasons and a
reload; the system master switch off disabling the Session switch with its
explanation; both settings layers surviving a reload; the artifact dialog's 审查
tab queueing a re-run with the right message id.

The shared `test/journey-reviewer-*.spec.ts` journeys, against the real control
plane (the mocked E2E layer's own stack), all pass in the same layer:
`journey-reviewer-auto-audit`, `journey-reviewer-localization`,
`journey-reviewer-result-matrix`, `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle`.

Closes #1203 — the desktop Reviewer Specialist feature request this implements.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this account has no write access to apply it)
User impact: the desktop app shows Reviewer Specialist verdicts, can re-run a
review from an artifact, and configures both Reviewer settings layers. The
desktop E2E suite becomes a required PR check.
Compatibility and migration: none. No API or configuration change.

pr:1215.body:
Closes #1199.

## What changes

The desktop 设置 › 技能 page gains the two surfaces the web app has and the
desktop did not: importing a Skill, and editing one in place. Both are pages
inside the settings pane rather than dialogs, so the list stays one step away.

- **添加技能** is a menu in the list header with three entries: **上传技能**
  (a `SKILL.md`, a ZIP package, or a `.skill` archive, dropped or picked),
  **从 GitHub 导入** (inspect the repository, then pick the packages to
  install), and **从零开始写** (the existing authored form).
- A repository is inspected first (`POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect`) and
  each chosen package is imported at the commit that inspection saw, so what
  the user reviewed is what gets installed. Replacing an installed Skill
  requires `overwrite` plus the revision the user saw (`expectedRevision`); a
  different revision is a 409 rather than a silent replacement of an edit made
  in another window. Re-importing identical bytes is a no-op instead of an
  empty revision, and a built-in Skill stays read-only.
- An inspection of a real, large repository says it is cloning and offers
  **取消**, which stops waiting without reporting a failure. The clone timeout
  is 180 s and a timeout is reported as one. The checkout an inspection made is
  kept for 15 minutes, so the packages that follow are imported from it
  instead of cloning the repository once per package. Measured against
  `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` (100 packages, ~471 MB): a
  package import used to take ~41 s on its own clone, and now takes ~0.1 s
  once the repository has been inspected. A request for another commit, ref or
  repository still clones.
- **编辑** opens from a managed Skill's card and edits its `SKILL.md` fields
  (description, license, compatibility, instructions) and its resource files.
  Saving rebuilds `SKILL.md` from the form and sends back the optional
  frontmatter keys the form does not show (`metadata`, `allowed-tools`), so
  they are not dropped. The package-file route can write but not delete, so the
  editor adds and overwrites only. A binary resource says it cannot be edited
  here instead of showing a broken pane. A stale revision from another window
  surfaces as a conflict message, not a failed save.

Every page below the list replaces it and is left through the header's back
control; the authored form no longer draws its own 取消, because a second exit
that discards a draft is a choice nobody asked for. The header names the page
that is actually open, and the list keeps the installed count. The pages share
one content measure so moving between them does not move the fields under the
pointer, and they reuse the pane's existing tokens and controls rather than
introducing a second visual language.

A newly installed Skill is enabled when the switches are available; updating an
already-installed Skill leaves its switch alone, because a user may have
switched it off on purpose. Closing 设置 after visiting 技能 re-reads the
catalog, so the composer's `/` palette reflects the change without a reload.

Backend support: `ImportSkillFromGitRequest` gains optional `commit`,
`overwrite` and `expectedRevision`; `SkillCatalog` accepts an injectable
checkout so the Git import branches can be tested without a network; and
`SKILL_VALIDATION` now maps to HTTP 400 instead of falling through to an
unclassified 500 when its message wording does not match the client-input
patterns.

## What was run

- `pnpm typecheck` — pass (all workspace packages)
- `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1185 pass, 0 fail
- `services/api` Skill suites (`skills.test.ts`, `skills-git-import.test.ts`) —
  25 pass, 0 fail (includes the new checkout-reuse test)
- `services/api` targeted suites (`server.test.ts`, `skills.test.ts`,
  `skills-git-import.test.ts`, `http/error-classification.test.ts`) — 144 run,
  141 pass. The 3 failures are pre-existing and environmental: `services/paper/.venv`
  is absent in this checkout (PDF upload test), and two subagent event-order
  assertions expecting a `model.usage` event that this host does not emit; both
  fail without this change.
- `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` — 96 spec files, 0 errors
- `pnpm docs:lint` — 0 issues

## E2E

`test/journey-desktop-skill-import-edit.spec.ts` (mocked, zh-CN, desktop Vite
entry on 4178 against the API stack): 5/5 steps pass on the PR head.

1. Open 设置 › 技能 on the desktop; the Skill about to be imported is not listed.
2. 添加技能 › 上传技能 hands the page one file; it reports the installed package
   by name, and the list is back through the header's back control.
3. Find the card, open 编辑 on it; the editor page is named after the Skill.
4. Rewrite 指令 and 保存; the editor reports the save.
5. Read the package back through the API: the new instructions are installed and
   the `license` key the form does not display survived the save.

The isolated stack ran locally with `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_STUB_ONLY=1`; this
journey never touches Evolve, so the stub-only environment does not weaken it.
The journey report (per-step screenshots and logs) was produced under the
gitignored `.e2e-results/` directory.

pr:1216.body:
Closes #1211

#1211 lists six findings from the #1200 review that the 5 GiB default exposed. This PR fixes all six, on the server, in the package library, and in both clients that save the archive.

## What changed, per finding

**F1 — the restore no longer holds a whole session's workspace objects.** `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` now collects the workspace `objectPath` list first (`workspaceEntries`) and looks each object up inside the write loop, so the peak is one object instead of the sum of the session's workspace. An object missing from the unpacked directory is recorded as an omission and the restore continues, which is what the memory requirement in `http/index.ts` already assumed.

**F2 — the 5 GiB default only reaches paths that stream.**
- Server: the synchronous `GET …/research-package` route now pre-flights the export on `archiveBytes` *before* writing headers (a refusal after `writeHead` can only truncate the body), builds the input with `streamObjects`, drops `content-length`, and writes tar → gzip straight into the response via `writeResearchPackage`; a failed write destroys the response instead of claiming success.
- Web: `exportResearchPackage` returns the live `Response` instead of `response.blob()`. New `apps/web/src/research-package/save-stream.ts` opens `showSaveFilePicker` *inside the click* — the picker needs the transient user activation that a `fetch` round trip would consume — then pipes `response.body` into the writable; a failed export aborts it so no partial file survives, and a cancelled dialog returns without closing the dialog or exporting anything.
- Desktop + shell: new `export-stream-begin/chunk/end/abort` IPC channels (`application/src/export-sink.ts`, `main.ts`, `preload.ts`) keep one file descriptor per destination token and append each chunk. The stream writes a sibling `<destination>.<token>.part` and `streamEnd` renames it onto the destination only after the close succeeds, so a save that fails at 80% - or a renderer that disappears - leaves the archive the user already had untouched; `abort`/`abortAll` remove the temporary only, a zero-byte stream is dropped instead of published, and a reused live token aborts the previous stream rather than committing it. The durable history row is written at `streamEnd` with the size the stream actually wrote, so it keeps the behaviour the whole-buffer `write` had. `apps/desktop` forwards `response.body` chunk by chunk and only falls back to the one-shot `write` on a shell that lacks the channels; a plain browser still falls back to the anchor download.
- Two client paths still buffer, and both are named here rather than implied away: a browser without the File System Access API keeps the old whole-blob download, and the background-export download (`downloadResearchPackageExport` → `downloadBlob`) runs in a completion poll, outside any user activation, so it cannot open the file picker and still takes `response.blob()`. Moving that one to a destination picked when the user starts the export is the follow-up, not part of #1211's six findings.

**F3 — a write error during a streamed import rejects instead of killing the process.** The object write races against `new Promise((_, reject) => file.on("error", reject))` and the catch destroys the file, so an `EEXIST` open or a late flush error rejects the import instead of becoming an unhandled `'error'` event.

**F5 — each check now charges only what it will still write.** `researchPackageRestoreRequirement` charges `unpacked * 3 + records` (snapshot objects, version blobs and workspace files — the three copies a restore writes), `researchPackageUnpackBudget` is `free / 4` so that a package the unpack step admits cannot be refused by the post-parse check on the same volume, and the export requirement charges the archive it writes (`bytes`) rather than the copies a restore adds. `researchPackageBudgetRefusal` quotes the same 3× figure it refuses on. The new case runs the two halves together — 16 GiB free, 3.8 GiB package — which is the pairing that was missing: each half passed alone and the pair still refused.

**F6 — trailing bytes after the tar terminator no longer hang the import.** `ChunkQueue.drain()` was added: after the zero block the decompressor is drained to completion, and non-zero trailing bytes are refused with `Research package carries data after its end` instead of parking the sink in `offer` forever.

**F7 — a missing CAS blob becomes an omission instead of a failed export.** `addObjectSource` is async and checks `provenanceRecorder.cas.has(hash)` before enqueueing the lazy source; a missing blob pushes `cas:<hash>:unavailable source object` into `omissions` and is left out of the inventory, matching the resident read path.

## Verification

Local, Windows 11 + Node 22.23.4. Tests that carry `os:linux` were run with the tag removed and then restored, and `node:test` skips are not counted as passes.

- `packages/research-package` `stream-import.test.ts`: **9/9** — including 20 MiB of trailing zeros completing, non-zero trailing bytes refused, and a `EEXIST` write error rejecting the import.
- `services/api` `research-package-preflight.test.ts`: **18/18** — including "an export is charged the archive it writes, not the copies a restore adds", "a restore is charged only the copies it still has to write" and "the unpack budget and the post-parse check agree on the same free disk".
- `services/api` `research-package-http.test.ts`: **23/23**.
- `services/api` `research-package-exports.test.ts`: **9/9**.
- Web: new `save-stream.test.ts` **4/4** (a two-chunk body arrives as two writes, which fails if the caller buffers first; picker cancel starts no request; a failed export aborts; no picker still downloads) and `ResearchPackageActions.test.tsx` **5/5**.
- Desktop: `export-bridge-stream.test.ts` **3/3**, `research-package.test.ts` **6/6**, and the view suite `research-package-export-ack` 1/1, `research-package-export-session` **2/2** (the new case asserts `begin → chunk → chunk → end` and that the one-shot `write` is *not* used), `research-package-trim` 5/5.
- Shell: `application/test/export-sink.test.ts` **4/4**, plus the existing `export-tokens` and `export-history` suites **12/12**.
- `tsc --noEmit`: `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and the root `tsconfig.tests.json` are clean.
- Mutation checks: restoring the whole-buffer `arrayBuffer()` write in the web sink turns the new web case red; short-circuiting the desktop streaming branch onto the one-shot `write` turns the new view case red; both were reverted.

## What was not run locally

- `application` (the Electron shell) has no `node_modules` on this machine, so `tsc -p application/tsconfig.json` cannot run here; the shell is covered by its unit tests above and by CI, and I have not run it in a real Electron window.
- No end-to-end save of a multi-GiB package through a real browser or shell was performed here. The 5 GiB server-side numbers are the ones measured for #1200 (`merge-group` run `44079501355`), and the client halves are covered by chunk-level assertions, not by a real 5 GiB transfer.

## Screenshots

Desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane, `window.sdShell` stubbed), 1440×900, zh-CN and en. Each capture is backed by a DOM assertion, not just a picture.

| state | zh-CN | en |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dialog open, nothing started | ![zh idle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-idle.png) | ![en idle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-idle.png) |
| saved: 证据包已保存 / Package saved | ![zh saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-saved.png) | ![en saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-saved.png) |
| saving: 1 个导出进行中 / 1 export in progress (sidebar row) | ![zh saving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-saving.png) | ![en saving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-saving.png) |
| cancelled: the dialog stays open, nothing started | ![zh cancelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-cancelled.png) | ![en cancelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-cancelled.png) |
| failed: 保存证据包失败 / Failed to save the package | ![zh failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-zh-CN-failed.png) | ![en failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1216/docs/screenshots/1216/1216-desktop-en-failed.png) |

What each state pins: `idle` shows the dialog with its size estimate; `saved` shows the success line after a streamed save (`1` chunk crossed the bridge); `saving` shows the sidebar row while the body is still arriving; `cancelled` shows the dialog still open with nothing started and no chunks written — cancelling the native save dialog is silent by design, which is stated here rather than implied away; `failed` shows the failure line when the shell's write rejects.

**web**: not captured. Driving the web app's session menu to the export dialog did not reach the dialog in this harness — `onSelect` runs, but `App.tsx:5217` only opens it when `activeProjectId` is set, and that state stayed empty under the mocked control plane. Rather than fake a screen, this PR records the gap: the web save path itself is covered by `apps/web/tests/save-stream.test.ts` (4/4: two-chunk body, picker cancel, failed export abort, no-picker fallback).


## Web client, same dialog

The web save path is the other surface this PR changes (`apps/web/src/research-package/save-stream.ts`, `ResearchPackageActions.tsx`): the picker opens before the request, an aborted picker writes nothing, and a failed write reports itself in the dialog instead of closing as if it had saved. Captured in the web client (Vite dev at `apps/web`, mock control plane, 1440×900), zh-CN and en, with the dialog text asserted at capture time:

| state | assertion at capture time |

pr:1217.body:
Three macOS release-chain follow-ups from the acceptance review (issue #1165). Based on latest main (`b2075e49`); none of the 24 commits since PR #1156 touched these two files (verified by blob sha). Head is now `0ce130c3` (three stacked follow-ups on the original three changes, see commit list).

## 1. 5f gate: blockmap assertion missed electron-builder 26.x naming

The M4 clean-room signed build (`0.4.0`, builder `26.15.3`) produced a **healthy** differential-update asset, but the 5f manifest gate failed to find it:

| builder | blockmap name |
|---|---|
| 25.x | `ScienceDiscovery-…-mac-arm64.blockmap` (replaces `.zip`) |
| 26.x | `ScienceDiscovery-…-mac-arm64.zip.blockmap` (appends to full name) |

The gate asserted the 25.x name only. Fix: gate like the DMG/zip discovery — **exactly one** of the two names may exist (0 or 2 candidates fail the gate), so a stale same-version blockmap left under the other naming cannot silently ship differential data that does not match the zip (review F1):

```bash
BLOCKMAP=""
FOUND=0
for candidate in "${ZIP}.blockmap" "${ZIP%.zip}.blockmap"; do
  if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
    BLOCKMAP="$candidate"
    FOUND=$((FOUND + 1))
  fi
done
if [ "$FOUND" -eq 2 ]; then
  die "… BOTH … a stale same-version blockmap … clean release/ and rerun"
elif [ "$FOUND" -eq 0 ]; then
  die "… the differential-update data was not written; rerun electron-builder (zip target)"
fi
```

(FOUND=0 and FOUND=2 carry separate messages — review F2: the shared line told the operator to clean `release/` even when nothing stale existed.)

## 2. 5f gate: uninstaller is not a gated release asset (F4)

`application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` is the supported macOS removal path (review F4: a macOS user who wants out — or hits a broken install — has no other removal path), but the 5f manifest never gated or listed it. Now:

- gated as the **fifth** asset: `missing scripts/uninstall-mac.command` fails the gate;
- listed in the printed manifest;
- appended to the printed `gh release create` command.

(Path correction vs. the PR #1156 merge description: the script lives at `application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command`, not repo-root `scripts/`.)

## 3. `minimumSystemVersion: 14.0.0` (acceptance ⑦)

Decision basis:
- Electron 37 upstream supports the last 3 macOS majors; macOS 13 (Ventura) has fallen outside that window — no test coverage, no Gatekeeper data;
- our only real acceptance machine runs 14.8.9;
- pinning it here writes `LSMinimumSystemVersion` into Info.plist so Gatekeeper enforces the floor at install/first-run instead of documentation.

## Verification

- `bash -n application/scripts/build-mac.sh` — clean
- `js-yaml` parse of `electron-builder.yml` — `mac.minimumSystemVersion = 14.0.0`, all mac keys intact
- exactly-one probe tested on all three paths: 1 candidate hits (real 26.x artifacts, `…zip.blockmap`, 674,136 bytes), 2 candidates rejected, 0 rejected — with the split messages landing on the right branch
- remote blob shas match local `git hash-object` byte-for-byte at every push (`46cfca97`/`d5603224` → `2516b9e0` → `651eca21`)

Part of issue #1165 (items ⑦ + bot F4 + the 26.x blockmap fix found while producing the M4 release build; review F1/F2 follow-ups folded in).

pr:1219.body:
Closes #1218

## Why

`assemble` discovered that the JiuwenSwarm venv no longer matched the swarm patch set only inside "verifying payload imports", i.e. after the backend tree, the venv template, micromamba and the bytecode precompile had all been written — 759 s on the run the issue cites. The refusal was right, the timing was not: the same run succeeds in 835 s after `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup`, so every dependency-carrying patch cost a full payload assembly to learn about.

## What changes

**A lockfile-driven preflight at the start of `assemble`, before any payload write.** `application/scripts/lib/venv-lock-consistency.mjs` reads the *patched* `data/jiuwenswarm/src/uv.lock`, asks the jw venv once for every installed distribution (`importlib.metadata` in a single python call) and reports each package whose installed version differs from the pin. `assemble-backend.mjs` runs it right after the stale-dist gate and **before `rm(out)`/`mkdir(out)`**, so a stale venv costs seconds and leaves `build/resources` untouched.

**It is generic, not greenlet-specific.** 0018-desktop-slim-deps, 0019-align-workspace-versions and 0021-greenlet-static-runtime all rewrite `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`; whatever a future patch pins is checked without touching this code. Packages the lock lists for other platforms or optional groups are ignored when the venv does not install them — the direction this exists for is an installed package lagging its patched pin.

**The end-of-run gate stays.** The greenlet MSVC140/native-import gate is untouched and still runs as the second line of defence (a venv can, in principle, change mid-run).

The refusal names both versions and the same repair command the end gate uses:

```
[assemble] FAIL: jw venv preflight FAILED: the venv does not match the swarm patch set:
pip 25.0.1 (uv.lock requires 0.0.1). A dependency-carrying patch rewrote the lockfile but
the venv predates it. Re-run node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup (or bash scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup), then rebuild.
```

## Proof that the refusal happens before the payload is written

A real `assemble` run against a fixture whose lock pins `pip` differently from its venv (the same shape as greenlet 3.5.0 vs 3.5.5):

```
[assemble] sanity checks passed
[assemble] stale-dist gate passed (services/packages/apps)
[assemble] FAIL: jw venv preflight FAILED: ... pip 25.0.1 (uv.lock requires 0.0.1) ...
exit=1  elapsed=516 ms  out exists: False
```

- **516 ms**, against the 759 s the issue measured for the same discovery at the end gate.
- **`--out` was never created**: the preflight runs before `rm(out)`/`mkdir(out)`, so there is no payload to leave half-written. The check is asserted by a test as well (`the preflight runs before assemble writes anything`) so a future edit cannot move it back below the copy steps.
- With a lock that matches its venv, the same fixture prints `jw venv matches the swarm patch set's uv.lock` and proceeds to the deploy step — the check does not fire on a correct tree.

## Tests

- `application/test/assemble-venv-preflight.test.ts` (new): parses `[[package]]` pins; reports a stale installed version and not the pin; ignores a locked package the venv does not install; no refusal when they agree; the message names both versions and both setup commands; the skew list is bounded; and the ordering pin above.
- `pnpm --dir application test`: **352 tests, 348 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped** (the skips are the Windows-inapplicable macOS cases).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm ci:l1` could not run on this host: the tagged runner spawns `pnpm` without a shell and this machine only has a `pnpm.cmd` shim (spawn ENOENT). CI runs the same gate; the local suite and typecheck above are the local evidence.

No behaviour change for a correct tree: the preflight only reads a lockfile and asks the venv for its versions.

pr:1221.body:
Desktop users currently need Web to manage execution resources and inspect model usage. This adds those capabilities to Desktop's existing settings layout, with Runner-owned environments and a compact deployment-wide token view.

Closes #1220.

## Changes

- Combine remote machines and scientific environments into Runtime environments. The overview contains registered Runners and global Conda/Pip sources; each Runner contains its connection, resources and environments. Source changes save automatically, and environment creation reports creation progress.
- Add execution quotas, JiuwenSwarm Web-provider configuration and network proxies. DeepSeek search and webpage fetching share one credential, fetching has a cost notice, and proxy bypass settings stay within global defaults. Upload-limit changes update Desktop preflight immediately.
- Add Model usage beside Models with Today / 7 days / 30 days / All time, total/input/output tokens, a flat per-profile table and manual refresh. Optional reporting coverage distinguishes missing fields from reported zeros; token-only requests skip exchange-rate lookup.
- Remove project-specific Runner selection from system settings. Unspecified selection follows the live registered catalog, including future registrations. Preserve explicit selections, explicit empty unified selections, legacy local-only writes and Runner admission checks. No session Runner picker is added.

Existing Web settings remain available. Analytics reporting fields are additive and exchange rates remain enabled by default. Saved dormant DeepSeek credentials require an explicit re-save to enable search rather than being silently activated.

## Validation

Checked on rebased head `2182547d` against upstream main `c4315cf5d`:

- Desktop component/settings regressions: **116 passed, 0 failed** across migrated settings, model usage, settings pages/screens and workspace configuration.
- Shared schema and API Runner/usage/configuration regressions: **38 passed, 0 failed**; focused store selection regressions: **2 passed, 0 failed**.
- Desktop and API type checks passed.
- Desktop/API dependency-graph builds passed, including the Desktop production build.
- `git diff --check` passed. The three feature commits rebase without conflicts and retain identical patches.

The targeted commands use `tsx --test` with Desktop's CSS preload where required. Full UT/ST/E2E gates, rendered browser checks and live JiuwenSwarm journeys were not run in this pass; this PR remains draft pending that product validation.

Release category: `release:feature`.

`apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx`, mounted under Settings › 智能 › Idea Tree. Reads and writes `GET/PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` with the field set the API actually accepts (`templateId`, `explorationIntensity`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensPerCall`, `maxDepth`, `maxNodes`, `scoreDirection`, the three prompt overrides, per-stage thinking effort). pr:1225.body:
The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds a credential-free static asset hub: a build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into one `catalog.json` plus download artifacts, a Vite site renders it, and two workflows publish the site and the session drop to a public-read OBS bucket. The site has no backend and reads exactly one `catalog.json` at runtime.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Four tabs — skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset; the bucket serves `site/index.html` for an unknown path. Every asset exposes its README (rendered from the repository markdown) and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en).

Session packages are the one kind whose bytes live outside the site bundle: the detail page fetches `<id>/README.md` from the sessions prefix, which is why the publication workflow derives the site base from the bucket's static-website domain rather than the object domain — one origin, no bucket CORS.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory.

Failures are deterministic and happen before anything is written: a team skill naming an unknown specialist, or two assets claiming the same output URL, fails the export; an unknown task/domain category is cleared with a warning rather than published.

## External skills

The MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) is not in this repository. `pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and its `index.json`; the exporter reads whichever snapshot the workflow points it at, adds each skill with its own zip and README, and records the commit, ref and fetch time in the catalog sources. Extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

## Session packages

A drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus a `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory (every entry's size and sha256), `records.json` hashed but never parsed, nothing executed — and resolves `related` ids against the catalog.

The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index. A run merges by id: entries it does not deliver survive, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working. Contradictory requests (unpublishing an id the same run delivers, or one that is not published) fail before any write. The index is written last (packages, then READMEs, then index) through a temp file and rename, so an interrupted upload leaves the previous index advertising only files that exist. A 404 on the index starts an empty one; a missing index is a normal first publish, not a build failure.

## Publication workflows

`hub-publish.yml` runs on a push to main affecting asset sources, weekly, and by dispatch. Automatic runs rebuild the catalog and sync `site/`, and never read or write `sessions/`. A dispatch that publishes sessions validates the staged drop, uploads the packages and READMEs, then the index, then rebuilds and re-syncs the site. `site/` is wiped before upload so a renamed asset cannot linger, `index.html` is uploaded with `Content-Type: text/html`, and packages with `application/octet-stream` plus attachment so a browser downloads instead of previewing. A concurrency group keeps a manual publish from interleaving with an automatic one.

`hub-skills-sync.yml` refreshes the frozen external snapshot weekly and then dispatches the publish, so a new snapshot reaches the site without a repository commit.

AK/SK live only in the credential step, are written to obsutil's own config, and never reach the site, the catalog or a log; nothing is anonymously listable.

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 42 passed, 0 failed (4 suites).
- `pnpm ci:ut` on `de624faa`: planned 7718, executed 7687, passed 7670, failed 17, skipped 0. The 31 planned-but-unexecuted entries are the tests tagged `swarm:required`: the JiuwenSwarm install did not finish over the public PyPI from this host during that run (it has since been provisioned from a mirror). All 17 failures are outside this diff, in files byte-identical to the base commit, and are this host's known constants:
  - 5 × `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` and 5 × `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts`: "control API and Web UI exited before becoming healthy (status 1)" and `ENOENT …/data/runner.pid`. A 1058-byte `package.json` at `/tmp` (left by another user) turns `/tmp` into an ESM package root for the launcher's temporary directories.
  - 1 × `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`: the pre-fix-body assertion ("the pre-fix body restored anyway"), a documented host constant on this machine.
  - 4 × `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`: trajectory events missing and "unable to open database file"; they depend on the JiuwenSwarm install, which this host could not complete over the public PyPI before it was provisioned from a mirror.
  - 1 × `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`: `bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns`; the host has bubblewrap 0.6.1.
  - 1 × `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`: `spawnSync bash ETIMEDOUT` under this host's load.
- `pnpm ci:st` on `de624faa`: planned 63, executed 63, passed 62, failed 1. The failure is `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts`, which fetches `python-build-standalone` from a GitHub release and gets `fetch failed` — this host has no route to it. The JiuwenSwarm contract command step in the same layer ran 100 pytest cases with 0 failures and 0 skips.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: 4 planned, 4 passed.
- `pnpm build`: exit 0 (all workspace packages, including `apps/hub`).
- Both workflows parse as YAML and every `run` block passes `bash -n`; the upload order was proved end to end with a stand-in `obsutil` that records each `cp`.

## E2E user journeys

Status: FAIL on this host — 7 of 188, all outside this diff. Tested commit `de624faa`. `pnpm ci:e2e`: planned 188, executed 188, passed 181, failed 7, skipped 0. Per batch: governed 5/5, literature 6/6, research 21/21, standard-config-fresh 3/4, standard-config-global 61/64, journeys 85/88.

The seven failures are this host, not this diff. The diff touches only `apps/hub`, `scripts/hub`, two workflow files, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `packages/specialist/src/skills.ts`, two team `SKILL.md` frontmatter blocks, `tsconfig.tests.json` and `.gitignore` — every failing spec and every product file it exercises is byte-identical to the base commit:

- 2 × `journey-desktop-configuration` (en, zh): the desktop dev server never started — `Error: Port 4178 is already in use`. The port is hard-coded in `test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts` and is held on this machine by another worktree's `vite preview`, so the page never rendered and `.side-session` was absent.
- 1 × `journey-prepare-environment` J3: `page.waitForResponse` timed out after 120 s waiting for the micromamba download; this host has no route to the download host.
- 1 × `journey-compact-process`: the E2E stack's data directory still holds a writable `project-skills` library from an earlier layer, so the "no writable library" precondition cannot be reproduced. The spec says so itself and asks for the data directory to be reset.
- 3 × `issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox`, `journey-drop-pdf`, `journey-permission-decisions`: 10 s UI waits (a running subagent card's detail line, a parsed-paper count polling to 1, a permission card) that expired on a shared host at load ~120. These three were not re-run on the base commit, so they are reported as unattributed rather than claimed as pre-existing; none of the code they exercise is in this diff.

The hub is a static site with no server, so `pnpm ci:e2e` has no journey for it. It was driven end to end in headless Chromium against a local mock of the deployed layout — the built site served under `/site/`, session packages and external skills under their own prefixes on the same origin:

- home: four tabs at 364 / 8 / 13 / 2 assets, catalog fetched from `/site/catalog.json`;
- deep link: `/site/skills?domain=biology` after a full reload renders the selected tree node and its cards, because the bucket serves `site/index.html` for an unknown path;
- session detail: stats and README headings, with the README fetched from the sibling `/sessions/<id>/README.md` (present in the resource timeline, so it did not come from the bundle); the download was saved and its sha256 matched the catalog entry;
- publication increment: 1 package, then 2, then 3 — each run keeps the entries it did not deliver, and every earlier package URL still returns 200;
- unpublish: removes only the named id (3 → 2) and its file still returns 200;
- an index URL answering 404 starts an empty index (0 sessions) instead of failing the build;
- the built bundle contains no AK, SK, endpoint or bucket name.

`pnpm build` (exit 0) and `pnpm hub:test` (42/42) were also run on `de624faa`.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a new static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and published session packages, each with its README and a download, in Chinese and English.

Compatibility and migration: none. A new app, new scripts and two new workflows; no existing behaviour, configuration or API changes. The site and the session prefix are new OBS prefixes.

pr:1226.body:
Desktop Settings can manage existing Specialists, but users need the legacy Web UI to create a custom one. This change adds **Add specialist** to the Desktop Specialists page, including when the list is empty.

The add action opens the shared form with a blank draft, Native runtime, and Full access. Name, description, and instructions are required, and the description and instructions limits match the existing API. A successful save refreshes the settings list. A failed save leaves the draft open for retry. Reopening the session picker refreshes the catalog and keeps the current selection.

Closes #1180.

- Desktop typecheck passed.

- Local `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st`, and `ci:e2e` were attempted in WSL. The runs ended before final summaries under the local time limits. UT, ST, and mocked E2E were still preparing the workspace build.

pr:168.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. pr:261.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

pr:269.body:
CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

pr:285.body:
## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Wire the saved global route into both Runner clients: the control plane's own local Runner, and every remote Runner that `RemoteComputeClient` deploys or installs into. Environment mode resolves on the remote Runner itself; a custom URL pointing at the control host's loopback is refused with the reason and the two ways out, because forwarding it would make the remote Runner call itself.
- Refuse proxy settings that cannot be applied instead of degrading silently: a `url` policy without an address, and a proxy URL carrying a path or query (rejected at save time as well, so a stored value cannot fail only per request). The generated `NO_PROXY` lists `::1` rather than `[::1]`, which no consumer matches against a bare hostname.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation, including the settings-projection contract change (environment summaries now mask credentials and query strings).

## Rebase onto `main` (`b31f74eb`)

- The branch was 699 commits behind and conflicted in three files. `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, `packages/executor` and the gateway tests were re-derived from `main`, then the PR's own deltas re-applied one hunk at a time.
- `normalizeUsage` is gone from this PR: `main` moved it to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` and already reads the protocol field per dialect with alias fallback, so the bug this branch started from is fixed upstream. Keeping the branch copy would have reverted that.
- The branch's `services/adapter/uv.lock` is dropped because `main` deleted the lockfile (`feat(sizeopt)`).
- The branch's last commit (`a49f92ed`, "preserve current runtime interfaces after rebase") is dropped: it reverted `model-connectivity.ts`, `client.ts` and the adapter `network.py` to the branch's older shape, i.e. it undid upstream work rather than preserving the PR. Its only real purpose was to make the stale branch compile, which the re-application above now covers.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter` builds: `schema`, `data-source`, `model`, `executor`, `runner`, `api` | Passed |
| `pnpm --recursive typecheck` plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | Passed |
| Proxy transport, resolver, connectivity (`packages/data-source`, `services/api`) | 14 passed |
| Model client and dispatcher regressions (`packages/model`) | 46 passed |
| Runner client proxy propagation (`packages/executor`) | 7 passed |

## Summary

Make provider token accounting a diagnostic instead of a real-E2E pass criterion, and keep the usage shapes it depends on pinned by deterministic tests. Functional task/delivery/quality assertions are unchanged.

## Rebased onto `main` (2026-11-07, `b9e5367`)

The branch had been open since 2026-10-14 and was 699 commits behind; it conflicted in three files. After the rebase:

- **The protocol-aware parser is no longer part of this diff.** `normalizeUsage` moved to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` on `main` and already takes the request's dialect, reading `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` for Chat Completions and `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` for Responses ahead of the aliases, with a conflict diagnostic. The reported bug - a probe returning `completion_tokens: 31` next to an extra `output_tokens: 0`, which the shared normalizer used to prefer - is already fixed there, so `packages/model/src/client.ts` is untouched by this PR.
- **One design choice from the original branch was not carried over.** The original parser dropped the fallback to the other dialect's fields and to `total_tokens` arithmetic entirely. `main`'s version keeps a dialect-first-then-fallback design and documents it; overriding that here would be a behaviour change on shared accounting that the maintainers already settled. The assertions that encoded the stricter rule were dropped with it rather than left failing.
- What is left is this PR's other half plus its regression coverage: the documented CI policy, the journey that stops gating on usage, and the mixed/missing-accounting cases exercised end to end.

## Changes

- `.ci/README.md` - provider usage is diagnostic evidence, not an E2E success or scoring gate; missing accounting is not evidence of zero cost; protocol parsing correctness stays enforced by deterministic tests.
- `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts` - the usage step attaches the ledger instead of asserting `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` are positive, and reads the route directly so a route that cannot answer still fails the case.
- `packages/model/src/client.test.ts` - a chat completion whose usage carries conflicting aliases reports the dialect's counts (35/31/66), and a stream without usage still completes with `usage: undefined`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts` - the gateway forwards the protocol's usage unchanged and serves the turn with none, in both streamed and non-streamed responses.

pr:311.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes #310.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-29)

- Closing keyword corrected to plain `Closes #310`; the earlier markdown-link form left GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` empty, so the merge would not have auto-closed the issue.
- Blocking item "CI green on this tip" is already satisfied **on this tip**: run [40645827814](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40645827814) (attempt 2) is `success`, 17 checks success (L1, ST, UT, Coverage, merge-gate, 5x L2, Freeze mocked E2E, CodeCheck); L3/L4-L5/Docker/Binary are `skipped` by policy.
- Remaining blocker is the human one: re-approval and the `needs-human` product-risk decision. The tip is unchanged (`070820a6`), so no CI re-run was triggered by this edit; the label is left untouched.

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

## Review follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5697796828, 2026-10-30)

Both points from that review are closed in code, not in prose. The branch was rebased onto today's `main` (`4e4837a9`) with no conflicts, and now carries three commits: the feature commit, the red test commit `85a78ad8`, and the fix `54889783`. New tip: `54889783e4831af67df7df517f7bd65912ea1da4`. Diff against `4e4837a9`: 15 files, +846/−14 (the two new files are the gate and its tests).

### 1. `requestConfirmation` is required, and the gate itself fails closed

- **`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:587`** — `EvolveTurnContext.requestConfirmation` is now required (`RequestEvolveConfirmation`, declared at `:203`), so any new evolve construction site that forgets it is a compile error instead of a silent spend. `tsc -p services/api` is what enforces it.
- **`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:385-387`** — the `turn.approvalMode !== "ask_for_dangerous"` fallback is gone; the runtime asks the gate and returns its refusal.
- **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:88-97`** — when the callback is absent (only reachable from a caller outside the type system: an untyped script, a stale build, a test double), the gate returns
  `{ confirmed: false, refusedBecause: "confirmation unavailable: this turn has no approval path, so the evolution search was not started" }`.
  **Caller-visible behaviour:** `createEvolveRun` returns that string as its `refusedBecause`; the tool layer hands it to the agent, which relays it; no run is created, no discrimination probe runs, no budget is spent. It is the same data-not-exception shape as the existing "not confirmed by the user" refusal.
- **Why required rather than only fail-closed:** the field is what makes the *next* construction site safe at compile time; the runtime guard alone would only cover callers the type system never sees, and those must still be refused rather than allowed.

On `always_allow`: with the gate wired, an `always_allow` session still short-circuits inside `store.requestPermission` (`services/api/src/store.ts:5532`) — that is the product's meaning of the mode for every privileged action (`run_shell`, `direct_code`, …). The defect the review named was the *absent* gate falling back to that mode; a missing gate can no longer start a search. Making evolve pop a card in `always_allow` would make it stricter than every other privileged action, which is a permission-model decision rather than this PR's change.

### 2. Grant matching is by `resource`, so the resource now names the search

Read, not inferred:

- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5545-5552`** — `const matcherResource = permissionMatcherResource(action, resource)`, then `permissionGrants.find(grant => grant.action === action && (grant.resource === matcherResource || grant.resource === resource) && grant.state === "active" && grant.scope !== "once" && (global / project / conversation / session …))`. A standing grant is matched by **action + resource**, and non-`once` scopes are reusable.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5621-5629`** — deciding `allow_matching` creates a grant with `resource: permissionMatcherResource(request.action, request.resource)` and `scope: "session"`.
- **`packages/governance/src/permission-policy.ts:56-62`** — for `code` the matcher resource is the resource verbatim, so any suffix survives matching.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5471-5485`** — `authorizeByJiuwenSwarm` does look a record up by `toolCallId`, but only to avoid double-booking the decision row; it is not the grant lookup.

So the old `evolve-search:<sessionId>` really did let one "allow matching" click cover every later search in the session. Fixed at **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:64-76`**: the key is now `evolve-search:<sessionId>:<fresh id>`, one per attempt — the card approves the search the user was shown and nothing after it, and even a retried call asks again. Wording follows the implementation in **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts:361`** ("That card approves one search: a later search in the same conversation raises its own card") and in the card label **`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:449`** / **`:3422`** ("this evolution search only" / "仅限本次演进搜索").

### Revert proof (fix reverted on the same tree, then restored)

```
$ git checkout 85a78ad8 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts
not ok 1 - a turn with no approval path refuses the search instead of allowing it
not ok 2 - each search attempt gets its own grant key, even for a repeated call
not ok 3 - a grant from one search does not authorize the next search in the same session
not ok 4 - the gate asks with the call's identity and the search it is paying for
# tests 4
# pass 0
# fail 4
$ git checkout 54889783 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts   # restored
```

The red commit `85a78ad8` carries the same four tests, failing on the unfixed gate. Test 3 drives the real `SessionStore`: it decides `allow_matching` on the first search's resource, shows the same search is then allowed, and asserts the next search is still pending (a card).

### Ran on this tip

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` → **4/4 pass**
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/*.test.ts` → **165/165 pass**
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → **exit 0** (this is the check that enforces the required field)
- `cd packages/evolve && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` → **10/10 pass**; `tsc -p packages/evolve` → **exit 0**
- `cd apps/web && tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → **1183/1183 pass**; `tsc -p apps/web` → **exit 0**

**Not run:** L2/L3, Docker and binary layers, and the full `pnpm check`.

CI: pushing a new tip re-triggers the pull-request gates for it; the previous tip's green run does not carry over to `54889783`.

## Low finding follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5706765348, inline 4419359334)

`PermissionDecisionActions` no longer offers **Allow same type** for an `evolve-search:` request. Each evolution search asks with a fresh single-use key (`evolve-search:<session>:<uuid>`), and a `code` grant is matched on the whole resource, so a same-type grant could never authorize a later search: the button promised a decision the backend drops, and it printed the attempt id in the help text and left a dead grant in `PermissionGrantManager`. That card now offers **Allow once** or **Deny**; ordinary `code` requests keep the button.

`RunTimeline` shows the localized scope (`permissions.evolveResource`) in its details **Resource** row instead of the raw per-attempt resource, matching the collapsed card that already hid it.

Coverage: `apps/web/tests/Permissions.test.tsx` and `apps/web/tests/RunTimeline.test.tsx` assert the evolve confirmation has one secondary action, no "Allow same type", and no `evolve-search:` string in the rendered markup. Reverting the two component files turns exactly those two tests red (`# tests 81 / # pass 79 / # fail 2`); restoring them returns 81/81.

Ran: `apps/web` `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` **1185/1185**; `tsc -p apps/web` exit 0; `services/api` `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` **4/4**.
Not run: full `pnpm check`, L2/L3, Docker/binary.

## Typecheck-gate fix

Deleting the type field left two test literals setting it; only the root `tsconfig.tests.json` checks extraneous properties (`tsc -p services/api` does not include test files), so the local run missed it.

Ran: `pnpm --recursive typecheck` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0; `tsc -p services/api` exit 0; `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` 4/4.

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）
