closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
### 1. Summary

On a **native Windows** deployment (host processes, no Docker/WSL), the Runner's managed scientific
environment never becomes usable. The micromamba provisioning run that builds `starter-python` fails
inside the **shared package cache**, and the failure is a path-length failure, not a download or a
disk failure:

* libmamba reports individual files inside extracted cache entries as `... is missing`;
* those files **are not missing** — they exist and are reachable through an extended-length (`\\?\`)
  path, and only unreachable through a normal Windows path;
* libmamba then declares the entry an invalid cache, tries to delete and re-extract it, and
  `remove_all: The directory is not empty.` fires because the delete step hits the same length limit;
* the entry is left with its `info\` directory gone, which is the condition under which conda
  considers a cache entry permanently unusable, and nothing in the Runner resets that shared cache.

Net effect: `scientificEnvs.available = false`, `shell.available = false`, and every `run_shell` call
returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE`. The instance cannot heal itself by restarting, and the damaged set grew
from 1 entry to 6 across two provisioning passes over the same cache.

### 2. Environment

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11, build 22631, x64 |
| Deployment | native Windows local stack (API, Runner, Evolve, Memory Graph as host processes) |
| Long-path policy | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled` = `0x0` (REG_DWORD, read with PowerShell `Get-ItemProperty`; not modified for this report) |
| Provisioner | micromamba pinned by this repo: `services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json` -> `"version": "2.8.1-0"`, `win-64` binary, 11 311 104 bytes |
| Provisioner manifest | the binary contains the `longPathAware` manifest declaration (2 string hits), which is inert while the system policy is `0` |
| Runner self-report | `/health` -> `platform=win32`, `status=ok`, `runnerVersion=0f1ff6de` (build id of a downstream fork of `main`) |
| Node.js | v22.23.4, read from the executable the Runner process is actually running |
| Cache layout | `<DATA_DIR>` (58 characters on this machine) -> `<DATA_DIR>\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs` (91 characters) -> `<...>\pkgs\https\conda.anaconda.org\conda-forge\win-64` (**135 characters**) |

The command the Runner runs, as echoed back by its own failure payload (only the prefix path is
ours, the argv is the product's):

```
micromamba.exe --no-rc create --yes --strict-channel-priority --override-channels
  --prefix <DATA_DIR>\scientific-envs\revisions\starter-python\rev-<uuid>
  --channel conda-forge python=3.12 numpy=2.0 pandas=2.2 scipy=1.14
  matplotlib-base=3.9 m2-bash m2-coreutils m2-grep m2-sed
```

### 3. Observed Evidence

#### 3.1 Path-length census over the whole cache tree

Method: walk the cache with an extended-length root, then re-`stat` every file through its plain
path. Nothing was deleted, moved or rewritten.

| measure | result |
| --- | --- |
| files in the cache tree | 15 024 |
| files whose plain path length is greater than 260 | 103 |
| files whose plain path `stat()` fails | **125** |
| of the failures, files at exactly 260 characters | 22 |
| files at 259 characters or shorter that fail | **0** |
| longest plain path that still resolves | 259 |
| directories unreachable by plain `stat` | 0 |
| deepest file in the tree | 143-character relative tail (`matplotlib-base` entry), plain absolute path 278 characters |
| budget arithmetic | 135 (channel directory) + 143 (deepest tail) = 278; keeping every entry addressable needs the channel directory at or below **116** characters |

The two counts (103 and 125) differ by exactly the 22 files sitting at 260 characters, so the
effective ceiling is **259**: the documented 260 includes the terminating NUL. 125 is the damaged set;
103 is what a strict "longer than 260" filter reports, and both are quoted where they differ.

#### 3.2 The six files reported as "missing" exist

Each entry below is one file inside a cache entry, checked by extended-length path and by plain path.

| cache entry | file reported missing | plain path length | exists | reachable by plain path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fonttools-4.68.0-py312h05f76fc_0` | `varLib\__pycache__\interpolatableTestContourOrder.cpython-312.pyc` | 262 | yes | no |
| `libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001` | `Library\share\man\man3\hwloc_obj_attr_u_hwloc_numanode_attr_s_hwloc_memory_page_type_s.3` | 262 | yes | no |
| `matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0` | `backends\qt_editor\__pycache__\_formlayout.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `numpy-2.0.2-py312h49bc9c5_1` | `_core\tests\__pycache__\test_casting_floatingpoint_errors.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `pandas-2.2.3-py312h72972c8_3` | `core\array_algos\__pycache__\datetimelike_accumulations.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `scipy-1.14.1-py312h337df96_2` | `optimize\_trustregion_constr\__pycache__\canonical_constraint.cpython-312.pyc` | 266 | yes | no |

So the correct statement is: **inaccessible through a normal Windows path, present on disk.** These
are not lost files and the archives themselves are intact (80 `.conda` archives still present,
55 under `win-64` and 25 under `noarch`; no partial-download markers anywhere).

Resulting cache state, 81 extracted entries (56 `win-64` + 25 `noarch`):

* exactly **6** entries now lack `info\` — the same six as the table above, all with the same
  directory mtime (14:41:58 of the same day);
* all 25 `noarch` entries still have `info\index.json`;
* entries that also contain over-long files but survived: `libpython` (5 files), `libwinpthread` (1),
  `m2-filesystem` (1), plus 260-character-only cases in `python` (3) and `m2-msys2-runtime` (1);
* `matplotlib-base` is the one gutted entry that also lost its `.conda` archive, which is why it is
  the entry the final `critical` line names.

#### 3.3 The messages, verbatim

First provisioning pass, one entry flagged (`<CACHE>` stands for the 135-character channel directory):

```
warning  libmamba Invalid package cache, file '<CACHE>\libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001\Library\share\man\man3\hwloc_obj_attr_u_hwloc_numanode_attr_s_hwloc_memory_page_type_s.3' is missing
error    libmamba Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache for 'libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001.conda'
critical libmamba Package cache error.
```

Second provisioning pass, same cache, now six entries flagged, each immediately followed by a failed
delete-and-re-extract:

```
warning  libmamba Invalid package cache, file '<CACHE>\<entry>\<over-long file>' is missing     (x6, alphabetical entry order)
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\pandas-2.2.3-py312h72972c8_3"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\numpy-2.0.2-py312h49bc9c5_1"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\scipy-1.14.1-py312h337df96_2"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\fonttools-4.68.0-py312h05f76fc_0"
critical libmamba remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0"
```

Two things follow from this transcript. The flagged set went from 1 entry to 6 over the *same* cache,
so which entry dies depends on scan order rather than on a fixed rule - the remaining deep-path
packages can be added on a later pass. And the earlier `Failed to load shard for package 'libgdal-*'
... will download` warnings are cold-cache noise: they are self-resolving, and extraction succeeded
after them.

#### 3.4 Runner state that results from it

* `/health` (Runner) and `/api/health` (API) both report `scientificEnvs` with `available=false`,
  `enabled=true`, `startersReady=false`, `provisioner=null`, `languages=[]`, and `unavailableReason`
  carrying the full transcript above; `revisions\` ends up holding no environment at all.
* In the captured run history we hold for one session, **11** `run_shell` tool results carry
  `{"code":"RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE","dispatched":false, ... }`.
* Capability probes return `shell.available=false` while the top-level `runner.status` still reads
  `ok` - the gap is only visible in the payload, never in the headline status.
* The bootstrap is fire-and-forget: a failed `setupManagedEnvironments()` logs one `WARN`
  (`server.ts:1300-1301`) and the service continues to report itself healthy.
* The user-visible cost is not an error dialog: each shell request parks for about 10 minutes in
  `wait_for_runner` and then hands the whole micromamba transcript to the agent as its "reason".

#### 3.5 Secondary: the failure is also hard to see in the logs

Not the cause, recorded because it cost us two rounds of diagnosis. `shortErrorMessage()`
(`packages/operational-logging/src/redaction.ts:40-42`) front-slices at 500 characters. The two
`runner.log` bootstrap-failure lines unescape to exactly 500 characters: 448 of them are the echoed
command line, leaving 52 characters of actual child-process stderr, so in `runner.log` the first
failing package name is simply absent. The untruncated copies exist only in `api.log`
(2 936 and 8 698 characters).

### 4. Controlled Experiment

#### 4.1 Reproduction recipe

1. Windows host, `LongPathsEnabled = 0`, native (non-Docker, non-WSL) stack.
2. Put the instance data directory at a realistic depth. The channel directory is the data directory
   plus 77 characters (`\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs\https\conda.anaconda.org\conda-forge\win-64`)
   and the deepest tail this package set creates is 143 characters, so a data directory of **40
   characters or more** is already enough to push an entry to 260 and out of reach (40 + 77 + 143 =
   260). Ours is 58.
3. Start the Runner so that it bootstraps `starter-python` with the default package set.
4. Observe: the messages in 3.3, `scientificEnvs.available=false`, and, in the cache tree, entries
   that have no `info\index.json` while still containing files whose plain path is 260 characters or
   longer.

#### 4.2 The comparison arm

Same micromamba binary, same `win-64` package set, same long target prefix (109 characters). The
only variable changed: the **package cache root** was pointed at a 10-character directory through the
mechanism `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` feeds (`CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` plus `--offline`). The long-path
registry policy stayed at `0` in both arms.

| measure | long cache root (production argv) | short cache root (arm B) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exit code | `Command failed` (non-zero) | `0`, 29.6 s, 195 output lines |
| `Invalid package cache` lines | 6 | 0 |
| lines containing `remove_all: The directory is not empty` | 7 (6 `error` + 1 `critical`) | 0 |
| `warning` / `error` / `critical` lines | 6 / 6 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| network use | downloads required - three packages announced `will download`, and the cache's 56 package directories were written in one contiguous 38-second window | `Total download: 0 B`, `will download` 0 times |
| environment produced | none to measure - `revisions\` holds no directory, because each failed attempt removes its own revision | 16 847 files, all 81 packages of the spec linked, **0** files unreachable by plain `stat`, deepest path 220 characters |
| real computation through it | not possible | `rc=0`, 2 550 ms, empty stderr, python 3.12.16 + matplotlib 3.9.4 (Agg), PNG 6 165 bytes, CSV 272 bytes |

What this establishes: the packages, the solver and the disk are fine, and moving **only** the cache
to a short root makes the identical provisioning succeed. What it does not establish is listed in
section 10.

### 5. Expected Behavior

1. Before provisioning, the Runner should know its path budget. The cache root is derived as
   `<dataDir>\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs`; the channel subdirectory is already 135 characters
   on this machine, and the deepest entry path this package set creates is 143 characters, so the
   channel directory has to stay at or under 116 characters for the entries to remain addressable. A
   length pre-flight (root length plus the expected tail) would catch this before micromamba runs.
2. If the budget cannot be met, fail fast with an explicit compatibility diagnostic that prints the
   offending root, its length, the platform's long-path state and the supported remedy - instead of
   letting a package manager report individual files as missing.
3. The cache location should be short and stable by default on Windows (a machine-level short root,
   or `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` honoured by default rather than only when explicitly set),
   rather than inheriting an arbitrarily deep per-instance data directory.
4. Cache validation and cache removal should use the same long-path-aware access that the rest of a
   Windows deployment needs (`\\?\` / `path.toNamespacedPath`, the pattern already used in
   `packages/cas`), so that a file libmamba just wrote cannot become invisible to libmamba one step
   later.
5. A path-length condition must not be reported as "file is missing" or as a generic
   `Package cache error`. As written, the message tells the operator that the package cache is
   corrupt, which invites exactly the wrong remedy (wipe the cache and re-download, which reproduces
   the same state).
6. After an entry is invalidated in the shared cache, the Runner should be able to recover it, or
   stop using it. Today the failure path removes only the per-attempt
   `revisions/<env>` directory (`environment-store.ts:924`) and never the shared entries, and the next
   start repeats the identical `create` against that cache, so every bootstrap re-reads the same
   poisoned entries.

### 6. Actual Behavior

* Provisioning fails, first with `Invalid package cache ... is missing` and
  `Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache`, then with `remove_all: The directory is not empty`
  and `critical libmamba ...`, and the shared cache ends up with 6 unusable entries.
* The state is stable across restarts: the entries keep their gutted form, `revisions\` stays empty,
  and a second pass flags more entries than the first.
* `scientificEnvs.available=false`, `startersReady=false`, `shell.available=false`;
  `run_shell` returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` with `dispatched=false`, so no shell or Python step can
  execute for the whole instance.
* `runner.status` still says `ok`, and the only log line about it is one `WARN` whose message is
  truncated to 500 characters, so neither the UI nor `runner.log` states that the scientific
  environment is dead.
* The guidance the failure itself returns points at a remedy that cannot work against this cause:
  `Recreate or update the starter environment on the target Runner to repair managed Bash and its
  required utilities.` Re-creating the environment re-reads the same poisoned shared cache; that is
  exactly what happened here, where a later pass flagged five more entries than the first one did.

### 7. Questions for Maintainers

1. Is native Windows (host processes, no Docker/WSL) a supported runtime mode for the Runner? The
   install and quick-start documentation is what we followed; nothing in it states a path-length
   requirement for the data directory.
2. If it is not supported, should the launcher detect the platform and refuse with a clear message
   at startup, instead of booting and reporting `status=ok` while `shell.available=false`?
3. If it is supported, which fix do you prefer: (a) a short machine-level default cache root, or
   honouring `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` by default on Windows; (b) long-path-aware validation
   and removal of cache entries; (c) a pre-flight length check plus an explicit compatibility
   diagnostic; or a combination?
4. Could CI gain a provisioning regression test whose cache entries sit at **259, 260 and 261+**
   characters, covering create, extract, and the cleanup/`remove_all` path? The 259/260 boundary is
   where our damaged set changes character, and it is the case a "just below MAX_PATH" test misses.
5. `services/runner/src/platform/win32.ts:117-128` already substitutes `matplotlib-base` for
   `matplotlib` precisely because the qt6 tree exceeds MAX_PATH. Our data says that substitution is
   necessary but not sufficient: `matplotlib-base-3.9.4` is itself one of the six gutted entries,
   because its own `Lib\site-packages\...\__pycache__` test artefacts reach 260+ characters. Should
   the starter set be screened by measured depth rather than by known-bad package names?
6. Should an entry invalidated in the shared cache be reset automatically (with an audit record),
   given that the instance cannot recover by restarting?

### 8. Scope

This report is about **Windows native Runner environment provisioning** and its package cache.
Deliberately excluded, each with its own report: agent output truncation, MCP connector bookkeeping,
Memory Graph behaviour, and usage accounting. The 500-character log slicing in 3.5 is mentioned only
because it hides this particular error, not as a logging proposal.

### 9. Source-code references (checked against the current `main`)

* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:389` - `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX: resolve(config.root,
  "provisioner")`, which is what ties the cache to the per-instance data directory.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:390` - `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` is exported only when
  `config.packageCacheDir` is set; `:1104-1105` - `--offline` likewise.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:540` - the only pre-flight on the cache directory is an
  existence check (`await access(...)`); there is no length check, and no `MAX_PATH`, `\\?\` or
  `toNamespacedPath` token appears anywhere in this file.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:906` and `:924` - `bootstrapStarter()` create arguments,
  and the failure path that removes only `revisions/<id>`.
* `services/runner/src/server.ts:397-398` - `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` is the sole override.
* `services/runner/src/server.ts:1300-1301` - `void setupManagedEnvironments().catch(...)`, one
  `WARN` on failure.
* `services/runner/src/platform/win32.ts:117-128` and `services/runner/src/platform/types.ts:80-86` -
  the existing MAX_PATH note for this starter package set.
* `services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json:2` - the pinned provisioner version.
* `packages/operational-logging/src/redaction.ts:16` and `:40-42` - the 500-character front-slice.

### 10. What this report does not establish

* **Mechanism granularity.** That micromamba validates and deletes cache entries through
  non-extended-length paths is inferred from the message text plus the resulting on-disk state (which
  files remain, which disappear, in what order), not from libmamba's source, which is a binary here.
  The observable facts in 3 are independent of that inference.
* **`LongPathsEnabled = 1` was not tested.** Changing the registry was outside the authorised scope,
  so we cannot claim that enabling the policy would fix it; the `longPathAware` declaration in the
  binary is inert while the policy is off, and we did not verify per-call behaviour with the policy
  on.
* **Concurrency is excluded as the cause of the damage in our instance**, but for a narrower reason
  than "locks exist": downloads and extraction all fall inside one runner generation's window
  (monotone, 09:00:07-09:00:45), the previous generation had only fetched repodata,
  `enqueueMutation()` serialises mutations in-process, no second `scientific-envs` tree exists on
  this machine, and `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` was unset so no cache is shared between
  instances. There is **no cross-process lock** around the package cache; two Runners configured with
  the same cache root could race. We report that as a structural risk, not as part of this failure.
* **The comparison arm in 4.2 bypassed the service.** It ran micromamba directly with the equivalent
  argv; configuring `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` in the launcher and restarting was not
  authorised. `Total download: 0 B` also does not prove the offline seed fully served the solve, and
  `--offline` pins the package set to what was seeded, so packages beyond this spec would need the
  seed to cover them too.
* **Sample size.** Two provisioning passes in one instance, one session's run history, and the six
  entries named above. We did not survey other Windows hosts.
* **The earlier Docker observation is a user-provided history, not evidence.** Running the same
  product under Docker worked, as reported by the operator, but we have not run a same-SHA,
  same-configuration controlled comparison, so we explicitly do **not** present "Docker works" as a
  proven cause-or-cure for anything in this report.

### 11. Related items and prior search

Searched the tracker before filing, over open and closed issues, for `MAX_PATH`, `micromamba`,
`LongPathsEnabled`, `Package cache error`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `remove_all`, `longPathAware`,
`Windows provisioning` and `scientific environment bootstrap`. No existing item covers this defect;
`LongPathsEnabled`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `remove_all` and `longPathAware` each return zero results. The
nearest items, all distinct from this one:

* #643 - Windows runtime: native startup chain, execution routing, micromamba environments (closed) -
  the feature this report is about.
* #916 - Windows managed Shell missing base Unix tools and a diagnosable capability declaration
  (closed) - adjacent, different defect: tools absent in a *successfully created* environment.
* #583 - CAS: Windows durable-directory sync with `toNamespacedPath` (closed) - precedent that the
  long-path namespace treatment is already applied elsewhere in this project.

### 12. References

* Installation (docs site we followed): https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/install/index.html
* Quick start: https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/docs/getting-started/quick-start.html
* Mamba troubleshooting, which documents the same class of Windows path problem:
  https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/troubleshooting.html
* Windows path limits (the 260 value that includes the terminating NUL, and the `\\?\` prefix):
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file

closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. (searched `backslash`, `path separator`, `llm_wiki_mcp`, `_page_path`, `relative Wiki page path`, `wiki path` across issues and PRs; the only separator-related reports are #903 and #1046, which concern Windows device names in the API/workspace layer and are already closed)
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. (verified against `main` = `807982f00da6253b41042146171554c51ecc2c3e`, committed 2026-11-11)
- [x] Environment information and a minimal reproducible demo are provided below.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The `llm-wiki` MCP bridge refuses to read any Wiki page whose path uses Windows separators, even though the
bridge's own `search` tool returns exactly such paths, and the Wiki HTTP API serves them happily.
`get_page` / `get_pages` therefore fail on the identifier that `search` just produced — and the failure is
client-side, so no HTTP request is ever attempted.

Upstream already recognizes this provider behavior and normalizes it on the **result** side:

```ts
// packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.ts:132-135
// Search results carry the provider's index paths, which may use Windows
// separators; normalize them so page lookups round-trip cleanly.
const rawPath = page.page_id ?? page.path;
const path = typeof rawPath === "string" ? rawPath.replaceAll("\\", "/") : rawPath;
```

and tests it under the name `"search normalizes Windows-style index paths so page lookups round-trip"`
(`packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.test.ts:67-81`), with fixtures that are themselves Windows-style
(`page_id: "debates\\fusion_v3_1_3_二烯.md"`, `path: "concepts\\mechanisms\\phase-transfer-catalysis.md"`).

The normalization is missing on the **input** side of both layers, so the documented round-trip closes only
halfway:

| layer | normalizes `\` → `/` on output | accepts `\` on input |
|---|---|---|
| `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py` (MCP bridge) | no | **no** — raises `ValueError` |
| `packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.ts` (connector) | yes (`:135`) | **no** — `validateInput` returns `valid:false` (`:118`, `:120`) |

`get_page`'s own description instructs the caller to pass the search result
(`llm-wiki.ts:38` — *"Read one LLM Wiki page by the path returned by search"*), and the JSON schema for that
argument permits a backslash (`llm-wiki.ts:26` — `pathSchema = { type: "string", minLength: 1, maxLength: 500 }`),
so both the schema and the documentation allow what the validator then refuses.

### Minimal reproducible demo (no Wiki server required)

The exception is raised before any network call, so the failure reproduces against a bare checkout:

```python
# repro.py — run from the repository root; needs no external service
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "services/gateway/src")
from sciencediscovery_gateway.llm_wiki_mcp import _page_path

# these three strings are verbatim search outputs; the last two are already used as
# normalizeResult fixtures in packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.test.ts:69-70
for page_id in ["sources\\photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md",
                "debates\\fusion_v3_1_3_二烯.md",
                "concepts\\mechanisms\\phase-transfer-catalysis.md"]:
    try:
        print("ACCEPTED  ", repr(page_id), "->", repr(_page_path(page_id)))
    except ValueError as exc:
        print("REJECTED  ", repr(page_id), "->", exc)

for ok in ["sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md", "知识/Overview 1.md"]:
    print("ACCEPTED  ", repr(ok), "->", repr(_page_path(ok)))
```

Observed:

```
REJECTED   'sources\\photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md' -> Expected a relative Wiki page path
REJECTED   'debates\\fusion_v3_1_3_二烯.md' -> Expected a relative Wiki page path
REJECTED   'concepts\\mechanisms\\phase-transfer-catalysis.md' -> Expected a relative Wiki page path
ACCEPTED   'sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md' -> 'sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md'
ACCEPTED   '知识/Overview 1.md' -> '知识/Overview 1.md'
```

Expected: the three `REJECTED` lines should normalize to the slash form and be accepted, exactly as
`llm-wiki.ts:135` already does for the same values on the way out.

### End-to-end reproduction against a live Wiki

Real reproduction path: the shipped module, imported the way the MCP server imports it, one request per arm,
the two arms of each pair differing **only** by the separator.

```
$ SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_WIKI_URL=http://<wiki-host>:8003 /opt/sciencediscovery/envs/gateway/bin/python repro_live.py
BASE_URL= http://<wiki-host>:8003
```

**1. `search` returns a Windows-style `page_id`** (`limit=1`, 882 ms, HTTP 200):

```json
{ "arm": "search_top_k_1", "outcome": "OK", "total_results": 1, "retrieval_mode": "hybrid",
  "hits": [{ "keys": ["chunk_content","matched_keywords","page_id","relevance_score","source","source_refs","summary","tags","title"],
             "fields": { "page_id": "sources\\photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md",
                         "source": "vector",
                         "title": "Photoinduced Copper-Catalyzed Asymmetric C−O Cross-Coupling" } }] }
```

**2. Passing that value verbatim to `get_page` raises before the request** — complete traceback:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/probe/pW44l-traceback.py", line 17, in main
    await get_page(page_id)
  File "/app/services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py", line 79, in get_page
    return await _request("GET", f"wiki/{quote(_page_path(path), safe='/')}")
                                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/app/services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py", line 47, in _page_path
    raise ValueError("Expected a relative Wiki page path")
ValueError: Expected a relative Wiki page path
```

`search returned page_id = "sources\\photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md"`, and the failing arm
sent **0** HTTP requests (the only outbound requests in the run are the successful `200` from `search` and the
slash control arm below).

**3. The same call with only the separator rewritten succeeds** (control arm, same process, same page):

```json
{ "arm": "search_then_get_page_real_chain",
  "search_returned_identifier": "sources\\photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md",
  "contains_backslash": true,
  "get_page_outcome": "RAISED", "get_page_ms": 0,
  "get_page_exc_type": "ValueError", "get_page_exc": "Expected a relative Wiki page path",
  "control_slash_outcome": "OK", "control_slash_ms": 58,
  "control_slash_path": "sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md",
  "control_slash_content_chars": 50524 }
```

Literal-path arms, for completeness:

```json
{ "arm": "get_page_backslash_literal",  "outcome": "RAISED", "ms": 0,  "exc_type": "ValueError", "exc": "Expected a relative Wiki page path" }
{ "arm": "get_page_slash_literal",      "outcome": "OK",     "ms": 59, "path": "sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md", "content_chars": 50524 }
{ "arm": "get_pages_backslash_literal", "outcome": "RAISED", "ms": 0,  "exc_type": "ValueError", "exc": "Expected a relative Wiki page path" }
```

`get_pages` with the slash form could not be verified as working in this environment: that deployment returned
`500 Internal Server Error` on `POST /api/v1/wiki/pages/batch` for every payload shape we tried (valid paths,
invalid paths, with and without a mix), which is an unrelated server-side fault and is reported here only so
the table above is not read as evidence about separators for the batch tool.

### The Wiki HTTP API itself accepts both forms

Direct `GET` against the same service, one request per arm, separator percent-encoded in the first arm
(`returned_path` is the page's own `path` field — the server echoes back the separator it was given):

```json
{ "label": "D1_raw_backslash",
  "url": "http://<wiki-host>:8003/api/v1/wiki/sources%5Cphotoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md",
  "status": 200, "ms": 59, "bytes": 102889,
  "returned_path": "sources\\photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md" }
{ "label": "D2_slash_normalized",
  "url": "http://<wiki-host>:8003/api/v1/wiki/sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md",
  "status": 200, "ms": 60, "bytes": 102888,
  "returned_path": "sources/photoinduced-copper-catalyzed-asymmetric-c-o-c.md" }
```

Same page, same 13 top-level keys, same title; the two bodies differ by exactly one byte, which is the echoed
separator. Neither the Wiki's index layout nor its HTTP layer requires `/` — only the bridge does.

### Source locations

`services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py:43-48` (blob `01991020f83eeaaa127f7e44c547aaac3b6ad178`):

```python
def _page_path(path: str) -> str:
    if (not 0 < len(path) <= 500 or any(c in path for c in "\\%?#:")
            or any(ord(c) < 32 for c in path)
            or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in path.split("/"))):
        raise ValueError("Expected a relative Wiki page path")
    return path
```

The two tools funnel through it, so a single change covers both:

- `llm_wiki_mcp.py:79` — `get_page`: `quote(_page_path(path), safe='/')`
- `llm_wiki_mcp.py:89` — `get_pages`: `"paths": [_page_path(path) for path in paths]`

`packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.ts:57-61` (blob `55f3adcf294510b8b927de286318becb65c9ed77`) encodes the same
rule in TypeScript (`!/[\\%?#\x00-\x1f:]/.test(value)`), applied to inputs at `:118` and `:120` and to outputs
only after normalization at `:136`.

## Suggested Fix

Normalize the separator **before** validation, keeping every current check, in the one shared validator each
layer already funnels through — so `get_page` and `get_pages` cannot diverge:

```python
def _page_path(path: str) -> str:
    path = path.replace("\\", "/")          # Windows separators from the Wiki index
    if (not 0 < len(path) <= 500 or any(c in path for c in "\\%?#:")
            or any(ord(c) < 32 for c in path)
            or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in path.split("/"))):
        raise ValueError("Expected a relative Wiki page path")
    return path
```

and in TypeScript, folding first inside `isPagePath` (already called from `:118`, `:120` and `:136`) rather
than at each call site:

```ts
function normalizePagePath(value: string): string {
  return value.replaceAll("\\", "/");
}
function isPagePath(value: unknown): value is string {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || value.length === 0) return false;
  const path = normalizePagePath(value);
  return path.length <= 500 && !/[\\%?#\x00-\x1f:]/.test(path)
    && path.split("/").every((part) => part !== "" && part !== "." && part !== "..");
}
```

Design constraints the fix must satisfy:

1. Backslash → forward slash, applied once, before every other check, in the shared validator used by both tools.
2. The 500-character limit is retained.
3. Traversal protection is retained: `""`, `.` and `..` segments are still rejected **after** normalization, so
   `a\..\b` collapses to the already-rejected `a/../b` rather than becoming a new escape.
4. Control characters, `%`, `?`, `#` and `:` are still rejected; percent-encoded separators (`a%5Cb`) stay
   refused because no URL-decoding step is introduced.
5. `get_page` and `get_pages` share one normalization point; no per-tool copy.
6. Nothing is weakened. After the change these inputs must **still** be refused: `../secret`, `/etc/passwd`,
   `a/../b`, `a\..\b`, `a//b`, `a\x\..\y`, `%2e%2e/x`, `a%5Cb`, `a?x`, `a#x`, `a:b`, `C:\Windows\win.ini`,
   `a\n`, `""`, and any path longer than 500 characters. This list was not assumed to be safe — it was measured
   by feeding each entry's folded form through the unchanged `_page_path`, and all fifteen still raise
   `ValueError("Expected a relative Wiki page path")`.

Test cases that must change, and nothing else in those files: `services/gateway/tests/test_llm_wiki_mcp.py:54`
(rejection list contains `a\x`) and `packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.test.ts:32` (rejection list contains
`a\b`). Both entries move from "rejected" to "normalized and accepted"; every other element of both lists
stays. The existing normalization test `llm-wiki.test.ts:67` must keep passing unchanged.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Deployment: Linux container running this repository; image tag `catalystpi-jd:task001-30178fda7`, i.e. built
  from a downstream fork at commit `30178fda77ae53c51bde1f8b77c62d2c14901929` (branch `integration/test`, clean
  working tree). The three files above are **byte-identical** in that fork and in `main` (see Version Information).
- Interpreter used by the MCP server: `/opt/sciencediscovery/envs/gateway/bin/python` → CPython 3.12.12 (the
  image's `/usr/bin/python3` is 3.11.2 and does not carry the gateway dependencies, so it is not what runs).
- Node in the image: 22.23.4. The TypeScript layer was verified by reading `main`'s source; we did not execute
  it because `packages/mcp-sources/dist` is not present in the deployed image, so that half of the report is a
  source-level finding rather than a runtime one.
- Wiki service: external LLM Wiki (self-reported `service: catalyst-knowledge`, `wiki_version: v1696`),
  `http://<wiki-host>:8003`; `/health` returned `{"status":"ok", "warming_up":false}` and `/ready` reported
  the BM25 index loaded. It is not part of this repository, which is why the compatibility fix belongs in the
  bridge that consumes its paths.
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_WIKI_MODE` was not changed; the bridge sends `mode: "hybrid"`.
- No credentials are involved: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_WIKI_TOKEN` was empty for these calls and the service
  returned `200` anyway.

## Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` `main` = `807982f00da6253b41042146171554c51ecc2c3e`, commit date `2026-11-11T15:36:12Z`. Current `main` still contains the rejection (`llm_wiki_mcp.py:44`).
- `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/llm_wiki_mcp.py` → git blob `01991020f83eeaaa127f7e44c547aaac3b6ad178`, 3945 bytes.
- `services/gateway/tests/test_llm_wiki_mcp.py` → git blob `263afbc4dc20d207cfe8d2e2efc7b76242c377d7`, 5063 bytes.
- `packages/mcp-sources/src/llm-wiki.ts` → git blob `55f3adcf294510b8b927de286318becb65c9ed77`, 9033 bytes.
- Same content confirmed in the deployed image, compared line-ending-independently by SHA-1 over CR-stripped bytes:
  `llm_wiki_mcp.py` → `e5ea86dbe7a473f6900ae801750e6baf0617c8f0` (image) = `e5ea86dbe7a473f6900ae801750e6baf0617c8f0` (`main`);
  `llm-wiki.ts` → `46a9a7cfe62600c67ffded9425a3925b3c21c2ee` (image) = `46a9a7cfe62600c67ffded9425a3925b3c21c2ee` (`main`).
- Also identical in the downstream fork used above: `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` returns the same three blob OIDs.

## Additional Information

Acceptance tests we would expect a fix to pass (beyond the design constraints above):

1. **Forward-slash baseline** — `get_page("sources/a.md")` issues `GET /api/v1/wiki/sources/a.md`;
   `get_pages(["sources/a.md","sources/b.md"])` posts `paths == ["sources/a.md","sources/b.md"]`.
2. **Windows separator** — `get_page("sources\\a.md")` issues the *same* `GET /api/v1/wiki/sources/a.md` with no
   exception, and `get_pages(["sources\\a.md"])` posts `paths == ["sources/a.md"]`.
3. **Mixed separators in one path** — `get_page("sources\\sub/a.md")` → `/api/v1/wiki/sources/sub/a.md`.
4. **search → get_page round-trip** — a mocked `search` response whose `sources[0].page_id` contains a backslash
   can be passed verbatim to `get_page` and to `get_pages`, and both succeed. Recommended fixtures are the ones
   already in `llm-wiki.test.ts:69-70`, so the Python and TypeScript suites assert the same values.
5. **Traversal still refused** — `../x`, `/x`, `a/../x`, `a\..\x`, `a//x`, `a/x/..`, `..\x` raise
   `ValueError("Expected a relative Wiki page path")` in Python and return `valid:false` in TypeScript.
6. **Illegal characters still refused** — `a%2Fb`, `a%5Cb`, `a?x`, `a#x`, `a:b`, `C:\x`, `a\nb`.
7. **Empty and oversized still refused** — `""`, an empty `paths` array, a 501-character path, more than 20 paths.
8. **Non-string input refused** — `None` / `undefined`, and non-string elements inside `paths`.
9. **Both tools agree** — a table-driven test asserting `get_page` and `get_pages` accept and reject exactly the
   same path set, so the unified validator is checked rather than assumed.
10. **Normalization is not a second code path** — for one page, the slash and backslash arms return identical
    payloads (in our live run both returned the same 50 524-character `content` and the same title).
11. **Connector returns the normalized value** — `validateInput("get_page", { path: "sources\\a.md" })` yields
    `{ valid: true, input: { path: "sources/a.md" } }`, and `validateInput("get_pages", { paths: ["a\\b.md","c.md"] })`
    yields normalized `paths`, so citation identifiers and lookups stay in one form.
12. **Existing rejection lists stay intact** — every entry of `test_llm_wiki_mcp.py:54` and
    `llm-wiki.test.ts:32` other than the single backslash case still rejects.

We did not open a PR (the observation came from testing a deployment, and the change is small enough that
maintainers may prefer to place the normalization wherever it fits the codebase best — e.g. normalizing inside
`_page_path` as above, or reusing `external_urls.py` if there is a shared path helper). Happy to send the
patch if that would be useful.

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** The mocked E2E suite is `87/88` and the one red case fails not on product behaviour but on a browser console error raised by the suite's own teardown:

```text
Error: no console/page errors expected, got:
[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  @ http://127.0.0.1:4410/api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...
```

Case: `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:380` — `S2b subagent 首个受控工具的权限卡也出现在主对话最外层`. Job `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job id 130151439627) on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462), sha `4bb737c2`.

**Evidence.** The mocked stack's `stack.log` (in `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`, artifact id 13807782121) shows the request arrives **after** the project was deleted by teardown:

```text
GET  /api/evolve/status HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
POST /cleanup/project HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/models/4eea8f0a-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET  /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...&defaults=1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

The same log carries **59** such `404` responses on `research-package/preview`, and in another case the deleted Session is still polled directly:

```text
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/runs HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/agent-activity HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

So the panel keeps polling a project/session that teardown has just removed. The browser logs every 404 as a console error, and the journey's "no console errors" assertion turns that into a failed case.

**Expected.** One of these, whichever the team prefers:

1. A mounted panel stops polling once its project/session is deleted (listen for the deletion the test performs, or cancel the poll on unmount).
2. The preview read treats "project gone" as a normal end of polling and does not surface it as a console error (checked request + handled 404, instead of an unhandled resource load).
3. The assertion is scoped to the case's own session being alive.

(1) is the honest fix: the product should not keep asking the API about a project it has removed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- Mocked E2E (`profile: daily`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`), 88 planned / 87 passed / 1 failed; run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).
- Stack: adapter 4410 → Node API 4510, runner 4411, memory-graph 17774; no real model calls in this job.

### Additional Information

This is a harness/teardown race rather than a user-facing delivery failure, but it reds the mocked gate on its own. It is unrelated to the four real-E2E failures on the same run (see the linked issues).

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; job 130151439627; artifact `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys` (13807782121)

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Three real cases die within seconds to a few minutes with the same gateway message, even though the gateway had already answered `200` and was streaming:

```text
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts;
delivery_status=failed; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=0;
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

Shards and durations on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462) (sha `4bb737c2`):

| shard | case | duration |
|---|---|---|
| research-1 | DRB-58 medium-hard Swarm research integration | 51.5 s |
| research-2 | DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration | 3.9 min |
| research-5 | DRB-75 very-hard Swarm research integration | 50.8 s |

**Evidence that the stream, not the product, broke.** `stack.log` of shard `research-1` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-1`, id 13805059079) records that request as:

```json
[model-sse-summary] {"requestId":"model-f758639a-...","httpStatus":200,"attempts":1,"retries":0,
  "elapsedMs":29176,"sseRecords":1208,"error":{"classification":"network"}}
```

So: headers `200`, 1208 SSE records delivered over ~29 s, then the transport died; `attempts:1, retries:0` — the API never retried. The previous Nightly (`c95f080`, run 42519625781) failed the same way on `research-4` (`read ECONNRESET`) and `research-6` (`other side closed`), so this is a recurring class, not a one-off.

**Why it is scored as the product's fault.** `.ci` accounting for this run reports:

```text
Planned 21; executed 21; passed 15; provider faults 0.
```

`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs:126-146` classifies a provider fault only when the text carries a 5xx status **or** one of `no available channel` / `model_not_found` / `new_api_error`. `APIError: read ECONNRESET` and `other side closed` carry neither, so these three failures stay plain `FAIL` and the gate treats them as regressions.

**Expected / decision needed.** Two separate questions:

1. **Retry (code):** a mid-stream transport break after `200` currently ends an 8–50 minute case. A bounded retry (one attempt, only when no tool result has been committed yet) would turn most of these into passes. This is a behaviour change and needs sign-off.
2. **Accounting (gate semantics):** should a failure whose only evidence is a broken transport, with no HTTP status, be recorded as `PROVIDER_FAULT`? Today it cannot be, and the result is a red Nightly for a provider outage.

Recommendation: land (1) as its own change and keep (2) separate, because (2) changes what "green Nightly" means.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`; Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).
- Model endpoint `https://api-4-agent-ci-infra.llmbots.co/v1`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`, `E2E_LLM_API_VARIANT=deepseek`, thinking mode enabled/low.
- Same failure class on the 2026-11-08 Nightly (`c95f080`, shards `research-4`/`research-6`).

### Additional Information

Shard `research-3` on the same run (`DRB-62`) failed differently — `run_error=interaction round execution failed` from `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` — and its `stack.log` does not retain the inner cause, so it is **not** claimed as the same root cause here. It is mentioned only so the two are not merged by mistake.

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; artifacts `real-e2e-evidence-research-1` (13805059079), `-2` (13805882980), `-5` (13806203752)
- Previous occurrence: Nightly 42519625781 (`c95f080`), shards `research-4`, `research-6`
