items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

items.body:
CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Current head
`4bf3ff891beb4ff0c8e9bf2776dc5882e28a551f` is a merge of `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928` and `origin/main` `f4ceca57b74b7f5a10b4f8f77313513a09886c02`. The merge tree matches a clean merge. No conflict was resolved by hand. `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`, and the CLA steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` are unchanged from `3bde9d39`. The CLA paragraph in `.ci/README.md` is unchanged; other README edits came in from `main`.

GitHub Actions run [40210190231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40210190231) completed with conclusion `success` on this head:
- UT: planned 4853, executed 4853, passed 4853, failed 0, skipped 0.
- ST: planned 24, executed 24, passed 24, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Mocked E2E, four shards combined: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118.
- Coverage and merge-gate succeeded. L3, L4/L5, Docker, and the binary release were skipped by policy.
- `Require CLA policy` ran. This pull request's own `license/cla` status was `success`, so the bot exemption was not the path that made the gate pass.

## Validation
Focused checks on `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928`, before the merge:
- `node --test .ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`: 24 passed, 0 failed. After the TAP summary the process aborted with status 134. That abort is a host behavior and not a failed assertion.
- Static collection of `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs` reported no dynamic registration.

Earlier local layers were run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`, before the exemption was narrowed. They are not the result for the current head.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4453, executed 4453, passed 4452, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.test.ts` (the scratch directory was already 86 bytes). That case passed when rerun with a shorter temporary directory.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5, skipped 0. All five failures were in `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` and matched baseline `7ee6c1d0`.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked): planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. The spec matched baseline `7ee6c1d0`.

The GitHub run above is the result for `4bf3ff89`. The earlier local UT failure in `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` did not fail this run.

## E2E user journeys
PASS on the current head for the mocked shards in run 40210190231: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118. Real-model journeys were not run. This change does not alter product UI.

The earlier local mocked run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d` failed one pre-existing layout assertion: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. Counts for that older run: planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0.

## Release
Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. Only `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` can merge when `license/cla` is present and not success. Other bots and human authors stay blocked in that case. A CLA check that never appears does not block anyone.

Compatibility and migration: none. `license/cla` stays off the required status checks on purpose. This workflow change needs a human review; merge-when-ready is not enabled.

Closes #44

### Summary
Users could not tell whether choosing a model in the conversation picker applied to just this conversation or persisted globally. It applies only to the current session; a new session inherits the project model, falling back to the system default when no project model is set. This change adds an English/Chinese trigger tooltip and a persistent explanatory note in the open dialog. The note is bound to the open dialog with `aria-describedby` via `React.useId`, not to the closed trigger. Only `apps/web/src/composer/ModelPicker.tsx` and `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` change; persistence, configuration, selection callbacks, and CSS are unchanged, and no dependency or tracked test file is added.

### Validation
Final signed commit `9d7818c0b6a15912b154fe23827c96525baa80bd` on base `4b23ad3abc519ca10c42bfc36eda567949ec6c41`. On the current base the single affected case reproduces RED solely because the hint is missing.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | PASS |
| Typecheck | PASS (`pnpm typecheck`) |
| Full 94-file web selector | 860 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `ci:l1` | 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (`pnpm ci:l1`) |
| Bilingual browser/API acceptance | 2 planned, 2 executed, 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped |

The results above were obtained on the final commit. Additional checks on that commit passed: the M1 smoke (1 test), `pnpm paper:test` (2 tests), and `pnpm gateway:test` (28 tests), with no failures or skips. The complete UT/ST/E2E layers remain unexecuted. Official collection produced 3 ST identities and 72 browser E2E identities; E2E also requires 9 separate SDK checks. The complete UT plan is still unknown, and SDK-dependent prerequisites remain unverified. These checks are not a complete four-layer green.

### E2E user journeys
A temporary local Playwright run using the repository fixture plus API checks; it is not a committed spec and not official `ci:e2e`. Keyboard opens the picker; after selecting a model the note remains; only the current-session override changes; a new session inherits the project model, and a new project's first session inherits the system default. EN/ZH pass, and the note is readable at 320px and 375px. At 320px the pre-existing popover frame extends roughly 7px outside the viewport while the note stays inside and stays readable; that CSS issue is out of scope.

### Release

This remains a Draft until hosted CI and review complete; it is not release ready.

items.author: Thibaultjaigu
items.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.

## Validation

- `node --test --experimental-test-coverage scripts/repo-issue-pipeline.test.mjs`: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Host line coverage **97.64%**, branch coverage **96.00%**, function coverage **50.00%** in this direct Node report. Do not interpret these as repository-wide coverage.
- Coverage gaps: the real SDK dynamic import/constructor and CLI signal callback wiring were not exercised through a live Codex process. CLI child-process coverage is not merged into the parent report. Factory injection verifies start/resume/options/event/failure behavior, but does not prove account/CLI compatibility or model scheduling quality. No paid Codex smoke, actual OS-signal integration or service-manager installation test was run.
- Skill metadata validation, JavaScript syntax check, architecture check and CI catalog check passed.
- Markdown lint: **0 issues**. Documentation links: **141 tracked Markdown files checked**, no broken targets.
- Full local UT/ST/browser E2E are **not claimed passed**. The clean checkout has not been provisioned with all package-local dependencies/build outputs: shared UT collection stopped at missing `react` in an existing web test. Initial pnpm entry-point checks also encountered dependency-layout verification; no shared dependency tree was purged. The host's serialized heavy-test lock was occupied by an existing worker, so this PR does not interrupt that task or start competing full-stack runs. Full CI remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

ScienceDiscovery product E2E: **not applicable to the changed product path**, because there is no application UI/API/agent-runtime behavior change. Full browser-suite execution is nevertheless unverified as noted above. The new contributor tool is covered by offline request-to-session/output tests; a real Codex-account-to-fork-PR journey remains an explicit integration gap and must not be represented as a mocked product E2E pass.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: optional contributor tooling only; no automatic process or new application dependency.

Compatibility and migration: none for application users. SDK dependencies are isolated in the skill's optional host package. Existing private pipeline state is neither imported nor modified.

## Follow-up: Issue-as-Interface + OSS ops skills

Added on top of `repo-issue-pipeline` (commit `01f1df6`):

- **IAI delivery:** `issue-as-interface-contract`, `issue-review-agent-ready`, `iai-developer-patrol`, `iai-worker-implement`, `iai-reviewer-patrol`, `iai-reviewer-execute`, `magpie-pr-review-pipeline`
- **OSS ops (parallel):** `oss-ops-newcomer-gfi`, `oss-ops-stale-sweep`, `oss-ops-maintainer-stats`, `oss-ops-repo-health`
- **Docs:** [zh](docs/zh/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) / [en](docs/en/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) (+ links from CONTRIBUTING and issue-pipeline pages)

Still opt-in documentation/skills only — installing does not start bots. Reviewer execute authority is skill text for hosts that enable it; this PR does not merge or change CI policy.

recent_closed_unmerged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Refs #1152 — stage 2, in progress. This branch is **stacked on #1173** (stage 1); the diff shows both until #1173 merges, and only the streaming work after that. I am opening it now so the pipeline can be reviewed while it is being finished rather than as one large surprise.

## What is in this branch so far

The background export no longer materialises the archive:

- `ResearchPackageExports.createPackage(options, destination)` — the task opens its own output file and hands the stream down;
- `writeResearchPackage(input, destination, cap)` — tar → gzip → sink, with the package checksum computed over the compressed bytes as they pass, so the receipt is byte-for-byte what the in-memory exporter produced (a unit case asserts the two archives are identical and that a source is read twice: once hashed for the manifest, once written).

Peak memory on this path drops from *payload + tar + archive* to *payload + one chunk*: the two whole-archive buffers are gone. Cancellation and the mid-export revision check now delete the partial file instead of discarding a buffer.

## What is still to land before this PR can close the issue

- **Object residency.** The packager still hashes `PackageObject.bytes`, so the payload itself is still resident. Removing it means handing the pipeline object *sources* (CAS paths) rather than buffers — the piece that makes a 5 GiB cap physically possible.
- **Streaming import.** `readArchive` still `gunzipSync`s the whole archive and keeps views into it; the plan is gunzip → temp file → per-object checksum → CAS, so the importer never holds a package either.
- **Memory/disk preflight** before a large export starts, refusing with a clear message instead of failing half way.
- **The default cap moving to 5 GiB**, with the peak-RSS measurements the issue asks for (256 / 300 / 500 MiB, and the 5 GiB-class run) recorded here.
- The import side's bound must follow the same decision, or the round-trip defect returns.

## Why it is not `Closes` yet

The issue's acceptance criteria run through the streaming pipeline and the 5 GiB evidence; only the export half of that exists here. `Refs` is the honest state, and it flips to `Closes #1152` in this same PR once the items above are in — not before.

## Verification so far

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `services/api` on this head.
- The streaming writer's unit cases (on the stacked #1173 branch): identical bytes to the in-memory exporter, a source opened exactly twice, an over-cap package refused before the sink receives anything.

ScienceDiscovery's issue, review and CI queues need explicit handoffs: the next actor, the missing evidence and the condition that permits progress. This proposal adds an operator-invoked development-loop skill and guide, linked from CONTRIBUTING.

## What changes

- Three queues: issue implementation, PR review, and CI/acceptance.
- Seven decision points: requirement claim, design/dependencies, implementation, source review, CI repair, real acceptance and release sign-off.
- Role-separated contributor/reviewer/maintainer TODOs, verified versus suggested ownership, release impact and recheck triggers.
- Exact-head review history, current readiness refreshes, pagination/error coverage and duplicate-request prevention.
- ScienceDiscovery's PR L1/L2, merge-group L3, daily L4 and release L5 stay distinct. Fix commits first reuse the automatic synchronize run; pending runs do not invite duplicate reruns.

Related: release tracker #249 and source-review skill proposal #231. This complements source review and does not adopt an unmerged proposal as trusted policy. Magpie is credited for unified agent/model routing and instruction-library inspiration; this is not represented as an imported upstream PR-loop skill.

## Scope and rollout

Documentation and agent instructions only. No scheduler, workflow, paid research, credentials or repository settings are installed or changed. Maintainers must separately approve deployment cadence, quotas, notifications and write actions. Keep this PR draft until the proposed handoffs and rollout choices are reviewed.

## Validation

- Skill frontmatter validator: passed.
- Relative links in new files: 11 targets verified against the pinned upstream tree and proposed files.
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed.
- Repository markdownlint configuration: 128 files checked, 0 issues.
- Repository documentation-link checker: 127 Markdown files passed.
- `node --test .ci/research-policy.test.mjs`: 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Independent read-only review: four manual scenarios checked (new head/new CI attempt, changed state before publication, incomplete screenshot evidence, PR versus merge-group gates); no blocking findings. These are reasoning checks, not an executed scheduler or production effectiveness measurement.
- Base inspected: `cc974a14468cbdfd66c76f2720ebd751aefb1cdd`.
- Full application UT/ST/E2E and live-model journeys have not been executed. No product/runtime files changed. CI policy tests establish routing invariants, not product or scientific correctness.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable to the product: this change adds contributor/agent workflow documentation with no user-observable runtime path. The eight dry-run acceptance scenarios describe checks required before future automation deployment; they do not claim that a loop has been deployed or tested end to end.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: developer-facing review and queue coordination guidance.
Compatibility and migration: none.
GitHub release label: pending verification/application.

AI assistance: Codex drafted the guidance and performed the checks listed above.

This PR addresses intermittent failures in the token onboarding journey and the artifact tool bridge without adding test randomness. It keeps artifact reads concurrent while making transient read-only bridge failures recoverable.

## Changes

- Make the zh-CN startup-token journey consume the persisted token after reload and exercise invalid-token recovery through the mounted app's hashchange path.
- Give the HTTP response-error test a single teardown owner so shutdown cannot race outstanding response-drain work.
- Retry only idempotent `read_artifact` bridge calls after transport errors or HTTP 502/503/504 responses, using bounded fixed delays; write tools are never replayed.
- Add deterministic adapter tests covering transport recovery, concurrent reads, and the no-retry rule for write operations.

## Validation

Local tests were not run during PR preparation, as requested.

Before rebasing this change set onto the upstream `main`, the existing local validation was:

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Closes #1128


## What this changes

Test-only: `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`.

`waitForRunStatus` polls **200 times at 25 ms — five seconds** (`:546`, `:557`), while one real-adapter turn measures 5.0–5.4 s in this same file (`waitForGatewayTurn`, `:455-461`, whose comment records that a 10 s budget once missed by ~460 ms). The delegated-child case has to watch a run through **three** round trips — turn 1 answers `task`, turn 2 is the child, turn 3 is the parent finishing — so it failed on the harness clock, not on the product.

That the product is fine is measured, not assumed: the same case on the same adapter passes in run `43162635488` / job `130997635702` / `group-549` (`planned 11 / executed 11 / passed 11`, `durationMs 48674`, `execution.backend = jiuwenswarm`), and the failing group `group-551` held only this one case with `providerFaults: 0`.

1. **`waitForRunStatus` gains a trailing optional `attempts = 200`.** The other 14 call sites keep failing in five seconds, which is what a genuinely hung run should do; only a case that needs several round trips asks for more.
2. **The delegated case passes `delegatedRunStatusAttempts`** — `3_600` on the swarm backend (90 s), `200` elsewhere — shaped like the `waitForGatewayTurn` budget already in the file, per the spec's first option with the conservative scope applied (the budget is opt-in rather than relaxed for every caller).
3. **`{ tags: ["swarm:required"] }` is back on that case**, so the swarm variant is covered again instead of being routed around.
4. **The comment above it is corrected.** It claimed the parent never leaves `running` under the real JiuwenSwarm instance; the passing run above refutes that, and leaving the old text would point the next reader back at the adapter.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: no error for this file that the unmodified file does not already produce in the same tree. The remaining `turnsRecorded` errors are the stale local schema missing #1119, which I verified by running the same project over the pristine `main` copy of this file — it reports the identical four errors at the shifted line numbers.
- The `swarm:required` variant needs `bash` plus a ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm instance, which this host does not have, so **CI is the executor**; I am not claiming a local run of it.

## Out of scope, stated so it is not read as an omission

**F3** — whether `closeApiServer`'s cleanup chain (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:4643-4672`) needs an overall deadline — needs a product decision and is deliberately not part of this PR, per the spec comment. The 600 s in the failing worker is teardown after the assertion failed, not a second defect demonstrated by this evidence.

Opening as a **draft**: this is not to be merged until the user says so.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Fixes #945

## What changes

`apps/desktop` carries its own copy of the feedback screenshot pipeline (the same blob web had before #942). One multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches the first 8 and the other 2 vanish: `prepareFeedbackImages` stops at `FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES` and returns only `{ images }`, while the dialog can render an unsuccessful pick (`imageError`) but not a partially successful one.

This PR counts what the cap drops and says so in both desktop dictionaries:

1. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` — `prepareFeedbackImages` returns `skipped: number`; every pick past the cap is counted (`continue` rather than `break`) so a multi-select is reported as a whole.
2. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — `skippedImages` state, rendered as one neutral `feedback-hint` beside the existing `preparing` hint when it is above zero, cleared on open, on remove, and after a successful submit.
3. `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` and `text/zh.ts` — `images.truncated: (max: number, skipped: number) => string`, function-valued like the `limit` entry beside it, with the wording #943 used for web so the two shells read the same.
4. `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — three module assertions and two mounted-dialog assertions (10 picks and 2 picks, en and zh).

## Red first

The test landed before the implementation, and the readings below are that pair — the same three cases, run with and without the change:

```
$ node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx
# before the implementation
not ok 1 - the desktop dialog counts the screenshots the eight-image cap drops
    undefined !== 2                      (also undefined !== 0 and undefined !== 1)
not ok 2 - an over-cap pick says how many screenshots were skipped, in English and Chinese
    actual: []                           (no feedback-hint for a ten-file pick)
ok     3 - a pick under the cap says nothing about skipped screenshots
# pass 1 / fail 2

# at this tip
ok 1 / ok 2 / ok 3
# pass 3 / fail 0
```

`skipped` was `undefined` before the change, so a ten-file pick could not report anything and the dialog had nothing to render. The third case passes in both states on purpose: the notice has to describe a dropped file, and a blanket banner would fail it.

## Ran / Not run

Ran:
- `apps/desktop` → `node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` — **982 tests, 0 fail** (699 subtests, 123 suites).
- `apps/desktop` → `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean.
- The red/green pair above.

Not run: `apps/web` (its own suite is untouched by this diff) and the desktop E2E journey, which needs the packaged shell.

Three macOS release-chain follow-ups from the acceptance review (issue #1165). Based on latest main (`b2075e49`); none of the 24 commits since PR #1156 touched these two files (verified by blob sha). Head is now `0ce130c3` (three stacked follow-ups on the original three changes, see commit list).

## 1. 5f gate: blockmap assertion missed electron-builder 26.x naming

The M4 clean-room signed build (`0.4.0`, builder `26.15.3`) produced a **healthy** differential-update asset, but the 5f manifest gate failed to find it:

| builder | blockmap name |
|---|---|
| 25.x | `ScienceDiscovery-…-mac-arm64.blockmap` (replaces `.zip`) |
| 26.x | `ScienceDiscovery-…-mac-arm64.zip.blockmap` (appends to full name) |

The gate asserted the 25.x name only. Fix: gate like the DMG/zip discovery — **exactly one** of the two names may exist (0 or 2 candidates fail the gate), so a stale same-version blockmap left under the other naming cannot silently ship differential data that does not match the zip (review F1):

```bash
BLOCKMAP=""
FOUND=0
for candidate in "${ZIP}.blockmap" "${ZIP%.zip}.blockmap"; do
  if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
    BLOCKMAP="$candidate"
    FOUND=$((FOUND + 1))
  fi
done
if [ "$FOUND" -eq 2 ]; then
  die "… BOTH … a stale same-version blockmap … clean release/ and rerun"
elif [ "$FOUND" -eq 0 ]; then
  die "… the differential-update data was not written; rerun electron-builder (zip target)"
fi
```

(FOUND=0 and FOUND=2 carry separate messages — review F2: the shared line told the operator to clean `release/` even when nothing stale existed.)

## 2. 5f gate: uninstaller is not a gated release asset (F4)

`application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` is the supported macOS removal path (review F4: a macOS user who wants out — or hits a broken install — has no other removal path), but the 5f manifest never gated or listed it. Now:

- gated as the **fifth** asset: `missing scripts/uninstall-mac.command` fails the gate;
- listed in the printed manifest;
- appended to the printed `gh release create` command.

(Path correction vs. the PR #1156 merge description: the script lives at `application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command`, not repo-root `scripts/`.)

## 3. `minimumSystemVersion: 14.0.0` (acceptance ⑦)

Decision basis:
- Electron 37 upstream supports the last 3 macOS majors; macOS 13 (Ventura) has fallen outside that window — no test coverage, no Gatekeeper data;
- our only real acceptance machine runs 14.8.9;
- pinning it here writes `LSMinimumSystemVersion` into Info.plist so Gatekeeper enforces the floor at install/first-run instead of documentation.

## Verification

- `bash -n application/scripts/build-mac.sh` — clean
- `js-yaml` parse of `electron-builder.yml` — `mac.minimumSystemVersion = 14.0.0`, all mac keys intact
- exactly-one probe tested on all three paths: 1 candidate hits (real 26.x artifacts, `…zip.blockmap`, 674,136 bytes), 2 candidates rejected, 0 rejected — with the split messages landing on the right branch
- remote blob shas match local `git hash-object` byte-for-byte at every push (`46cfca97`/`d5603224` → `2516b9e0` → `651eca21`)

Part of issue #1165 (items ⑦ + bot F4 + the 26.x blockmap fix found while producing the M4 release build; review F1/F2 follow-ups folded in).

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1205

A conversation created after the user has picked a model now starts from that model, **including after a restart**. Only an explicit pick writes the memory; opening an existing conversation reads its own model and never becomes the default for the next one.

## What changed

- **`state/storage.ts`**: `sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model`, next to the locale and panel-width preferences. Read at boot, written on every explicit pick, cleared when the catalog loses the model or empties.
- **`session-model-memory.ts`**: `modelForNewConversation` (the catalog check) plus `readRememberedModel` / `writeRememberedModel` over a `ReadableStorage`, so a missing or throwing storage degrades to instance-only memory instead of failing.
- **`use-workspace.ts`**:
  - the ref starts from storage, so a fresh process begins with the remembered model;
  - `selectModel` writes the pick *before* the session update, so a conversation created while that write is in flight already starts from it;
  - `createOpenSession` sends `settingsOverrides: { modelId }` instead of the top-level `modelId` shortcut: the shortcut also pins the session's `reviewModelId` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3138-3144`), while `createProjectAndOpen`'s `PATCH { modelId }` changes only the task model — both paths now change the task model only and agree;
  - a fresh draft shows the remembered model (then the project default, the global default, the first catalog model); `openSession` never writes the memory.

## Behaviour against the acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it holds |
| --- | --- |
| A new conversation defaults to the last explicitly selected model, including after a restart | the pick is stored on selection and read at boot; the captures below reload the window and the next draft already shows it |
| A later selection is used by subsequently created conversations | every explicit pick overwrites the stored value |
| Conversations with messages keep their own model; reopening does not change the memory | `openSession` only clears the one-shot draft override and displays that conversation's `modelId` |
| An unavailable remembered model does not leave a dangling selection | `modelForNewConversation` rejects an id the catalog lost, the refresh clears the stored value, and the project/global default applies |
| Relevant automated tests | see below |

## Review round 1 (head `e62925a1`)

- **Restart persistence** (zhaozhaozz and HongyeZhou, required): implemented in storage, as above — not handed to #1204 any more.
- **Review-model split** (zhaozhaozz, required): the creation path now sends `settingsOverrides.modelId`; the project path's `PATCH { modelId }` was already task-model-only. Both paths now leave `reviewModelId` alone.
- **Wiring only tested at helper level** (zhaozhaozz, required): `workspace-model-setup.test.ts` now mounts the hook against a fake client that records bodies, and asserts the create body is `{ settingsOverrides: { modelId: "second" } }` and the project path PATCHes `{ modelId: "second" }`.
- **Indentation at `use-workspace.ts:817`** (HongyeZhou, optional): fixed.

## Screenshots

Desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane), 1440×900, zh-CN and en. **Before**: a fresh window with the project default (Alpha). **After**: pick Beta in the composer's model menu, then **reload the window** — the next draft already shows Beta, read back from `sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model = model-beta`.

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before — project default | ![before, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-en-before.png) | ![before, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-zh-CN-before.png) |
| after — remembered model, after a reload | ![after, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-en-after.png) | ![after, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1205/docs/screenshots/1205/1205-zh-CN-after.png) |

The capture script read the values back from the DOM: `before="Alpha model"`, after the reload `"Beta model"`, and `localStorage["sciencediscovery-desktop:last-model"]="model-beta"` in both locales — so the Chinese captures show the dictionary's own strings, not a re-encode.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/session-model-memory.test.ts` **5/5**: the three decision cases, plus a stored pick surviving a fresh read and a missing/broken storage degrading safely.
- `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-model-setup.test.ts` **5/5**: the three existing cases, plus the create body and the project-path PATCH.
- Mutation: sending the top-level `modelId` on creation again makes the create-body case fail with the review-model reason.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean. The tagged suites were run with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored; the tags in this commit are unchanged.

## Scope

- The web client is unchanged; whether #1205 covers it is an open question for the user, not decided here.
- The memory is per browser profile, the same way the desktop keeps the locale, panel width and (#1204) the approval mode.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1218

## Why

`assemble` discovered that the JiuwenSwarm venv no longer matched the swarm patch set only inside "verifying payload imports", i.e. after the backend tree, the venv template, micromamba and the bytecode precompile had all been written — 759 s on the run the issue cites. The refusal was right, the timing was not: the same run succeeds in 835 s after `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup`, so every dependency-carrying patch cost a full payload assembly to learn about.

## What changes

**A lockfile-driven preflight at the start of `assemble`, before any payload write.** `application/scripts/lib/venv-lock-consistency.mjs` reads the *patched* `data/jiuwenswarm/src/uv.lock`, asks the jw venv once for every installed distribution (`importlib.metadata` in a single python call) and reports each package whose installed version differs from the pin. `assemble-backend.mjs` runs it right after the stale-dist gate and **before `rm(out)`/`mkdir(out)`**, so a stale venv costs seconds and leaves `build/resources` untouched.

**It is generic, not greenlet-specific.** 0018-desktop-slim-deps, 0019-align-workspace-versions and 0021-greenlet-static-runtime all rewrite `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`; whatever a future patch pins is checked without touching this code. Packages the lock lists for other platforms or optional groups are ignored when the venv does not install them — the direction this exists for is an installed package lagging its patched pin.

**The end-of-run gate stays.** The greenlet MSVC140/native-import gate is untouched and still runs as the second line of defence (a venv can, in principle, change mid-run).

The refusal names both versions and the same repair command the end gate uses:

```
[assemble] FAIL: jw venv preflight FAILED: the venv does not match the swarm patch set:
pip 25.0.1 (uv.lock requires 0.0.1). A dependency-carrying patch rewrote the lockfile but
the venv predates it. Re-run node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup (or bash scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup), then rebuild.
```

## Proof that the refusal happens before the payload is written

A real `assemble` run against a fixture whose lock pins `pip` differently from its venv (the same shape as greenlet 3.5.0 vs 3.5.5):

```
[assemble] sanity checks passed
[assemble] stale-dist gate passed (services/packages/apps)
[assemble] FAIL: jw venv preflight FAILED: ... pip 25.0.1 (uv.lock requires 0.0.1) ...
exit=1  elapsed=516 ms  out exists: False
```

- **516 ms**, against the 759 s the issue measured for the same discovery at the end gate.
- **`--out` was never created**: the preflight runs before `rm(out)`/`mkdir(out)`, so there is no payload to leave half-written. The check is asserted by a test as well (`the preflight runs before assemble writes anything`) so a future edit cannot move it back below the copy steps.
- With a lock that matches its venv, the same fixture prints `jw venv matches the swarm patch set's uv.lock` and proceeds to the deploy step — the check does not fire on a correct tree.

## Tests

- `application/test/assemble-venv-preflight.test.ts` (new): parses `[[package]]` pins; reports a stale installed version and not the pin; ignores a locked package the venv does not install; no refusal when they agree; the message names both versions and both setup commands; the skew list is bounded; and the ordering pin above.
- `pnpm --dir application test`: **352 tests, 348 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped** (the skips are the Windows-inapplicable macOS cases).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm ci:l1` could not run on this host: the tagged runner spawns `pnpm` without a shell and this machine only has a `pnpm.cmd` shim (spawn ENOENT). CI runs the same gate; the local suite and typecheck above are the local evidence.

No behaviour change for a correct tree: the preflight only reads a lockfile and asks the venv for its versions.
recent_merged.head: fix-1218-venv-preflight
recent_merged.title: fix(application): refuse a stale JiuwenSwarm venv before the payload is written

Closes #1204

## What changes

**The composer shows the permission mode and lets it be changed there.** The mode existed only behind the composer's settings menu, so what the next turn would run under was invisible until that menu was opened; the composer footer now carries a compact selector after the + and settings buttons:

- closed, it is the shield plus the mode's own word — `请求批准` with a check mark, `完全访问` with an exclamation mark and in the warning colour the flyout row already uses;
- with no session open it names what a conversation created now would run under: the project's `defaultApprovalMode`, else the global one, else `请求批准`. A default of full access is therefore shown as 完全访问 rather than 请求批准, and there is no third "follow settings" state (#1204 owner decision; the neutral label from the previous head was replaced by reading the effective default, the reviews' other allowed fix);
- open, it is the same two-row scope flyout the settings menu shows, so the scope descriptions live in one place rather than being copied;
- below 640 px it keeps the shield and drops the word: the footer is 270 px at 390 px, and a labelled third control pushed the send button outside it (the desktop-configuration journey measures exactly that), so the narrow composer uses the icon-only form the flyout still explains;
- it is disabled while a run is active, for the same reason the settings row is;
- the settings row keeps its choice: this adds a visible door, it does not remove the existing one.

**A new conversation starts in the last mode the reader selected, and that survives a restart.** `apps/desktop/src/app/approval-mode-preference.ts` keeps the choice in desktop storage under a namespaced key (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), next to the panel-width and locale preferences. It is read on creation, and a stored value that is not one of the two modes is treated as no choice at all. Consequences:

- conversations that already exist are never updated by it — nothing here writes to them, and reopening one only displays its own mode;
- the choice travels only in creation-time values: `CreateSessionRequest.approvalMode` for the normal path, and one best-effort `updateSession(approvalMode)` for the two paths whose conversation the service creates on its own — a new project's first conversation and an untouched draft reused by 新增会话. A failed inheritance write there never hides the conversation;
- with nothing stored, the request carries no `approvalMode` and the service default applies exactly as before.

No API change was needed: `CreateSessionRequest` already accepts `approvalMode` and the server route honours it. Permission enforcement is untouched.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/approval-mode-preference.test.ts`: 3 cases — a fresh call after `rememberApprovalMode` carries the mode (this is what a restart looks like, because the module keeps no state of its own); a stored value that is not a mode is ignored; `inheritForSession` applies the remembered mode to a conversation created by another path and makes no request when nothing is remembered.
- `apps/desktop/tests/composer.test.tsx`: 30 cases, three covering this change — the selector's position after the + and settings buttons with the asking label and check, the full-access warning colour and label, and the popover's two scope explanations with the callback receiving `ask_for_dangerous` when that row is chosen.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and the root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean. `pnpm ci:l1` and the rest of the gate are CI's evidence.

## Verification of the restart requirement

This was the one acceptance criterion the first head missed, so it is stated explicitly: the choice is written to `localStorage` on every selection (`sciencediscovery-desktop:approval-mode`), and the capture run below read it back after selecting full access (`stored: "always_allow"`). A fresh module instance reads it through `readStoredText`, which is what a new application process does; the unit test uses a storage stub to exercise exactly that read.

## Screenshots

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (composer, no selector) | ![before, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-before.png) | ![before, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-before.png) |
| closed, 请求批准 (shield + check) | ![ask, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-ask.png) | ![ask, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-ask.png) |
| closed, 完全访问 (warning colour) | ![full, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-full.png) | ![full, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-full.png) |
| open flyout, both scope explanations | ![flyout, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-flyout.png) | ![flyout, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-zh-flyout.png) |
| narrow (390 px), icon-only | ![narrow, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1204/docs/screenshots/1204/1204-en-narrow.png) | — |

Captured from the running desktop shell (vite dev + the repository's `e2e/fixtures` control plane), zh and en, 1440×900, on this head. The text was checked programmatically, not by eye: the DOM read back `请求批准` / `完全访问` and both scope explanations exactly, so the Chinese in these captures is the dictionary's own string rather than a re-encoded one — the #1148 failure was a transcoding bug and there is none here. The capture script also asserted the classes (`is-danger` only for full access) and that selecting full access stored `always_allow`.

The 会话设置 row for 程序演进实验 reused a search whenever the Session already had one. After the
first run it could never reach the create dialog again, so the preflight advice "start again from
the setup dialog" pointed at a surface the UI would not show, and a second search could only be
started by typing an `/evolve-design` command.

The same Session also showed a second, independent problem when the continuation was written as a
plain message ("基于Node #2，继续进化"): the model omitted `allowUnisolated`, because that message
carries no `--allow-direct`. The server does not read the current message: it reads the Session's
**latest** `/evolve-design` command, which did carry the flag, so the run was refused by the
model's reading of the rule, not by the server.

## The settings row always starts a design
`openEvolve` in `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` now always opens 新建程序演进实验 instead of selecting a
running/newest search. Existing searches stay reachable through their cards in the transcript, and
the composer's draft still rides into the new design's task field. The Composer prop comment follows
the behaviour.

A search that is **still running** holds the form rather than disappearing from it: the server
starts one search per Session (`startProposedRun` refuses a second with "this session already has a
search running"), so the dialog now takes the same `isEvolveRunActive` over `evolve.runs` the panel
uses, and `blocked` names it — the form opens, says a search is running and where its card is, and
leaves 开始设计 disabled. A finished search leaves the form usable, which is the state this change
is about. The new cases in `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` cover both: a finished search still
gets a usable dialog from the settings row, and a running one still opens the dialog but cannot
start a second search.

## Consent for a continuation started from a plain message
`skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md` and the `allowUnisolated` description in `packages/evolve/src/index.ts`
now scope the consent to the design being continued: what it inherits is the `/evolve-design`
command that started that design, read together with the design it started. That is the Session's
latest command only when the continued design is the newest one — with two designs, the latest
command can belong to the other one — so when that cannot be told the flag is left out and the
server refuses with `unisolated_run_unconfirmed`, telling the user to start the run from the setup
dialog. A checkpoint answer does not replace the command, a plain message is not itself an answer,
and a design that begins from one has no command of its own, so it must not inherit another
design's `--allow-direct`.

## Validation
On this head (`fix/desktop-evolve-second-run` rebased onto `e0983db4`):

- Typecheck: desktop and evolve packages pass.
- Desktop unit tests: 1176/1176 pass (0 failed, 0 skipped).
- Evolve unit tests: 16/16 pass (0 failed, 0 skipped).
- Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`, mocked entry): 154 tests, 150 passed, 4 failed.
  The four also fail on the base commit (`b3ec144e`, the previous main) in a detached worktree with the same
  command, in files this diff does not touch: `boot` "resumes the most recent session", both
  `research-package` cases, and `settings-interactions` "a card opens to the skill's source".
- The repository-wide UT and ST layers were last run on the previous head before the rebase; the
  only packages this head changes are the two above, and both were rerun. That earlier run:
  UT 7707 planned / 7676 executed / 7660 passed / 16 failed, all 16 attributed to this host (14
  pass under a clean `TMPDIR`; the remaining 2 also fail on a pristine `main` worktree in files this
  diff does not touch — bwrap 0.6.1 lacks `--disable-userns`, and `start-stack-lock` cannot
  reproduce its interrupt). ST 63 planned / 63 executed / 62 passed / 1 failed:
  `test/api/evolve-distribution` downloads the pinned Python runtime from GitHub Releases, which
  this host cannot reach.

## Screenshots
Captured from the mocked desktop entry, on a Session whose `session-1` already has a search,
clicking 会话设置 → 程序演进实验.

The "before" pair is the same head with `App.tsx` taken from the base, so the only difference
between the pairs is this change.

<details open>
<summary>zh-CN — before / after (finished search)</summary>

Before: the row opens the existing search's 任务 panel.

![zh before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/zh-before-run.png)

After: the row opens 新建程序演进实验.

![zh after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/zh-after-dialog.png)

</details>

<details open>
<summary>en-US — before / after (finished search)</summary>

Before: the row opens the existing search's task panel.

![en before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/en-before-run.png)

After: the row opens New evolution run.

![en after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/4a960e901a84a21dbb73f07cbf0f68c838759166/pr-assets/1212/en-after-dialog.png)

</details>

<details open>
<summary>zh-CN / en-US — a search still running</summary>

The same row with a live search: the dialog opens, names the search and disables 开始设计 / Start
designing.

![zh blocked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/d062580abad4534b150a5caa514776f167b00d76/pr-assets/1212/zh-blocked-running.png)

![en blocked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/d062580abad4534b150a5caa514776f167b00d76/pr-assets/1212/en-blocked-running.png)

</details>

## E2E user journeys
The change is observed on the desktop browser entry. The repository-wide mocked journeys were
not rerun on this head: nothing in them reaches the settings row or the create dialog, and the
server-side consent check is unchanged.

- `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` — 16/16 passed, including "the settings row starts a new design
  when the session's search has finished" and "the settings row still opens the create dialog while
  a search runs, and says why it cannot start".
- Full desktop suite — 154 tests, 150 passed, 4 failed, all four pre-existing on the base (above).
- No API, CLI or local-stack journey exercises this surface: the change is the desktop dialog's
  entry and its blocked copy. The server-side consent check it describes is unchanged.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: the 程序演进实验 row in 会话设置 now always opens the create dialog, so a second
experiment can be started from the UI without typing a command; while a search is live the dialog
says so instead of offering a start the server would refuse; and a continuation started from a
plain message can carry the no-isolation consent the user already gave.
Compatibility and migration: none.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1152

Stage 2 of the issue: the pipeline no longer materialises an archive on either side, the default cap moves to 5 GiB, and both sides check the machine before starting rather than failing halfway.

## What changed

**Export.** `writeResearchPackage` writes tar → gzip → the task's own file; the background export hands it a destination, so there is no whole-archive buffer, and a cancelled or failed task deletes a partial file instead of discarding one. Objects are handed over as sources — a CAS stream, or a workspace file read twice — so the payload is not all resident.

**Import.** `importResearchPackageStreamed` takes the compressed bytes as they arrive, gunzips incrementally, parses the tar sequentially and writes each object to `objectDirectory/<sha256>` while hashing it, so a digest is verified against its address before the object can be used. Manifest, records and readme are the only resident entries; the object map is backed by that directory and reads one object at a time.

**HTTP.** `POST .../research-package/inspect` and `.../import` stream the upload to `<data dir>/research-package-uploads/<purpose>-XXXX/package.sdresearch` and parse it from there. The inspection cache now owns that directory instead of a `Buffer`; a cached import deletes it only after the restore has copied the archive into its snapshot, and a read-only restore uses `copyFile(..., COPYFILE_EXCL)` instead of rewriting bytes.

**Preflight.** Each side is charged only what it writes: an export against the preview's `archiveBytes` (one compressed file, the uncompressed estimate being an upper bound); an upload against `content-length` (the staged file); a streamed parse against `min(ceiling, free disk / 3)`, which reserves the two copies a later restore adds; a restore against `2 × unpacked + records` on disk (snapshot objects and CAS blobs — the unpacked upload is already there) and `max(largest object, records) + 256 MiB` in memory. `inspect` charges nothing after its parse, because it writes nothing more. Memory is measured on `MemAvailable` so reclaimable page cache counts. Insufficient capacity is refused with HTTP 507 and `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` / `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY`, naming what is missing.

**Cap.** Default 5 GiB, ceiling `8 GiB - 1` — the largest value an 11-digit octal tar header field can express, so the existing header writer stays valid; a single entry beyond it is refused instead of producing a broken header. The upload bound stays derived from the ceiling, as #1173 left it.

## Measurements

Incompressible payload, one object, this host (Windows, 15.7 GiB RAM), `--max-old-space-size=3072`, one process per mode, `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` after each step:

| payload | archive | export peak — before (whole archive) | export peak — streaming | import peak — before | import peak — streaming |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256 MiB | 256.1 MiB | 1082 MiB | 141 MiB | 1164 MiB | 152 MiB |
| 300 MiB | 300.1 MiB | 1260 MiB | 139 MiB | 1300 MiB | 145 MiB |
| 500 MiB | 500.2 MiB | 2066 MiB | 139 MiB | 2101 MiB | 179 MiB |
| 5100 MiB (5 GiB class) | 5101.6 MiB | not run — needs ~15 GiB resident | 155 MiB | not run | 459 MiB |

The "before" column reproduces the numbers the issue measured (1071 / 1248 / 2056 MiB at 256 / 300 / 500 MiB). Times on the same runs, 256 / 300 / 500 MiB: export 11 / 15.6 / 29.4 s before and 10.6 / 15.2 / 28.5 s streaming; import 0.9 / 1.1 / 3.0 s before and 1.9 / 4.9 / 6.2 s streaming — the streamed import writes each object to disk and copies it. The 5 GiB-class round trip exported in 269 s and imported in 81 s at 155 MiB / 459 MiB peak, on a host whose `--max-old-space-size` is the API default.

## Tests

- `packages/research-package/src/index.test.ts` 16/16 and `stream-import.test.ts` 4/4: the streamed import matches the in-memory import on records, inventory and package checksum; a flipped payload byte fails the per-object digest check; a truncated archive and an over-cap archive are refused.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` 23/23, `research-package-exports.test.ts` 9/9 (including a failed streamed write leaving no partial archive), `conversation-branches.test.ts` 6/6, `research-package-overcap-roundtrip.test.ts` 1/1, `research-package-preflight.test.ts` 5/5.
- The tagged suites were run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run and restored before pushing; the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutations: dropping the per-object digest check fails the tampered-payload case; removing the preflight refusal fails both refusal cases; removing the partial-file cleanup fails the write-failure case.
- `tsc -p services/api`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and the package build are clean.

## Limits worth knowing

- A workspace file is read three times: once to name the object, once by the writer's hash pass, once by the tar pass. A CAS object is read twice. Turning the hash pass off would need the caller's checksum to be trusted; this PR does not trust it.
- The streamed import is slower per byte than the buffered one (see the times above) because each object is written to disk and then copied; that is the trade for bounded memory.
- Old packages are unaffected: the format is unchanged and an import still accepts the hard ceiling.
- No user-visible copy changed in this PR: the stage-1 limit line and over-cap confirmation are #1173, already merged. The two preflight refusals surface through the existing task error, with their message naming the missing capacity.
- The measurements above are of the package library round trip. The API restore reads one object at a time rather than materialising the package; its footprint is the largest single object plus records, which the post-parse preflight enforces.

A refusal caused by the measured free-disk budget answers HTTP 507 with `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK` and the disk copy; an overrun of the absolute ceiling stays its own client-input error.

Follow-up to #1194 (#1182 and #1187 both closed by it): the three suggestions that were deliberately not pushed onto the approved head.

## What changes

**F1 — the read-only fixture is judged by its own write (`application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`).**
`hostMadeReadOnly` had its `writeFile` and its conditional `rm` inside one `try`, so a failed unlink of a file the host had just created was classified as "read-only". Only the write decides now; the unlink is best effort. It failed loudly rather than passing silently, but the classification was wrong.

**F3 — the writable half runs before the skip (same file).**
`assert.equal(await dirWritable(join(root, "rw")), true)` had moved below the NTFS probe, so on the one platform this suite runs on, a regression that made `dirWritable` answer `false` for a writable directory would have been reported as `# skipped`. It is asserted before the probe again, and only the read-only assertion sits below the skip.

**F2 — the build-only flag is pinned in the contract (`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`).**
`/pnpm --dir application dist/` matches with or without `--publish never`, so the publish half of the Windows gate had no contract check while the split half did. The contract now asserts the flag, so a later edit cannot restore electron-builder's implicit publish (the #1187 failure) while the test stays green.

## Validation

On this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files pushed:

- `application/test/bootstrap.test.ts`: **34 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped** — the same two NTFS skips, with the writable assertion now before the probe.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` passes, including the new `--publish never` assertion (run with that file's `os:linux` tag released for this host; the other failures in the file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are untouched here).
- Root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` is clean for these files through CI's gate.

This is test-only; no product or workflow behaviour changes.
