recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1182

Closes #1187

## Why

`pnpm --dir application test` is the gate in front of `pnpm --dir application dist`, the command that produces the NSIS installer. Four of its assertions asked for POSIX capabilities a stock Windows host does not have, so the gate was red for environment reasons — and because the CI step ran `test` and `typecheck` in one pwsh block, a failing suite was recorded as a green step. The same Windows job then failed one step later on electron-builder's implicit GitHub publish.

Both issues describe the same job from different ends: #1182 the four host-dependent assertions, #1187 the publish attempt and the masked step. This PR fixes all three paths together, because fixing any one alone leaves the gate lying about the other two.

## What changes

**The four assertions now gate on the capability they need, not on a platform guess** (`application/test`):

- `bootstrap.test.ts` — `dirWritable` and the `bootstrapPackaged` W16 case. After the `chmod(0o555)` fixture the test judges the fixture with a **write probe of its own** (`hostMadeReadOnly`), not by asking `dirWritable`; the skip happens only when that write succeeds (NTFS: `chmod` only toggles the read-only attribute), and the DMG degradation path keeps its coverage on hosts where the fixture is meaningful. Judging the fixture with the function under test would have made the assertion circular — a `dirWritable` that over-reported writability would have skipped the test instead of failing it — so the probe writes and the assertions below it stay falsifiable.
- `uninstall-data.test.ts` — the `bash -n` check is skipped when `/bin/bash` is absent, stating that the macOS 3.2 syntax check runs where that shell exists. It is the capability the assertion needs.
- `venv-launchers.test.ts` — only the `replaceVenvSymlinks` case is gated, on `process.platform === "win32"`: that block models a *darwin* venv (`replaceVenvSymlinks` is reached only from the darwin assembly and bootstrap paths). Without Developer Mode the fixture raises `EPERM`; on the elevated CI runner the link is created but `readlink` answers in the Windows dialect, so the relative-target comparison fails for a reason that is not the code. Here the platform gate **is** the capability gate — a POSIX filesystem that stores symlink targets as POSIX paths — rather than a guess: the fixture cannot describe a Windows venv at all. The trampoline, DLL and regular-file cases keep running on win32.

Four tests skip with a named reason; nothing is deleted, and no product code is touched.

**The CI step stops masking its suite, and the build stops publishing** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

```yaml
      - name: Test the desktop shell
        run: pnpm --dir application test

      - name: Typecheck the desktop shell
        run: pnpm --dir application typecheck

      - name: Build the Windows installer
        run: pnpm --dir application dist --publish never
```

The two commands are separate steps, so the suite's exit code is the step's result. `--publish never` keeps this gate build-only: `electron-builder` treats CI detection plus the configured `github` publish provider as "upload now", and this job has no token to upload with. Publishing stays manual, as `electron-builder.yml` already documents, and `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` asserts `/pnpm --dir application dist/`, which the new line still matches.

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` also pins the split now — one step named `Test the desktop shell` running the suite, one `Typecheck the desktop shell`, and no `Test and typecheck the desktop shell` — so folding them back into one pwsh block fails the contract test instead of silently re-blinding the gate.

## Two premises in #1182 corrected

- **The cited CI job did not pass the suite.** In job `133716724096` (head `5058334f`) step 16 is recorded `success` while its TAP tail is `# tests 343 / # pass 339 / # fail 4` with the same four `not ok` lines, because pwsh keeps the last command's exit code. The four failures were red in CI too, unnoticed.
- **The cited job did not fail on this gate.** It failed at step 17 with `Error: GitHub Personal Access Token is not set …` from `GitHubPublisher`, after the NSIS build succeeded and the artifact was uploaded. #1187 carries that half of the story and this PR closes it with `--publish never`.

## Validation

Run on this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files this PR pushes:

- `pnpm --dir application test`: **343 tests, 339 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped** (`# skipped 4`, exit 0). The skips are the four reported ids, each with its reason: `27`/`28` `host chmod cannot make a directory unwritable (NTFS)`, `248` `no /bin/bash on this host…`, `288` `models a darwin venv; POSIX symlink targets only exist on POSIX hosts`.
- Before the change the same command on this host was `339 pass / 4 fail`, matching the report.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (the `typecheck` step): exit 0.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: the `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` assertion passes, including the new three pins on the split step (run locally with that file's `os:linux` tag released; the other failures in that file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are not touched here).
- The read-only fixture is falsifiable again: with `hostMadeReadOnly` mutated to answer "read-only" without writing, `dirWritable answers true for a writable dir and false for a read-only one` fails with `expected: false, actual: true` instead of skipping (checked, then restored).
- pnpm argument forwarding checked with pnpm 11.1.2: `pnpm <script> --publish never` appends the two arguments to the end of the script command, so `electron-builder --win` receives them (a `run` + `--` form would insert an extra `--`, which is why the shorthand is used).

## Scope

## Changes

Fix two failures in the Windows installer: a simple greeting can fail while loading `_greenlet` on machines without the VC++ x64 runtime, and the default scientific-environment layout can prevent managed Bash from becoming available before any command is dispatched.

- Use compact internal environment/revision directory names while retaining full public IDs, collision checks, existing prefixes and the pre-provisioning path-budget guard. The reported default layout drops from 283 to 235 characters against the 259-character budget.
- Pin the patched JiuwenSwarm dependency/lock to greenlet 3.5.5, which restores the static C++ runtime. Payload assembly exercises native greenlet execution and checks the version and DLL-name references, so the build machine's installed runtime cannot hide this dependency.
- Project `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` Shell results without repeated capability snapshots or escaped multiline diagnostics. Retain complete tool details, the recovery operation ID and independent Python/Shell readiness.

Existing Conda prefixes are never relocated. Previously created overdeep prefixes can still require rebuilding; new compact prefixes are used on all platforms. The greenlet fix requires a newly built payload rather than changing an already installed old payload.

## Verification

Candidate tree tested on Linux x86_64. These targeted checks were run before commit; the reviewed candidate tree is committed as head `3b051b4a84f27cbb1319450b652c281f037ffff6`.

- Runner environment paths/store: **42 passed, 0 failed** (fake provisioner; Windows paths simulated on Linux).
- Desktop launcher/dependency helpers: **11 passed, 0 failed** (synthetic native-extension fixtures).
- Blocked Shell projection and existing Shell diagnostics: **12 passed, 0 failed** (mocked tool callbacks).
- Runner/workspace typechecks, changed MJS syntax checks, final SDK patch application check, and complete diff whitespace check passed. The patched SDK lock also passed `uv lock --check` in an isolated replica without installing dependencies.
- Application package typecheck passed.

Closes #1183

## What this changes

The session header had an Export button at its upper right (#1171, added for #1154) while the session's sidebar menu already offers the same action. Both opened the same package dialog, so the header carried a permanent second entry for one action — what the report asks to remove.

- **`SessionBar`** loses the button and its `onExport` prop. The panel toggle is the bar's only action again, which is what the component's own doc comment already said ("the one control that acts on the panel"); that sentence was no longer true after #1171.
- **`App`** stops passing the prop. The sidebar's `onExportSession` is untouched: it opens the same `ResearchPackage` dialog, and the export history lives inside that dialog (`ExportHistoryList`, rendered when the shell bridge is present), so nothing about the export flow or its history becomes unreachable.
- **`sessionBar.export`** copy is removed from both locales — nothing else referenced it.
- **`session-bar.test.tsx`** gains a case that pins the absence: no `task-head-export`, no export label, and exactly one button in the bar when the panel is closed. A future re-add fails a test instead of returning silently.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `apps/desktop` and for the root `tsconfig.tests.json` (the project that actually type-checks test files).
- `apps/desktop/tests/session-bar.test.tsx`: **7/7** through the suite's own loader (`--import tsx --import ./tests/support/css-preload.mjs`), including the new case.

## Still owed

This is a `UI` change, so it needs a rendered before/after of the session header — the button present versus gone, with the sidebar's export entry visible in both — and that pair needs the user's own eyes. I have not claimed otherwise here.

## Note on overlap

This touches `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` and `zh.ts`, which the open #1173 also touches (it adds keys there). The edits are in different blocks (`sessionBar` versus `researchPackage`), so a merge should be clean, but whoever lands second rebases onto the other.

Captured from the PR's own trees — **before** at `e727e750` (current `main`), **after** at this head `2ff0799c` — with the desktop app served by vite and the API mocked through `apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures`, in a 1440×900 Edge window. recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Refs #1152 — this is **stage 1** of the issue's own two-stage plan. The cap becomes one visible, enforced value; the streaming pass that lets the default move to 5 GiB is stage 2 and stays tracked in #1152.

## What changes

**One cap, one place.** `packages/research-package/src/index.ts` had `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024` and `services/api/src/http/index.ts` had a second, independent `256 * 1024 * 1024` upload bound. That pair is the round-trip defect: incompressible content makes an archive ≈ its payload, so a 300 MiB export produced a package its own importer refused. Now:

- `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` is the single value, exported and consumed by the export refusal, the import inflation bound, and the upload bound.
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` overrides it, clamped between 64 MiB and 16 GiB, following the `SCIENCE_AGENT_API_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` precedent: a malformed or out-of-range value falls back to the default rather than either being ignored or letting one typo turn a clean refusal into an out-of-memory crash. **The default is still 512 MiB in this PR** — it moves to 5 GiB in stage 2, which is the only point at which the streaming pipeline makes it safe.
- The upload bound is derived from the cap (+5% and 1 MiB of slack for an incompressible gzip frame), and the inspection cache bound is derived from both views of one package (compressed + unpacked), so a valid inspect no longer hands the dialog a checksum the import cannot reuse — which used to make the client upload the whole archive twice.

**Refuse before packaging.** `prepareResearchPackage` charged the tar-block arithmetic, but the dialog could only see `estimateResearchPackageBytes`, which pads the manifest as `1024 + 256 * objects` and differs from the real archive in both directions (one 32 MiB object: 32.005 vs 32.011 MiB; 500 small objects: 901,632 vs 870,400 B). A dialog gating on that number can let a near-cap selection through and still get the late refusal. Added `researchPackageArchiveBytes`, which computes the exact tar size without hashing or compressing — hashes and object paths have a fixed width, so a manifest built from placeholders is byte-for-byte the same length as the real one, and the unit test asserts equality against `gunzipSync(export).byteLength` rather than against a second estimate.

**Server-side enforcement, not just the dialog.** A synchronous export is refused with `413 RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` right after the input is built and before any tar exists. The background task keeps its own late refusal (its revision can change mid-flight). The upload path answers the same stable code; the raw byte count is gone from the message.

**Both dialogs.** The preview response gains `maxBytes` and `archiveBytes` (additive; a client that ignores them keeps the old behaviour). Both export dialogs now:

- render the limit next to the estimate;
- over the limit, show the size against the limit, suggest the necessary export, and state the risk in plain words (long read, memory pressure);
- when `necessary` is already the selected profile, say that no smaller scope exists instead of offering one;
- keep both export actions disabled until `Export anyway` is pressed — the second confirmation the issue asks for;
- show localized copy for `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` instead of the server's English prose.

The acknowledgement is keyed by revision + size, so any new selection asks again. Every new string exists in zh-CN and en, in both dictionaries (`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` + `zh.ts`).

## What this does not do

- **The 5 GiB default, and the peak-RSS evidence for it.** The exporter still reads every object into memory, builds one tar buffer and gzips it; the importer still inflates the whole archive. Peak RSS is ≈3× payload, so 5 GiB is ≈15 GiB — raising the constant today would convert a clean refusal into an OOM, which the issue itself predicts. That is stage 2: stream tar → gzip → file, stream gunzip → temp file with per-object verification, preflight memory and disk, then raise the default.
- **A round-trip test whose compressed size exceeds 256 MiB.** It needs stage 2's temp-file import to be meaningful, and this machine cannot allocate it (15.7 GB total, 4.8 GB free). It belongs to stage 2's PR with the RSS harness.
- **The per-file tar field caveat** (`MAX_FILE_BYTES = 32 GiB` against a 12-byte octal size field, ~8 GiB usable): unreachable while the total cap is ≤5 GiB, so it is left for whoever raises the per-object bound.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/research-package`, `services/api`, `apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, and the root `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- `packages/research-package` unit tests: **13/13** locally, including the new ones —
  - the archive-size helper equals the real uncompressed tar, and the cap refuses at `predicted - 1` while accepting `predicted` (the ±1 byte boundary from the test plan);
  - the environment override clamps: empty/malformed → default, `1` → min, 999 GiB → max.
- The API suite (`research-package-http.test.ts`) now also asserts `maxBytes`, `archiveBytes` and `archiveBytes <= maxBytes` for every level/trajectory/memory combination. It is tagged for the shared plan, so its runtime result comes from CI, not from this machine.
- The dialogs were type-checked, not yet seen rendered: `UI` review and the rendered proof belong with the user's confirmation, and I have not claimed otherwise.

## Not covered by this PR, for the reviewers' decision

- `#1024` also owns a dialog limit line and proposes `archiveLimitBytes` as the field name. This PR uses `maxBytes` as #1152 defines it; if #1024 should own that surface, the field is additive and can be renamed before anything depends on it.

## Rendered evidence for the limit surface

Captures of the export dialog in the three states this change adds. They are
renderer-level: the dialog's markup with the repository's own `tokens.css` / `base.css` /
`primitives.css` / `dialogs.css` and the real `messages.ts` strings, rendered in Chromium.
They are not Electron-window captures and not a live interaction — the size and the
over-limit condition are the values the component receives.

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| under the cap (limit line only) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-under.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-under.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-under.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-under.png) |
| over the cap (warning + `Export anyway`) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-over.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-over.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-over.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-over.png) |
| after confirming (actions enabled) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-confirmed.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-confirmed.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-confirmed.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-confirmed.png) |

What the three states show: the limit line renders `512 MiB` rather than a raw byte count;
the over-cap state names the selection's size against the limit, offers the necessary
export, states the memory/latency risk in plain words, and keeps both export actions
disabled until `Export anyway` is pressed; the confirmed state shows the acknowledgement
and enables the actions.

Checked without looking at the images, since I cannot view them: the pages carry the
exact `messages.ts` strings with **0** latin-1 mojibake runs (the failure that broke an
earlier screenshot set), and the Chinese renders use a named CJK fallback rather than the
browser's implicit one.

**One limit, stated plainly:** this is a programmatic check of the strings and styles, not
an eye check. Whether the wording and layout are acceptable is the user's and the
reviewers' call.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1190

A conversation branch keeps the candidate entries of the searches it carries, but not their source objects. The branch package then imports with `evolve:<run>:<hash>:missing candidate source object`: the candidate tree stays empty, `/api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>` has nothing to serve, and `get_evolve_run` loses `bestSource` — the same class of loss #1176 removed for plain imports.

## Why it happens

`buildConversationBranch` rebuilds the `needed` object set from workspace `objectPath`s, artifact-version `objectPath`s, `casHashes(records)` and `versionObjects`. `casHashes` collects a nested `hash` only when a sibling `size` is a number, and a candidate entry is `{ hash, objectPath, runId }` with no `size`. The top-level export lists those objects explicitly; the branch did not, and `prepareResearchPackage` does not cross-check records against objects, so the export succeeded and the loss surfaced only at import.

## What changed

- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.ts`: the kept candidates' `objectPath`s join the retained object set, so a kept entry always travels with its source, while a search the branch drops still brings neither its entries nor its objects.
- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts`: the fixture now carries real candidate objects, and the branch case asserts that the kept search's object survives and the dropped search's object does not.

## Validation

- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts` passes 6/6 with this change, run on this machine with the `os:linux` tag released and restored before pushing — the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutation: removing the line that adds the candidate objects makes the new case fail with `the kept search keeps its candidate source object` (expected `true`, actual `false`); the line was restored afterwards.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are both clean.
- The `os:linux` variant and the rest of UT / merge-gate run on CI.

Relates to #1176, whose review raised this as F4 after the merge.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Imported Evolve searches disappear when their run ID already exists in the destination, including when a read-only import is copied into a writable research session. Restore conflicting runs with new IDs and use the mapping for their candidate sources, preserving the event log, budget, and best node.

## What changed

- `restoreEvolveRuns` returns the source→restored run mapping; a colliding run is recreated under a fresh id with its event log, goal, status, budget and best node.
- Candidate sources are written under the restored id, so a run in the destination can still serve its source code.
- A run's result artifact now carries the restored id: the `evolve/<run>/` prefix of its name/logicalName/sourcePath and `originMeta.evolveRunId` are rewritten through the mapping, so `get_evolve_run` names an artifact this session actually has. The copy-integrity check compares the expected side through the same mapping.
- `buildConversationBranch` trims the evolve payload with the branch cutoff: only runs that finished at or before the selected reply travel, and only their candidate sources — a branch no longer lists a search from a turn it excludes.


## Validation

- **`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean**, which is the `check:typecheck` slice of `UT` that this branch failed on.
- **`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`: 21/21** (the import, repeated-import, continuation-copy, candidate-source, event-replay and artifact assertions), and **`conversation-branches.test.ts`: 6/6** including the new cutoff case, both run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the duration and restored before pushing.
- **`evolution/package.test.ts` 16/16 and `research-snapshot-integrity.test.ts` 4/4** on the same basis; `services/api` and the root tests typecheck are clean.
- CI runs `UT`, `ST`, `L1`, `Coverage` and `merge-gate` on this head; the ST and mocked E2E results are the CI's, not claimed here.

## E2E user journey

The desktop journey (import → continue → open the Evolve card and task panel) was **not executed on this host**: it needs the real shell plus a full stack, which is not available here. What covers the same data path instead:

- the API regression test above drives import → writable continuation → restored runs, their event log, candidate source and result artifact;
- **no capture covers the rendering**: the desktop Evolve card and task panel drawn from `GET /api/evolve/runs` and `/events` were not exercised for a restored run, and #1171 (merged) captured the export dialog's history list, not this surface — it is not evidence for it.

The UI itself is unchanged in this PR, so no new screenshot is offered; if the journey is required as a merge condition, say so and I will say plainly that it cannot be produced on this machine rather than claim it.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: imported Evolve runs can appear in each restored session instead of being skipped on ID collision.
Compatibility and migration: packages created before Evolve data was included cannot recover omitted data and must be exported again from the source.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Starting a new conversation should not require selecting the same model again. Related: #462 requests remembered model selection, including persistence across restarts; this request tracks the same behavior alongside #1204.

### Design Ideas

Initialize each newly created conversation with the last model explicitly selected by the user, including after an application restart. A later selection becomes the default for subsequent new conversations. Existing conversations that already have messages keep their own model selection; reopening one must not change it or count as a new selection. Persist the last selection across application restarts.

### Involved Public APIs

Determine whether API changes are needed; preserve existing model selection and execution behavior for existing conversations.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Conversation model picker, new-session initialization, model configuration and session settings. Coordinate the inheritance behavior with permission-mode request #1204.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Select model B, create a conversation and verify B is selected; restart the application and verify another new conversation still uses B. Select C and verify the next new conversation uses C. Reopen an existing conversation with messages and verify its own model remains unchanged. Verify behavior when the remembered model is no longer available and that the displayed model matches the effective selection.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new conversation defaults to the last explicitly selected model including after an application restart.
- [ ] A later model selection is used by subsequently created conversations.
- [ ] Conversations that already have messages retain their own model; reopening one does not change the remembered selection.
- [ ] An unavailable remembered model does not leave a dangling selection; use a valid default or provide actionable feedback.
- [ ] Relevant automated tests and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.

### Additional Information

Related issue: #462. Coordinate implementation and validation with the broader acceptance criteria in that issue.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Inherit the last selected model in new conversations

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A packaging run discovers that the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv no longer matches the swarm patch set **only at the very end of `assemble`**, after the payload has already been copied and precompiled. The failure itself is correct and actionable, but it arrives ~13 minutes in, so every attempt at a packaging run that touches a dependency-carrying patch pays that cost again.

Observed on `main` at `b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46` (2026-11-18), running the Windows installer chain:

```
[08:09:41] assemble payload
[08:22:20] assemble exit=1 elapsed=759s
[assemble] verifying payload imports (self-check)
[assemble] payload import OK: jiuwenswarm venv
[assemble] payload import OK: sd-services venv
[assemble] FAIL: payload greenlet check FAILED: 3.5.0 is below 3.5.5. Windows wheels 3.3.1..3.5.4
           dynamically link MSVC P140.dll (VC++ x64 redistributable) and fail on clean machines.
           Re-run scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup (or bash scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup) with the
           greenlet>=3.5.5 patch, then rebuild.
```

The gate is at `application/scripts/assemble-backend.mjs:1051-1077` (`greenletVersionAtLeast`, then `greenletRuntimeProblem`), which runs inside the "verifying payload imports" stage — after the backend tree, the venv templates, micromamba and the bytecode precompile have all been written. The preceding work in that same run was `[assemble] copying micromamba`, `precompiled bytecode for …` and so on, i.e. several minutes of payload writing that a check made at the start would have refused in seconds.

Why the venv was stale: patch `0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch` (added with the macOS adaptation work) rewrites `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` to require `greenlet>=3.5.5`, but applying swarm patches only touches the source tree. Nothing in the packaging entry point re-syncs the venv, so a machine that had a working venv from before that patch keeps `greenlet 3.5.0` until someone runs `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` by hand. After doing exactly that (`greenlet 3.5.5`, native `_greenlet` import verified), the same commit assembled in 835 s and the installer built.

Minimal reproduction, no hand-editing of the repository:

```powershell
# 1. a checkout whose jw venv predates the greenlet>=3.5.5 patch
node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup            # once, from an older main
git switch main && git pull                   # brings 0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch
# (applying patches / building is enough; the venv is NOT re-synced by the packaging chain)

# 2. package, and watch where the greenlet refusal arrives
pnpm --dir application dist
# -> payload greenlet check FAILED: 3.5.0 is below 3.5.5, after the payload has been written
```

Impact: anyone packaging the Windows desktop app against a main whose swarm patch set changed its dependencies loses a full payload assembly per attempt, and the same waste applies to the CI Windows job. The message is good; the timing is not.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Microsoft Windows 11 家庭版 10.0.26200 (build 26200) |
| Node / pnpm | v22.23.4 / 11.1.2 |
| Desktop shell | `application/` (sd-shell 0.4.0), electron-builder 26 |
| JiuwenSwarm venv | `%REPO%\.sciencediscovery-data\jiuwenswarm\src\.venv` (CPython 3.12.16) |
| Stale package | greenlet 3.5.0 (required by patch `0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch`: `>=3.5.5,<4`) |
| Command | the Windows installer chain through `pnpm --dir application assemble --expect-runner-sea` |

## Additional Information

Suggested change (small, no behaviour change for a correct tree): make the venv/patch consistency check a **preflight** of `assemble`, run before the payload is copied. Two ways:

1. Move the greenlet gate (and any other "venv must match the patch set" assertion) to the start of `assemble-backend.mjs`, keeping the existing end-of-run gate as a second line of defence.
2. Or have `assemble` compare the patch set's `uv.lock` requirement for `greenlet` (and the pinned versions it cares about) against the venv's installed version, and `fail()` with the same message before any copy when they disagree.

Either way the observable contract is: **a stale venv costs seconds, not a payload assembly**, and the failure names `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` as the fix (it already does).

Related: the same class of skew exists for any future dependency-carrying patch (`0018-desktop-slim-deps`, `0019-align-workspace-versions`, `0021-greenlet-static-runtime` all rewrite `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`), so a check driven by "does the venv satisfy the patched lockfile" is preferable to a greenlet-specific one.

A local workaround exists on the packaging side (re-apply patches, then run `jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` whenever a dependency-carrying patch changed), but the repository's own `assemble` remains the place where a packager should learn about it quickly.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46` ("fix(ci): stabilize nightly research and Windows package gate") |
| Patch that introduced the requirement | `0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch` |
| Desktop shell | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 |
| Node | v22.23.4 |
| JiuwenSwarm venv | greenlet 3.5.0 before the fix, 3.5.5 after `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` |
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: assemble discovers a stale JiuwenSwarm venv only after the whole payload is written, so a dependency-carrying patch costs ~13 minutes per attempt

closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

The permission mode is currently tucked inside the conversation composer settings, making it inconvenient to see and change. Make the active mode visible and accessible directly in the composer.

### Design Ideas

Place a compact permission selector after the + and settings buttons. When closed, show an icon and a short label:
- Request approval / 请求批准: a shield with a check mark.
- Full access / 完全访问: a shield with an exclamation mark and red text.

Clicking the selector opens a popover for choosing the mode, with a short explanation of each permission scope in smaller text; the existing scope descriptions can be retained. Provide both Chinese and English UI text.

A newly created conversation should default to the last permission mode selected by the user, including after an application restart. This inheritance applies only to new conversations: do not change the saved permission mode of conversations that already have messages. Keep each existing conversation's own setting when reopened. Persist the last selection across application restarts.

### Involved Public APIs

Determine whether an API change is needed; preserve existing permission enforcement and mode meanings.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Conversation composer, new-session initialization, session settings, localization, and permission enforcement.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Verify the selector and popover in Chinese and English, including icons, red full-access text, labels and scope descriptions. Select each mode and create a new conversation and verify it inherits the last choice, both before and after an application restart. ## 🚀 Background Description

Session research packages (`.sdresearch`) can contain datasets, artifacts, logs and trajectories. The current main-branch implementation limits the uncompressed archive to 512 MiB and the compressed import upload to 256 MiB. Consequently, an export containing incompressible data can succeed but produce a package that the same application cannot import.

PR #1173 is the baseline for this issue: **assume its changes are merged when implementing the remaining work**. At the time of this update it is still open, so its behavior should not be represented as already present on main. It unifies the configured warning threshold, raises the compressed upload bound to cover the hard archive ceiling, adds preview information and confirmation, and keeps a 1 GiB uncompressed hard ceiling. It does not establish that multi-GiB packages work safely end to end.

This issue tracks the remaining user outcomes: make the threshold and hard ceiling honest and understandable, verify that allowed exports can be imported, and then support larger packages without loading entire packages into memory. Deliver these in stages; do not wait for multi-GiB support to correct an earlier round-trip or user-facing defect.

## Design Ideas

### Stage 1: Complete the reliable round trip and limit experience

- Treat the configured export threshold as a **warning threshold**. Above it, explain the time and memory costs and allow the user to choose a smaller scope or explicitly continue, only while the selection remains within the actual hard ceiling.
- Treat the uncompressed archive hard ceiling separately. Show the ceiling and a clear message when it is exceeded; do not offer a confirmation that cannot succeed. Suggest necessary export or deselecting files.
- Make the distinction consistent in desktop and Web, including localized import/inspect errors. Expose the actual warning and hard limits through the preview or another backward-compatible API rather than assuming client constants.
- Verify the compressed upload, decompressed total, per-file and entry-count constraints independently. Prove that every package the same build allows itself to export can be imported under its own applicable limits; in particular, test a valid incompressible archive larger than the former 256 MiB upload limit. Do not infer this solely from a formula or a scaled-down test.
- Reject an oversized selection before reading and packaging its payload where possible. Keep server-side enforcement and handle changes between preview and export.

### Stage 2: Larger packages with bounded memory

- Stream export from object sources through the archive/compression pipeline and to the destination, without holding all payloads or the complete archive in memory. Ensure frontend and desktop save paths do not re-buffer the complete archive.
- Stream upload and import through bounded storage, validate archive entries and checksums before making imported records available, and preserve path, size, file-count and decompression protections. Clean up partial files on cancellation, failure and interruption.
- Check available disk space where practical and handle disk-full and memory-pressure failures clearly. Memory preflight is advisory because free memory can change during an operation.
- Use 5 GiB uncompressed as a **target for evaluation**, not an unconditional default. Set the eventual default and any configurable ceiling only after full export/import measurements on representative machines demonstrate an acceptable memory, disk and time cost. Document the resulting limits and compatibility.
- If a future per-object limit reaches the tar format's size-field boundary, use a supported encoding or impose a correct per-object limit.

## Involved Public APIs

Keep existing export, preview, inspect and import routes compatible. Add preview fields for warning and hard limits if needed, and document which limit measures compressed versus uncompressed data. Any changes to upload limits, streaming responses or error codes must be compatible with desktop and Web consumers.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Research-package archive creation and validation; API preview, background export, inspect and import; desktop native save and Web download/upload; temporary files, checksums and storage; localized dialog text and export-scope selection. Coordinate UI changes with #1024. PR #1173 is the assumed baseline; #1177 explored part of the streaming export approach and is not a complete import/export solution.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Test warning threshold and hard ceiling at and around their boundaries, including changing export scope after acknowledgement; verify both desktop and Web do not offer an impossible override.
- Run a real export → inspect → import round trip using an incompressible archive larger than 256 MiB, and compare restored content hashes. Cover synchronous/background and desktop flows as applicable, plus server-side refusal above the hard ceiling.
- Test malformed archives, decompression limits, missing data, cancellation, interrupted transfers and disk-full cleanup. Ensure the application does not execute imported content.
- For the larger-package stage, measure peak RSS, disk consumption and elapsed time for representative sizes, including a 5 GiB-class round trip on a 16 GiB machine before choosing the default. Measure the complete client-to-storage path, not only the compression function.
- Run `pnpm ci:l1` and the applicable unit, system and E2E gates; record counts and any blocked checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Warning threshold and hard ceiling are distinguished in the API and both export dialogs; a selection beyond the hard ceiling cannot be confirmed into an inevitably failing export.
- [ ] Users receive actionable localized guidance and can reduce the export scope; server-side checks refuse oversized exports before payload packaging where possible.
- [ ] A package allowed by the exporter can be inspected and imported by the same build; a real incompressible package larger than 256 MiB round-trips with matching content hashes.
- [ ] Import and export limits remain enforced independently for compressed upload, uncompressed data, individual files and entry count, including malformed or truncated archives.
- [ ] The larger-package implementation bounds memory across the whole export/import path, cleans up partial files, and records representative performance evidence before changing the default.
- [ ] The eventual default and ceiling are based on measured end-to-end behavior; 5 GiB is a target to evaluate, not a claimed capability before verification.
- [ ] Required tests and user journeys pass, with results and remaining limitations recorded.

## Additional Information

Earlier Windows measurements in the original report for incompressible payloads showed approximately 1,071 MiB peak RSS for 256 MiB, 1,248 MiB for 300 MiB, and 2,056 MiB for 500 MiB, measured across one export and import using the then-current in-memory implementation. These are historical measurements, not evidence for current main or a streaming implementation.

The reported user need is to export real research sessions larger than 512 MiB, while receiving an early and useful explanation when the chosen scope is too large. Large-package support must preserve a safe, verifiable export/import round trip.

closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Four tests in `application/test` assume POSIX capabilities that a stock Windows 11 host does not have, so `pnpm --dir application test` (and therefore the Windows installer build) is red on such a machine even though the product code is fine. They pass on the CI `windows-latest` runner (see Additional Information), which is why this only shows up for people packaging the Windows app locally.

Running `pnpm --dir application test` on a stock Windows 11 host (Node 22.23.4) gives `# tests 343 / # pass 339 / # fail 4`:

```
not ok 27 - dirWritable answers true for a writable dir and false for a read-only one
  location: 'application/test/bootstrap.test.ts:417:1'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    true !== false

not ok 28 - bootstrapPackaged degrades in-place to copy mode on a read-only payload (W16 DMG run)
  location: 'application/test/bootstrap.test.ts:434:1'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    true !== false

not ok 248 - uninstall-mac.command: syntax-clean under macOS bash 3.2 (bash -n)
  location: 'application/test/uninstall-data.test.ts:80:1'
  error: 'spawnSync /bin/bash ENOENT'

not ok 288 - replaceVenvSymlinks rewrites burned-in absolute targets to the relative bundled target
  location: 'application/test/venv-launchers.test.ts:102:1'
  error: "EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink 'C:\\Users\\builder\\.workbuddy\\...\\bin\\python3'
          -> 'C:\\Users\\...\\Temp\\sd-sym-...\\v\\bin\\python'"
```

Cause, one by one:

1. **`bootstrap.test.ts:417` / `:434`** — the fixture runs `chmod(dir, 0o555)` and expects `dirWritable()` to answer `false`. On NTFS `chmod` only toggles the read-only attribute and does not make a directory unwritable for its owner, so `dirWritable()` correctly answers `true`; the second test is the same assertion through `bootstrapPackaged`. Both describe a macOS DMG-mounted payload (`W16`), which cannot be simulated this way on Windows.
2. **`uninstall-data.test.ts:80`** — `execFileSync("/bin/bash", ["-n", SCRIPT])` needs a real `/bin/bash`, which a Windows host does not have (Git for Windows ships `bash.exe` elsewhere, WSL is not guaranteed, and the test should not depend on either).
3. **`venv-launchers.test.ts:102`** — `makePosixVenv()` creates symlinks; creating symlinks on Windows needs Developer Mode or elevation, so it raises `EPERM` on a default install.

Minimal reproduction (no test code needed):

```powershell
pnpm --dir application install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir application test          # 339 pass, 4 fail on a stock Windows 11 host
```

Impact: `pnpm --dir application dist` is the command that produces the user-facing NSIS installer, and CI runs the same test step before it. Anyone who builds the installer on a normal Windows machine has to either ignore a red gate or hand-skip it; our Windows packaging job is currently blocked at exactly this gate.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Microsoft Windows 11 家庭版 10.0.26200 (build 26200) |
| Node | v22.23.4 (x64) |
| pnpm | 11.1.2 |
| Shell used for the build | Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9818 (non-interactive) |
| Electron workspace | `application/` (renamed from `win_desktop/` by the macOS adaptation) |
| Developer Mode | off; the process is not elevated |
| `bash` on PATH | none (`/bin/bash` absent; no Git Bash/MSYS exposure in this shell) |
| Test command | `pnpm --dir application test` (`node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/*.test.ts`) |

## Additional Information

**CI does pass this step, which localises the problem to host capabilities rather than product code.** For commit `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`, Nightly run `43984975918`, job `Gate / Windows desktop installer` (`133716724096`, `windows-latest`): step 16 "Test and typecheck the desktop shell" = **success**; the job fails later, at step 17 "Build the Windows installer". The same job is skipped on `push` (`43886126438`) and `merge_group` (`43880862208`) because it is gated on `needs.policy.outputs.windows_desktop == 'true'` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:896`), so only the Nightly/release runs exercise it.

Suggested change — gate on the capability the test needs, not on a platform guess:

- `uninstall-data.test.ts:80`: skip when `/bin/bash` is not executable (`existsSync("/bin/bash")` or a `spawnSync` capability probe), and say in a comment that the macOS 3.2 syntax check only runs where that shell exists.
- `venv-launchers.test.ts:102`: skip when a symlink probe in the temp dir throws `EPERM`/`EACCES`, so a machine without Developer Mode still exercises the rest of the file.
- `bootstrap.test.ts:417` / `:434`: these two describe the macOS DMG payload; either skip them on `win32` (the payload is never read-only there) or replace the `chmod` fixture with a Windows-valid read-only simulation (an ACL that denies write) so the assertion means something on both hosts.

The four failures are test-only; `pnpm --dir application build`, `assemble` and `electron-builder --win` are unaffected once the gate is passed.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74` ("feat(mac): macOS desktop adaptation — shell, packaging chain, sandbox & distribution") |
| Desktop shell package | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 (`application/package.json`) |
| Electron | `^37.0.0` (declared in `application/package.json`) |
| Node | v22.23.4 |
| CI evidence | Nightly run `43984975918`, job `133716724096` |
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Windows desktop shell tests depend on POSIX host capabilities (read-only dirs, /bin/bash, symlink privilege), so the installer build gate is red on a stock Windows host

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop session header has an Export button at the upper right while the session's sidebar menu already provides an export action. These duplicate entries add an unwanted persistent control to the session header.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a session in the desktop application.
2. Observe the Export button in the upper-right session header.
3. Open the session's sidebar menu and observe its Export session action.

**Expected:** Remove the upper-right session-header Export button and retain the existing session-menu export entry so users can still export sessions.

**Actual:** Both export entries are present.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Desktop application, Windows (user-reported).
- The user's exact Windows version and packaged build identifier were not provided.
- The latest main-branch source at `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74` contains both the session-header button and sidebar menu entry; this source inspection is not a separate packaged-app reproduction.

## Additional Information

The session-header entry was introduced by #1171 for #1154. Preserve access to the existing export flow and export history when removing the redundant header control. Related: #1024 discusses the broader export interface.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Inspected main commit: `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`
- User's packaged build: not provided.

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which would reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens**

Forking a conversation branch from a session that has run an Evolve search produces a package whose `records.evolve.candidates` still lists the kept candidates, but whose `objects` no longer contains their source bytes. The package exports without a warning, and the loss only shows up at import: every candidate is reported as `evolve:<run>:<hash>:missing candidate source object`, `evolve-candidates/<restored run>/` is left empty, `/api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>` has nothing to serve, and `get_evolve_run` drops `bestSource`.

**Why** (verified by reading the code on `main` at `e727e750`)

`services/api/src/conversation-branches.ts:258-260` rebuilds the object allow-list from four sources only:

```ts
const needed = new Set([...workspace.map((file) => file.objectPath),
  ...records.artifacts.flatMap((artifact) => artifact.versions.flatMap((version) => version.objectPath ? [version.objectPath] : [])),
  ...casHashes(records), ...records.versionObjects.map((ref) => ref.digest.slice(7))]);
```

and then drops every other object (`:274`). Evolve candidate sources are not covered by any of the four:

- They are not workspace files or artifact version `objectPath`s.
- `casHashes` (`services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:60`) only collects a nested `hash` when the same record also carries a numeric `size`:
  ```ts
  if (typeof record.hash === "string" && typeof record.size === "number") hashes.add(record.hash);
  ```
  A candidate record is `{ hash, objectPath, runId }` with no `size`, and its key is `hash`, not one of the `content_hash|code_hash|stdout_hash|stderr_hash|env_hash` keys the same function matches next.
- They are plain CAS objects added with `addObject(bytes, "log")`, so they are not `versionObjects`.

The full-session exporter gets this right: `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:686` adds `evolveCandidateSources.map((source) => source.objectPath)` to its own `needed`. `buildConversationBranch` has no equivalent entry, and the candidate objects do reach it — `buildResearchPackageInput` (`research-snapshots.ts:346`) adds them at `:575` and keeps them at `:686`, so `input.objects` handed to the branch builder contains them.

The export-time receipt check does not catch it either: `research-snapshots.ts:957-959` only warns when the whole candidate array is empty (`packageCarriesEvolveCandidateSources`), and here the array is non-empty while the bytes behind it are gone.

**Minimal reproduction**

In `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts`, extend `branchFixture()` so that `input.objects` contains the candidate source object whose `path` is the `objectPath` of a candidate kept by the branch (any non-empty bytes), then assert it survives:

```ts
const output = await buildConversationBranch(input, source.session.id, "fixture-answer", async () => { throw new Error("missing"); }, countExport);
const keptRun = (output.records as any).evolve.runs[0].run.id;
const candidate = (output.records as any).evolve.candidates.find((c: any) => c.runId === keptRun);
assert.ok(candidate, "the branch keeps the candidate entry");
assert.ok(output.objects.some((object) => object.path === candidate.objectPath),
  "the branch carries the bytes the candidate entry points at");
```

The second assertion fails today: the entry is kept, the object is filtered out. (A runnable end-to-end view: fork a session that ran an Evolve search, import the resulting package, and read `receipt.omissions` — one `missing candidate source object` line per kept candidate.)

**Expected**

A branch package should be self-consistent: every `records.evolve.candidates[]` entry it carries must have its `objectPath` present in `objects`, exactly like the full-session export. Alternatively the branch should drop the candidate entries it cannot carry and say so in the receipt, rather than shipping dangling references.

**Suggested fix**

Add the kept candidates' `objectPath`s to the `needed` set in `conversation-branches.ts:258`, next to the artifact-version paths, and pin it with the assertion above.

**Impact**

User-reachable data loss on the branch path, and it defeats the purpose of carrying Evolve runs through a branch: the restored branch shows searches whose candidate source code cannot be read or re-run. Events, goal, status, budget and best node still restore, so the run itself is not lost.

Related: introduced with the branch-side Evolve carrying in #1176 (`fix(evolve): restore searches in imported and continued sessions`, merged at `e727e750`). Imported/continued copies are not affected — the writable-continuation path reads the bytes stored during import.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- `main` at `e727e750844c0dd3db58ed558e61526427097f40` (merge of #1176), observed 2026-11-17
- Node 22.19.0 (the version pinned by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), Linux x86_64 CI image
- Reproducible by code reading plus the `UT` test harness; the failing assertion is in `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts`

### Additional Information

Not a blocker for the restored session's usability in the narrow sense (the branch still opens and the runs are listed), so I am filing it rather than asking for a revert. The failing path is `POST` a branch export → import → `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>`.

Found while reviewing #1176 at head `cd0a525c`; it was also raised there as a must-fix finding by the repository's review bot after that head had already entered the merge queue, so it landed on `main` with the PR.

### Version Information

- sciencediscovery `main` @ `e727e750844c0dd3db58ed558e61526427097f40`
- Introduced by #1176 (head `cd0a525c9b67195ad9d48258cc41768491494eca`)

closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Users need a research session exported to a `.sdresearch` package and imported again to retain its Evolve history. In a Windows desktop test, after exporting a session with a completed Evolve search, importing it and choosing to continue the research, the conversation no longer showed the interactive Evolve card or the task panel containing the optimization results.

This request covers the complete user-facing preservation and acceptance of Evolve history across export, import and creation of a writable research continuation. Related: #1019 addressed the earlier absence of Evolve run records in research packages; #1060 and #1136 added run/event and candidate-source packaging. Draft PR #1176 addresses run-ID collisions during import and continuation; its desktop journey and full validation remain outstanding.

## Design Ideas

- Carry each selected session's Evolve runs, configuration, budget, status, events, candidate tree, scores, best result and available candidate source content in the package, for both supported export levels.
- Restore each run under the correct imported session. Repeated imports, importing on the source machine, and creating a writable continuation must produce independent, correctly associated records without overwriting another session's runs or mixing candidates.
- In both the read-only imported snapshot and the writable continuation, show the Evolve card and allow it to open the desktop task panel. Preserve the optimization tree, budget and results, node selection, candidate details and available source/diff views.
- Preserve multiple runs and their ownership. Report missing or omitted run data, events or candidate sources explicitly, while keeping the rest of the session usable. Older packages cannot recover data they never contained.
- Do not automatically restart a search when importing or viewing it. An in-flight search cannot continue on the target merely from a historical snapshot: present a truthful historical/terminal state and retain available partial results. Access to a still-running source session remains a separate live status, not an imported live execution.
- Re-running a search or achieving identical scientific results in another environment is outside this request.

## Involved Public APIs

Prefer the existing session export/import and research-continuation APIs and the Evolve run-list, event and candidate-source read APIs. Verify their behavior with remapped run IDs and session ownership; document any necessary additive contract or compatibility changes. Import must not execute package contents.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Research package serialization, validation, import and continuation; Evolve run/event storage and candidate source storage; session ownership and ID mapping; desktop conversation cards, task panel, tree and node inspector. Preserve compatibility with old packages and sessions without Evolve.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Add regression coverage for completed, stopped, failed and in-flight searches, multiple runs, missing candidate sources, malformed package data and sessions without Evolve.
- Export and import on the source machine and a fresh data directory; repeat the import and create a writable continuation. Check independent ownership, run identifiers, event order, budgets, scores, candidate content, and absence of automatic execution.
- Exercise the actual Windows desktop user journey: complete a search → export → import → open the card and task panel → inspect tree nodes and source/diff → continue research → repeat the inspection. Also verify the imported snapshot remains read-only and the new session supports chat.
- Run the applicable unit, system and mocked E2E gates (`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`) and report counts; distinguish blocked environment checks from passing results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After export and import, each Evolve run is associated with the right session and its interactive card opens the task panel, including optimization results, tree, budgets, scores and available node details and source/diff.
- [ ] Creating a writable research continuation preserves the same available Evolve history and allows subsequent chat; the imported snapshot stays read-only.
- [ ] Same-machine import, repeated import and multiple Evolve runs retain independent, correctly associated records without overwriting the original or mixing sources.
- [ ] Stopped, failed and previously running searches display truthful status and available partial data; viewing or importing never starts a new search.
- [ ] Missing or omitted data and limitations of older packages are reported explicitly, and the rest of the session remains usable.
- [ ] Relevant automated regression and Windows desktop user-journey checks pass, with command results and any remaining limitations recorded.

## Additional Information

The requested behavior is preservation and inspection of recorded Evolve results, not deterministic reproduction or automatic resumption. PR #1176 is a draft and must not be treated as full desktop validation.

closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

After a session export completes, the desktop app shows the saved package only for as long as the export dialog stays open, and only as a single line with a 打开文件位置 button. Once the dialog closes — or the app restarts — the package is gone from the product: the only way back to it is remembering which folder the OS save dialog used.

Two independent facts cause that:

- **The list is component state.** `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx:83` keeps `exports` in `useState<ExportRecord[]>([])`; the 已保存的会话包 block at `:349` renders from it and nothing writes it anywhere.
- **Even the reveal token dies with the process.** The renderer never holds a path (deliberately: `win_desktop/src/export-tokens.ts` explains why a renderer-chosen path is refused); the main process keeps an **in-memory** `Map` of tokens with a default limit of 32 (`export-tokens.ts:22-48`), and the only thing `win_desktop/src/export-state.ts` persists is `lastExportDir` — a folder, not a list, and not a token.

So today "打开文件位置" works for the packages exported in the current run, in the current dialog, and never again. A user who exports a session for a colleague, closes the app, and comes back tomorrow has no in-product way to find that file.

Related: `#1024` describes a durable "export center" as its phase 2 inside a wider export-dialog redesign, and `#986` / PR `#999` built the native save flow this history would sit on. This issue is the narrow slice — a durable list plus where it is reachable — so it can be delivered without waiting for the whole redesign; if `#1024` is taken as one piece, this should fold into its phase 2 rather than run in parallel.

## Design Ideas

### Where it belongs (recommendation)

**Primary entry — the session header.** `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx:100` already owns `task-head-actions` (the workspace toggle lives there). Add an 导出 button that opens the export surface: the scope form on top, and 本会话 / 本项目的导出记录 underneath. Rationale: exporting is a session-level task, so its history belongs next to the action, and the user never has to remember a folder. This also matches `#1024`'s point 5 (give export a first-class entry instead of the row-menu).

**Global fallback — 设置 → 导出记录.** `SystemSettingsDialog.tsx` already renders grouped categories with a side nav (`:185-227`), which suits a longer, searchable list across projects and sessions: filename, size, time, session, destination, 打开文件位置 / 重新保存 / 移除记录. Rationale: the "I exported this last week, where is it" case is not tied to the session the user happens to have open.

**Keep the in-dialog list**, but read it from the durable store rather than component state (`ResearchPackage.tsx:349`). Users already know that block; it should stop being amnesia.

**Not recommended:** a third entry in the 64px rail — `Rail.tsx` deliberately exposes only 任务 and 设置 as surfaces (its own comment notes even scientific memory is not a rail surface, it is a header capsule), so a third glyph changes the app's structure for one list. Equally, leaving history only inside the session row menu (`Sidebar.tsx`) keeps it buried, which is exactly what `#1024` wants to fix.

### What has to be persisted

- A new `exports.json` under the shell's `userData`, written with the same temp-file-then-rename discipline as `win_desktop/src/window-state.ts` / `export-state.ts`: one row per finished export — `id`, `token`, `path`, `filename`, `bytes`, `savedAt`, `projectId`, `sessionId`, `sessionTitle`.
- **Only successful writes are recorded** (after `markWritten`). Canceled, failed or still-packaging exports must not create entries; a "retry save" updates the existing row instead of adding a second one.
- The token stays in the main process. Persist the token→path mapping so `sd-shell:export-show-in-folder` still resolves after a restart; the renderer continues to receive and send only opaque tokens, which keeps the existing safety model intact.
- Keep `ExportDestinations`' in-memory 32-entry cap as the per-run guard, and give the persisted list its own bound (for example the newest 200 rows). Eviction removes the record, never the user's file.
- On reveal, stat the path first: a row whose file was moved or deleted stays visible as 文件已被移动或删除 with 移除记录, instead of disappearing silently.
- IPC surface next to the existing `sd-shell:export-*` handlers: `export-history:list`, `export-history:reveal(token)`, `export-history:forget(token)`; `preload.ts` exposes them on `sdShell`, mirroring `exportFile` (`preload.ts:79-86`).
- Web (browser, no shell) has no reveal capability: show the same list degraded to filename, size and time, without the 打开文件位置 action, so both clients keep working.

### What it must not become

Not an export manager that copies or moves packages: it only remembers where the user put them. No background re-export, no checksum verification on every load (a stat is enough), no new server endpoint.

## Involved Public APIs

No server API change is required: the history lives in the desktop shell, and the byte count is known from the write itself.

- Electron IPC/preload only: three new methods on `sdShell` alongside `exportFile.saveDialog/write/showInFolder/downloadsDir`. Additive; the renderer already feature-detects the shell (`apps/desktop/src/app/export-bridge.ts`).
- If the export task's finished size is later exposed by the API (`#1024` proposes `archiveBytes`), the row can prefer it over the written byte count; not required here.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `win_desktop/src/export-tokens.ts` | Persist issued+written destinations, load on start, keep the in-memory cap |
| `win_desktop/src/export-state.ts` | Either extend to a record list or add a sibling `export-history.ts` with the same atomic-write discipline |
| `win_desktop/src/main.ts`, `preload.ts` | Three IPC handlers + `sdShell` methods |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/export-bridge.ts`, `views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Read/write the durable list instead of local state |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx`, `SystemSettingsDialog.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx` | Entries; keep the row-menu item as a shortcut |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/{zh,en}.ts`, `apps/web` | Copy and the degraded web list |
| `#1024` | Phase 2 overlap: coordinate so both do not build two lists |

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit** (`win_desktop`): history store appends, dedupes by token, evicts at the bound, survives a corrupt/missing JSON as empty, and keeps the atomic rename; token resolution works for a token loaded from disk (the restart case).
- **Component** (desktop): the row renders filename, size, time and session; 打开文件位置 calls reveal with the stored token; a missing file renders its state plus 移除记录; empty state has copy; zh-CN and en both covered.
- **E2E with the real shell**: export a package → close the dialog → restart the app → the export is still listed and 打开文件位置 opens the folder; delete the file on disk and reload → the row shows the missing state; 移除记录 drops it; a canceled export leaves no row.
- **Commands**: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots of the history in the session-header entry and in 设置 → 导出记录, including the missing-file state, go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval (UI review rule).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A finished export appears in a history list that survives closing the panel and restarting the app.
- [ ] Each row shows filename, size, saved time, originating session, and destination, and 打开文件位置 works for exports made before the restart.
- [ ] Only completed writes are recorded; canceled or failed exports create no entry, and 重新保存 updates the existing row.
- [ ] A package whose file was moved or deleted stays listed with a missing-file state and can be removed from the list (never silently dropped).
- [ ] The list is reachable from the session header's export entry and from 设置 → 导出记录, with search or project filtering in the settings view.
- [ ] The renderer still handles only opaque tokens; no filesystem path is accepted from the page.
- [ ] zh-CN and en copy; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

## Additional Information

Current behaviour, for reproduction:

1. Export a session (导出会话 → 保存). The dialog shows the saved package with 打开文件位置 and the app flashes a success toast.
2. Close the dialog, then reopen it: the list is empty again (it is component state).
3. Restart the app: nothing in the product refers to that package any more, and `%APPDATA%\ScienceDiscovery\export-state.json` contains only `lastExportDir`.

Where the pieces live today: `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx:83` (list state), `:349` (saved block), `apps/desktop/src/app/export-bridge.ts` (shell bridge contract), `win_desktop/src/export-tokens.ts` (in-memory token map, limit 32), `win_desktop/src/export-state.ts` (`lastExportDir` only).

Requested by the user as: exporting is only acknowledged with a one-line 打开文件位置 notice at the bottom of the page, and they want a findable export history so earlier packages can be located quickly from the desktop UI.
