closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

When the model connection is reset after the model has already streamed part of its answer, the agent run fails. No layer retries it.

That is what ended three research jobs in the manual Nightly run [41852669139](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41852669139) on 2026-11-04 (branch `ci/l5-biomnibench-da`, head `b8819fc8b`, JiuwenSwarm backend, model `deepseek-flash` behind an OpenAI-compatible relay gateway).

### What failed

`research-1` (DRB-58) and `research-5` (DRB-75) both ended with:

```
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The `[model-sse-summary]` lines in each job's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-<shard>`) identify the request:

| Job | Request sent (UTC) | 200 headers | Connection reset | Streamed before reset | Attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| research-1 | 15:00:19.235 | 15:00:23.403 | **15:01:46.872** | 83 s, 848,494 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |
| research-5 | 16:00:31.110 | 16:00:36.449 | **16:03:30.928** | 175 s, 2,791,403 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |

`research-10` failed in the same way. Its run error reads `interaction round execution failed`, and each of its three failed runs directly follows a mid-stream reset (16:26:31.901, 16:31:37.391 and 16:49:24.951).

### The fault is external; the failure is ours

- 16 of the run's 382 requests to the gateway ended with `error.classification: network`. They came from 5 independent runners, and all of them fall between 15:01 and 16:50 UTC.
- The same gateway served 1,386 requests in the two earlier runs on this branch (03:07–06:38 and 10:09–12:50 UTC) without a single network reset.
- Streams of 176 s / 2.9 MB and 214 s / 2.8 MB completed normally in the same run, so a fixed size or duration limit is not the cause.
- 9 of the 16 resets were retried and recovered. They all came before any answer text or tool-call delta: either before the response opened, or while only reasoning had streamed. The head under test (PR #853) retries the second case.
- The other 7 happened after answer text or tool-call deltas had started. Nothing retried them. Every run failure in research-1, research-5 and research-10 follows one of these 7.

### Retry behaviour on `main` (`48848578`)

On the JiuwenSwarm backend, a model call travels Swarm → ScienceDiscovery model gateway (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`) → `packages/model/src/client.ts` → provider.

| Layer | What it retries | After the stream has started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/model` `requestWithRetry` | Connect errors, header timeout, 429 and 5xx. Budget: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES=2`. Backoff: 0.5 s doubling up to 4 s, or a numeric `Retry-After`. Header timeout: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` | Nothing. The code says so: "Once the stream starts flowing, errors surface to the caller". `bodyTimeout: 0` also means a stalled body is never treated as lost |
| JiuwenSwarm model gateway | Nothing of its own. It holds response headers until the first answer byte, so a failure before the stream opens reaches Swarm as a real HTTP error | Forwards the error |
| Swarm's OpenAI SDK | Its built-in retries before a response arrives | Nothing |
| openJiuwen `agent_teams` `StreamController` | — | Re-drives a team member's round that failed with `181001`: up to 10 times, with a "continue" query. The main session run is not covered: research-1 and research-5 logged `run of <session> failed: [181001]` straight after the reset |
| Run | Nothing. `classifyRunFailure` maps ECONNRESET to `transport-error`, which is only displayed and recorded | — |

PR #853 adds one more retry in `streamModelTurn`: `network` and `timeout` errors are retried while `answerStarted` is still false. It cannot cover the 7 resets that came after output had started.

One safety property already holds. The gateway withholds tool-call arguments until the upstream turn finishes; in the meantime it sends empty deltas as progress. A stream cut mid-turn therefore never executes a partial tool call, so re-driving the failed turn cannot repeat a side effect. Text and reasoning deltas, on the other hand, are forwarded as they arrive. That is why the transport layer cannot replay the request transparently once text has started.

### How other agents handle a mid-stream drop

All rows except the DeepSeek API docs were read from current sources.

| Agent | Mid-stream drop | Budget and backoff | Partial output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | Retries stream disconnects, connection failures, timeouts, 5xx and 429. A stream idle for `stream_idle_timeout_ms` (default 300000) counts as lost | `stream_max_retries` 5 and `request_max_retries` 4. Exponential backoff with jitter; server retry advice wins. After the budget runs out it falls back from WebSocket to HTTPS | Only items completed with `output_item.done` enter history. The retry re-samples from history: the partial item is dropped, completed tool calls are kept |
| [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) | `StreamError` and `EventStreamError` are retried; `IdleTimeout` is not | 15 retries (`GROK_MAX_RETRIES`). 2 s doubling to 30 s, ±20% jitter. The first retry rebuilds the HTTP client; rate limits are retried once | The same request is re-sampled and the failed attempt is discarded |
| [pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) | Restarts the whole turn at the agent level, matching the error text (`terminated`, `socket hang up`, `other side closed`, `stream ended…`) | 3 retries, 2/4/8 s, capped at 60 s. Shows `Retrying (n/3)` and can be cancelled | The failed assistant message stays in the raw log but is hidden from the model; the agent continues from the previous message |
| [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | Retries mid-stream errors, including `ECONNRESET` and `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` | 3 retries, 1/2/4 s. Failures before the stream opens have a separate policy (5 s up to 30 s) | Emits a `RETRY` event and resends the request |
| [DeepSeek API docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit) | No agent. 500 and 503: "retry your request after a brief wait". Waiting streams receive `: keep-alive` comments, and the connection is closed if inference has not started within 10 minutes | — | No guidance on mid-stream drops |
| [DeepSeek-TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) (third-party) | Retries only a stream that failed to open. A drop while reading the body is reported and not replayed, to avoid duplicated output | — | — |

The common pattern: retry at the turn, not at the HTTP request. Output counts only once an item or turn completes. On failure, the partial attempt is discarded and the turn is re-sampled from the last committed state, with a bounded, jittered backoff and a visible status.

## Design Ideas

1. **Re-drive the main run's failed turn on a transient transport fault.** This covers a `181001` caused by a network or stream error, or `transport-error`. Drop the failed round from the model's context and continue from the last committed round. openJiuwen already does this for team members, and pi does it for every turn. Budget 3–5 attempts with jittered exponential backoff capped at 30–60 s, honour cancellation, and show a retry status in the run timeline. Still to decide: whether this lives in the JiuwenSwarm patch set or in `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`. The native loop needs the same behaviour.
2. **Treat a stalled stream as lost.** Add an idle timeout on the response body (Codex uses 5 minutes), so a hung stream enters the same recovery instead of waiting forever.
3. **Use a fresh connection on the first retry**, as Grok Build does, so a reset does not reuse a broken pooled connection.
4. **Keep non-transient errors out:** authentication, quota, context-overflow, invalid-request and content-policy errors stay non-retryable.

Alternative, for comparison only: buffer text in the gateway as it already buffers tool calls, so the transport layer can replay the whole upstream request transparently. This would remove live text streaming on the Swarm path.

## Involved Public APIs

This may add settings for the turn retry budget and backoff and for the stream idle timeout, next to `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES`. It may also add a run-timeline event for "retrying after a dropped model stream". No change to existing request or session APIs is expected.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/model/src/client.ts`: retry policy, idle timeout, and the `retryErrors` wire diagnostics.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`, the JiuwenSwarm patches, and the native loop.
- Web run timeline: the retry status, and partial text that a retry replaces.
- CI accounting (related to #813): `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs` does not count these failures as provider faults; the run's verdict shows `provider faults 0`. The error text carries no 5xx status, and `PRODUCT_REPORT` (`main run must complete`, `delivery_status`) vetoes it in any case.
- PR #853: the retry it adds for interruptions during the reasoning phase.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- UT for `packages/model` and the gateway: a fake upstream returns 200, streams text and tool-call deltas, then resets the socket. Assert that the turn is re-driven within the budget, that no tool call from the cut attempt executes, and that exhaustion still fails with the original error and wire diagnostics.
- UT: a fake upstream stops sending bytes mid-stream. Assert that the idle timeout classifies the stream as lost and retries it.
- UT: 401/403, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- Mocked E2E: the stub model resets the stream after some answer text. The run completes, the timeline shows the retry, and the answer text is not duplicated.
- Real nightly: wherever `[model-sse-summary]` shows a mid-stream `network` reset, a completed turn follows instead of a failed run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stream reset after answer text or tool-call deltas have started no longer ends the main run while retry budget remains; the run continues from the last committed turn.
- [ ] No tool call from the interrupted attempt executes, and no completed tool call runs twice.
- [ ] The retry is visible in the run timeline and can be cancelled. When the budget is exhausted, the run fails with the original provider error preserved.
- [ ] Authentication, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- [ ] The JiuwenSwarm and native backends behave the same.
- [ ] A test covering the mid-stream reset fails on current `main` and passes with the change.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

The other failures in run 41852669139 are outside this issue; they come from the head under test, not from the provider:

- `research-6`: none of the 16 evolve expansions produced a runnable candidate. The most common reason logged was that the 16000-token per-call cap was spent on reasoning.
- The mocked `standard-journeys` and `standard-config` workers: the head buffers reasoning deltas until answer text or a tool call starts.

The main scheduled Nightly that day ([41919338127](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41919338127), `main` `48848578`, provider called directly) passed, with no network reset in 826 requests.

## Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop conversation shows “Skipped 1 event this version does not recognise” when the API sends a valid `mcp.readiness` event. Users see the same notice when reopening an affected conversation. The desktop transcript discards the connector diagnostic, while the web timeline already renders it.

Minimal reproduction against the desktop run-stream reducer:

```ts
const state = reduceRunStream(emptyRunStream(), {
  type: "mcp.readiness",
  summary: "example: degraded; omitted tools: search.",
}, 1);
```

On main, `state.unknownEvents` is 1. To reproduce through the UI, run a desktop conversation with a selected MCP connector that is unavailable or degraded, then reopen the conversation and inspect the run. The desktop instead should keep the diagnostic in the run details and reserve the unknown-event notice for genuinely unrecognized events.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

Desktop development UI and local API, Ubuntu under WSL 2, Node.js 22.19.0. The reducer reproduction takes a synthetic event and requires no external connector, model, or credentials.

## Additional Information

The API event is declared in `packages/schema/src/session.ts` and emitted from `services/api/src/runs/index.ts`. The desktop reducer in `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts` falls through to its unknown-event counter. Its live and history paths both use that reducer. I am preparing a desktop fix and regression coverage for those paths.

Confirmed on upstream main `2062a636ca23a87c99d60cc77fb56ccd4135db8f`.

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
## 1. Summary

On the JiuwenSwarm executor, the link between a model call and the provider response it belongs to is stored in a single mutable field on the recorder (`responseId`). It is **written synchronously** by the event path and **read later, from a queued task**, by the code that writes the `model.completed` record. Neither call passes the identity as an argument, so the value a record gets is whatever the field happens to hold when the queue drains.

Across four completed runs, **54 of 303 `model.completed` records carry no `responseId` even though a response with the same `evidence.turn` did emit one**. The correlation existed and was lost on the way to disk.

## 2. Expected behaviour

A model completion record should carry the identity of the response it completes, bound **per call**, and that binding should not depend on scheduling:

- `assistant.response.started` arrives with `responseId` (`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts:940-944`);
- the `model.completed` record for that same call (`versioning.ts:259`) should reference that id.

The recorder already takes the identity as a parameter for other work — `recordObservation({ …, sequence })`, `afterTurn({ turn, … })` — so a per-call binding is the established shape here; `responseId` is the exception.

## 3. Actual behaviour

`responseId` is process state on a shared object. It has one setter, two clearers, and one consumer that reads it on a different tick from the setter.

## 4. Source code

All paths relative to the repository root, quoted at main `f0efd382e`.

### 4.1 One mutable field, one setter, two clearing points

```ts
// services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts   (AgentVersionRecorder — the single recorder for both executors)
:155  private currentTurn = 0;
:156  private responseId?: string;                     // the only place the correlation lives
:185  async beforeTurn({ turn, history } …) {
:187    this.currentTurn = turn;
:189    this.responseId = undefined;                   // clearing point 1 — runs inside the recording queue
:213  async afterAssembly({ turn, assembly } …) {
:214    // The new response ID is allocated by the loop after assembly, including retries.
:215    this.responseId = undefined;                   // clearing point 2 — also inside the queue
:245  event(event: RunEvent<U>): AgentEventEvidence {
:246    if (event.type === "turn_start") this.currentTurn = event.turn;
:247    if (event.type === "response_start") this.responseId = event.responseId;   // the ONLY setter — synchronous
:251    return this.evidence();
:254  async modelCompleted(result: unknown): Promise<void> {
:259    await this.record("model.completed", undefined, undefined, this.evidence(), this.modelAction);
:285  private evidence(): AgentEventEvidence {
:287    … turn: this.currentTurn,
:288    ...(this.responseId ? { responseId: this.responseId } : {}) };   // snapshot at read time, not at call time
```

### 4.2 The write is synchronous; the read is queued

```ts
// services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts
:286  private emit(event: AgentEvent): void {
:288    const evidence = this.trajectory?.evidence(event as { type: string; responseId?: unknown; turn?: unknown });
:290    for (const listener of this.listeners) listener(tagged);      // no queue on this path
:940  case "assistant.response.started": {
:943    this.emit({ type: "response_start", responseId: String(event.responseId), turn });

// services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts
:82   private turn = -1;
:171  modelRequest(input) { return this.run("model_request", async () => { … this.turn += 1;
:177      … this.recorder!.beforeTurn({ turn: this.turn, history }) … }); }      // clears, on the queue
:192  modelCompleted(turn, history) { return this.run("model_completed", async () => {
:195      await this.stage("model_completed", () => this.recorder!.modelCompleted(turn)); }); }  // reads, on the queue
:208  evidence(event) { …
:216    const runEvent = event.type === "response_start"
:217      ? { type: "response_start", responseId: String(event.responseId), turn: this.turn }
:219    return this.recorder.event(runEvent as never);                 // sets, synchronously
```

### 4.3 The await on the queue is not the guarantee it looks like

```ts
// services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts
:501  if (!auxiliary) { last = undefined; lifecycle?.beforeTurn?.(); }   // turn_start per call
:523  await prepare();          // → observer.request → queued beforeTurn + afterAssembly (both clear)
:558  await record(turn);       // → observer.completed → queued modelCompleted (reads)
:351  const observed = auxiliary ? undefined : observer;   // housekeeping/compaction calls are never observed

// services/api/src/agent-run/recording-wait.ts
:6    /** Stop waiting, not the underlying write. Keep handlers attached for late failures. */
:7    export function waitForRecording<T>(work: Promise<T>, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
:9      const abort = () => reject(signal.reason ?? new Error("Recording wait cancelled"));
```

`waitForRecording` returns control to the caller on abort **while the queued write keeps running**. So the ordering that §4.2 appears to provide (`prepare` drains, then the response starts, then `record` drains) is only guaranteed for calls that are not aborted — and an aborted call is exactly the case where a later turn's `beforeTurn`/`afterAssembly` can clear the field before the earlier `model_completed` reads it.

### 4.4 Who consumes the field (this is user-visible, not just audit)

```ts
// packages/trajectory/src/server.ts
:117  if (contextRef && typeof event.responseId === "string") responses.set(`${agentId}:${event.responseId}`, `context:${contextRef.digest}`);
:281  const contextId = contextRef ? … : legacy?.contextId ?? call?.contextId ?? responses.get(`${item.agentId}:${String(event.responseId ?? evidence.responseId)}`);
:285  if (contextId && typeof (event.responseId ?? evidence.responseId) === "string") responses.set(…);

// apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx
:295  function findAssistantByResponseId(entries, responseId) …
:300  function findThinkingByResponseId(entries, responseId) …
:377  if (last?.type === "thinking" && last.turn === event.turn && last.responseId === undefined) {   // adopt an unstamped placeholder
:482  … && entry.responseId === undefined && entry.turn === event.turn) adoptIndex = index;
:497  if (entry.type === "thinking" && entry.responseId === event.responseId && entry.status === "running") …
```

A missing id pushes the trajectory server onto the `legacy?.contextId ?? call?.contextId` fallback (`server.ts:281`) and pushes the timeline onto turn-based matching, where an unstamped placeholder can be adopted by whichever response arrives (`RunTimeline.tsx:377`, `:482`). A wrong id attaches one response's thinking block to another response.

## 5. Reproduction

Observed on four existing completed runs (read-only pass over their run records; no agent was re-run).

| Run | `model.completed` rows | with `responseId` | without | `assistant.response.started` records | **without id, but a started record exists at that turn** | without id and no started record at that turn | started ids never appearing on any completed row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `c48cf34a…` | 108 | 93 | 15 | 111 | **14** | 1 (turn 54) | 18 |
| `483d89ca…` | 33 | 30 | 3 | 31 | **1** | 2 (turns 1, 2) | 1 |
| `71987d15…` | 104 | 76 | 28 | 101 | **25** | 3 (turns 1, 3, 5) | 25 |
| `324a1e1f…` | 58 | 39 | 19 | 57 | **14** | 5 (turns 1, 3, 6, 7, 14) | 18 |
| **Total** | **303** | **238** | **65** | **300** | **54** | **11** | **62** |

Ordering evidence from one run (`483d89ca…`), the earliest missing-id row and its neighbours:

```
2026-11-12T02:17:48.813Z  model.completed              turn=1   responseId=<absent>
2026-11-12T02:18:22.525Z  model.completed              turn=2   responseId=<absent>
2026-11-12T02:18:24.269Z  assistant.response.started   turn=3   responseId=356e99dd-e7b5
2026-11-12T02:18:26.093Z  model.completed              turn=3   responseId=356e99dd-e7b5
```

Turns 1 and 2 recorded no identity while turn 3, handled by the same code a second later, recorded it — so this is not a capability gap in the executor; the field simply held nothing at read time.

**A deterministic unit reproduction does not need a live run**: construct an `AgentVersionRecorder`, call `event({ type: "response_start", responseId: "r1", turn: 1 })`, then `beforeTurn({ turn: 2 })` (or `afterAssembly`) and only then `modelCompleted(result)`. The resulting `model.completed` evidence carries `turn: 2` and **no** `responseId`, although the response it completes is `r1`. This pass did not execute that test, so it is stated as a design check rather than as a measured result.

## 6. Scientific impact

1. **A model turn cannot be tied back to the provider response that produced it** for 54 of 303 turns (17.8 %). When a claim in a report traces to a `model.completed` record, the record can name the turn but not the response, so re-deriving the exact prompt/response pair for that turn is not possible from the record itself.
2. **Silent, partial and non-reproducible.** No error is raised and nothing is logged. The rate of "id lost although a started record exists at that turn" per completion row differs by run — 13.0 % (`c48cf34a`), 3.0 % (`483d89ca`), 24.0 % (`71987d15`), 24.1 % (`324a1e1f`) — so an audit that spot-checks a few records will sometimes see nothing wrong.
3. **Downstream correlation is heuristic, not authoritative.** The trajectory server's response→context map (`server.ts:117`, `:285`) is only populated from stamped records; the web timeline adopts unstamped placeholders by turn proximity (`RunTimeline.tsx:377`, `:482`). Both degrade to guessing exactly for the rows where the identity is missing.
4. **62 started responses never reach a completion record.** Whether those calls ended without a completion or the identity was dropped is not distinguishable from the surviving data — which is itself the cost of the design: two different failures produce the same artifact.

## 7. Suggested fix direction

1. **Bind the identity per call instead of per recorder.** Allocate the response id alongside the turn in the object the queue already carries (the `pending` entry at `jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts:196`), and pass it into `modelCompleted` so the record is stamped from a parameter, not from `this`.
2. **If a field must stay, make the loss visible.** When `evidence()` is called for `model.completed` with `responseId` unset while a `response_start` for the same turn has been seen, that is a detectable inconsistency — log/count it instead of dropping it silently.
3. **Make the queue the only writer.** Both clearing points already run inside the queue (`:189`, `:215`) and the only setter does not (`emit` → `event` at `:247`). Routing the setter through the same queue would serialize the field; the correctness fix is (1), and (3) at least removes the cross-domain interleaving.
4. **State the contract in a test** next to `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`, which already drives `assistant.response.started` with `responseId: "r1"/"r2"` at `:225-231` and `:255-262`, but asserts only event order (`:239-245`, `:721`), never what lands on the completion record.

## 8. Relation to existing reports (why this is filed separately)

- **[#710] / PR #711** (closed, merged `84c81b80`) fixed the **desktop display layer** for response events — 4 files under `apps/desktop/`, no server-side change. Neither `native-agent/versioning.ts` nor `agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts` appears in it.
- **[#978]** mentions `assistant.response.started` only while enumerating events of a stuck run; no attribution claim.
- Searching all 469 current issues and their comments: `response_start` = **0 hits**, `currentTurn` = **0 hits**. Nothing on record describes this correlation.
- **#1125** and **#1128** are about Artifact provenance reconcile and delegated-child terminal state respectively — different subsystems.
- Open PRs touching candidate-adjacent files: #311 and #965 edit `agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` (`+4` and `+32/-8`), so line numbers in §4.2 may shift; **no open PR touches `versioning.ts` or `jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts`**, i.e. nothing in flight fixes this.
- No action on any of those issues is requested here.

## 9. Version this was measured against

- SD `main`: `f0efd382e5e79260386ce89674eef7af1bbc05a9` (2026-11-12T08:49:00Z).
- `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts` sha256 `7e9be52faf60a667e96692ef2030f14b704e129c2d8998c680e069007008896d`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts` sha256 `ae61b67aa5bfab0165743818d3606cec21b0992754c9cfb31a8d37ee6d6487d7`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/recording-wait.ts` sha256 `4b9530f167e3d2b9f88fafa42279a6c8e944d8a083499c60c2397b460556ec53`.
- Run records: existing data volume, read-only.

## 10. What this report does and does not establish

**Established (CONFIRMED):** the correlation is carried in one mutable field, written synchronously and read from the queue, with two queue-side clearing points and no per-call binding; and 54 of 303 completion records in four real runs lost an identity that had been issued.

**Not established (NEEDS MORE EVIDENCE):** the opposite failure mode — a completion stamped with a *neighbouring* call's id. It is structurally possible for the same reason the loss is, but it is **not observable in this data**, and one check that looks like it would catch it does not: "does a completion carry an id belonging to a different turn's started record?" returned **0 rows in all four runs**, because both records take their turn from the same counter (`jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts:216-218`), so a mis-bound id still agrees with its neighbour by turn. Separating "dropped" from "mis-bound" needs a run with timing instrumentation (e.g. logging the field value at set, clear and read for one turn), which was out of scope here.

**Inherited, not re-derived:** the 11 "no started record at that turn" rows were sub-classified in an earlier analysis as 2 genuinely unstarted plus 9 compaction-driven. This pass reproduced the 65 = 54 + 11 partition only; the 2/9 split was not recomputed and is not relied on above.

## Problem

The nightly real journey `J5` (shard `research-9`) failed with `locator.click: Test timeout of 600000ms exceeded` while reading the run timeline. Playwright had already resolved the first `details.timeline-disclosure.tool` summary, but the element never became visible and 1049 click retries consumed the whole test budget.

## Cause

A live run folds adjacent exploration steps into a collapsed `<details class="timeline-exploration">` (`apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx`). Whether that wrapper exists depends on the tool sequence the model happens to produce, which a journey does not pin. `test/helpers/journeys.ts` expanded only the tool card itself, so a card nested in a closed group stayed invisible.

The trigger is model-dependent, which is why it is intermittent: reruns on a local model that only called `run_shell` passed 4/4 and produced no exploration group.

A second gap surfaced in review: the region name is localized, and the two `zh-CN` journeys that call `expandToolStep` resolved zero regions, so the expansion was a silent no-op there.

## Fix

PR #735 expands the timeline's own grouping containers before reading or locating tool cards, matches both UI locales (`Agent activity` / `Agent 活动`), and caps a card-summary click at 30s so a future timeline layout change fails fast with an attributable visibility error instead of spending the 600s test budget.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `J5` passes repeatedly against the nightly model, including runs that produce exploration tool steps.
- [ ] `journey-first-run` and `journey-artifact-archive` (`zh-CN`) still expand and read tool steps.
- [ ] A timeline layout change fails a journey in seconds with a visibility error, not in 600s.

## Evidence

- Nightly failure: first summary resolved, `element is not visible`, 1049 retries, 600s timeout.
- Local DOM probe with the same structure: the nested summary is invisible while the group is closed, and expands/clickable after the group is opened.
- Local reruns on the helper: `research-9` planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1, twice (1.1m, 2.5m).

Refs #735
closed_recent.title: Nightly J5 can hang for 600s when a live run groups its exploration steps

closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The CI today is a cumulative gate model: PRs run L1/L2, the merge group runs L3, the nightly runs L4 and a release runs L5 (see the header comment of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). As the suite grows, three engineering capabilities have to be built in step:

1. **Test coverage**: the Coverage job merges only the UT and ST layers, the mocked browser E2E is not measured, and no gate reads the published coverage as an admission threshold.
2. **CI stability**: real-model E2E (L3/L4/L5) depends on external services and credentials, and occasional failures have no systematic mechanism for flake identification, isolation and tracking.
3. **Release CI efficiency**: the L5 release pipeline has no end-to-end budget of <5 hours, and the bulk data downloads (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install, dependencies, datasets) happen again on every run.

Related files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the L1–L5 pipeline: policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e jobs)
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` (real E2E; `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the L5 release)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (the case catalog and profile selection)
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`, `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy and result summaries)
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` (coverage merge and summary)

## Design Ideas

### 1. Test coverage

**Baseline** — the `releases/v0.3.0.beta` line, authoritative run at `6d3c49a`:

| metric | whole repo | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lines | 73.11% (105840/144777) | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| branches | 63.59% (39639/62335) | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| functions | 81.43% (7208/8852) | 81.43% | — |

- Weakest modules by line coverage: `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `scripts` 63.49%, `artifact-json` 63.16%, `specialist` 68.51%, `gateway` 68.40%.
- Cases: 3934 tagged — UT 3694/3806, ST 2/4, E2E 69/124; real-model 0/16, LLM judge 0/8, external 0/89, legacy 0/42.

**Gaps**

- Coverage is display-only: no gate reads it, and the `external` / `real` / `llm` classes are permanently 0.

**Plan**

1. Gate on industry health lines rather than the current 73%:

| metric | healthy | excellent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| branches | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| functions (Node) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| statements | ≥80% | — |
| new / changed code (diff on a PR) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| core paths (auth, sandbox execution, gateway, API routes) | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| per-package floor | ≥60% | — |

2. Land it in that order: diff coverage is enforced immediately (new code meets the line, existing code is not blocked), and the whole-repo figure ratchets upward and may never fall.

3. Starting gap: lines 73.11% (−6.89pt), branches 63.59% (−6.41pt), functions 81.43% (already passing). Four packages sit below the 60% floor — `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `services/runner` 0% — and each gets its own raise target.

4. Case-level coverage, not just a case count: a profile is the gate tier a run resolves to (`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`), and `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` states which tag combinations each one selects. Today the 16 real-model, 8 LLM-judge and 89 external cases are selected by no profile at all, so they never run and read 0 forever; every case must either be selected by a profile or explicitly marked out of scope in the tag catalog, so the omission surfaces at review time.

5. Tie cases to modules: the tagged catalog carries the case-to-module mapping, so a new module without an executing case fails the gate, and `planned / executed / passed` remains the execution view beside it.

**Cases no profile can ever select.** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` defines every profile as one of five rules (L1/L2 hermetic, L3/L4/L5 real), so a tag combination outside those rules never runs. On the `main` catalog (359 cases), 45 are permanently dead:

| tag shape | why no rule matches | cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic accepts only `reviewed`; real only `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | same, with no path back in | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | the real rule is pinned to `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | all five rules require `npu:none` | 1 |

Four more shapes are structurally dead and simply have no case yet: `os:macos` / `os:windows`, `arch:arm64` outside real e2e, `judge:llm` combined with `model:none` / `mock`, and any case missing a `tier` tag — the old release-line catalog has no tier dimension, so under today's policy it would match nothing at all.

A further 131 cases read 0 without being dead: 61 UT and 70 real e2e do run, but the `ut` and `e2e-real` slice catalogs are never uploaded (`slices` registers only `e2e` and `st`), so their execution cannot be attributed.

- Fix the 45: delete or migrate the 42 `legacy` cases, give `quarantined` an exit, retag `st` + `real` as `e2e` or mark it out of scope, and open a separate NPU tier or declare it unsupported.
- Reachability check in the catalog check (`ci:catalog:check`, reusing the rule union exported by `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`): a case whose tags match no profile fails catalog generation, so a dead case is caught at review time instead of reading 0 for months.

### 2. CI stability

- Automatic failure classification: product defect / environment / external dependency / test flake.
- Flake governance: when a case's failure rate over its last N runs crosses a threshold, mark it quarantined automatically — it keeps running and recording results, but its failure no longer blocks merges, and a tracking issue is opened for the owner. It leaves quarantine once it passes N consecutive runs, so a flaky case neither freezes the queue nor silently disappears.
- No blanket retry. A case is rerun only when its failure is attributable to network jitter or an unstable gateway / upstream — connect and read timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, HTTP 429/5xx, interrupted streams. Every other failure, including a flaky real-model case, is reported as it happened and handled by the classification and quarantine above. A retry is labelled as an infrastructure retry, its count is visible per case, and sustained gateway failures beyond the retry budget are reported as an infrastructure incident rather than a test failure.
- Explore disabling the model's thinking mode, or setting the reasoning effort to its lowest level: much of the flakiness of the real-model cases comes from the randomness of the reasoning path; disabling or minimizing thinking narrows the output variance, makes the results more reproducible, and shortens per-case inference time (an efficiency win as well). The conclusion has to be backed by an A/B experiment — run both configurations N times each, compare pass rates and failure variance; if the pass rate does not regress beyond the accepted bound, fix it as a CI-only inference configuration applied to the L3/L4/L5 journeys only, leaving the product default untouched.

### 3. Release CI efficiency (<5h)

- Give the L5 pipeline a 5-hour end-to-end budget, add a timing view of actual per-job duration against that budget, and alert automatically when it is exceeded.
- Compress duration through caching (pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm are cached already), parallel test sharding (the mocked E2E matrix exists; extend it to UT/ST), and trimming redundant layers from the release profile.
- Run the real-model journeys at the lowest thinking effort: thinking off, or reasoning effort at its minimum, for L3/L4/L5 — reasoning tokens are the dominant cost of a case, so this shortens per-case latency directly. It is the same A/B switch as the stability item; here it is measured as p50/p95 duration per case against the 5-hour budget and fixed once the pass rate shows no regression.
- Data-download optimization: inventory the bulk downloads in the pipeline (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install with its virtualenv, pnpm / uv dependencies, test datasets and fixtures, model and sidecar data, Docker images, and the base images of the release binaries) and eliminate the repeated ones item by item — pre-download into `actions/cache`, use an internal mirror / CDN, prefetch in parallel with the build steps, and key the cache on lockfiles / content hashes. Track download time separately in the budget view; a rerun with a cache hit must not download the bulk again.
- Produce an L5 duration baseline report marking the top-N slowest jobs and the optimization suggestions (including the share of download time).

## Involved Public APIs

No new or changed product public APIs; all of this is CI-internal capability.

- Reuse the existing CI-internal interfaces: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...` (case selection), the `.ci-results` directory layout, and the `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs of `real-e2e.yml`.
- The new outputs (coverage report and duration baseline report) are uploaded as artifacts, following the existing artifact naming convention (e.g. `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`).

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.ci/` scripts: the policy, matrix and summary scripts are extended to emit coverage and timing data.
- `test/support/tagged`: the case catalog gains coverage-ownership and flake-marker fields.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`: a wider merge scope and a new output format.
- `release.yml`: the L5 budget check hooks into the existing `workflow_call` chain.
- No product code changes (apps/*, services/*); the model thinking-mode configuration is injected through the CI / E2E harness only and does not touch product defaults.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Coverage**: with a change of a known coverage delta, verify that the PR comment and the threshold block trigger correctly; verify the numbers are sound once the E2E layer is included.
- **Stability**: on a test branch, produce deterministic failures and random failures, and verify the classification, the quarantine isolation and the auto-issue flow; inject network jitter and gateway failures (timeout, connection reset, 429/5xx, interrupted stream) and verify the case is retried and, when it then passes, recorded as a pass with a visible retry count, while a product-defect failure is not retried; run the thinking-mode A/B experiment N times per arm, and verify that the failure variance narrows with no unacceptable pass-rate regression.
- **Efficiency**: take the last 3 release runs as the baseline, verify that the budget view times correctly and that the L5 end-to-end is <5 hours after the optimization; verify that the bulk data downloads take near-zero time on a cache hit; and record the per-case p50/p95 duration with thinking off or at its lowest, before and after.
- All of the above is CI behavior and automatable within L2; no new real-model cases are added (the existing L4/L5 journeys are reused).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Coverage is gated on the industry health lines: whole-repo lines ≥80%, branches ≥70%, functions ≥80% and statements ≥80%; new code ≥80% diff coverage; each package ≥60% and core paths ≥90%.
- [ ] Case-level coverage is closed: no case sits outside every profile, and every module maps to at least one case the gating profile actually executes.
- [ ] Flaky cases are identified and quarantined automatically; only failures caused by network jitter or an unstable gateway are retried, labelled as infrastructure retries and never applied to product defects; the thinking-mode (off / lowest) A/B experiment is concluded and, if viable, fixed as a CI-only inference configuration.
- [ ] The L5 release CI finishes end-to-end in <5 hours with in-pipeline over-budget alerts, every bulk download is cache/prefetch managed with no re-download on a cache hit, and the real-model journeys run at the lowest thinking effort with the latency gain recorded.

## Additional Information

- This is an engineering-effectiveness request; maintainers are invited to schedule it as the three sub-items above.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

当前 CI 采用累积门禁模型：PR 跑 L1/L2，merge_group 跑 L3，nightly 跑 L4，发布跑 L5（见 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 头部注释）。随着用例规模增长，三个方面的工程能力需要同步建设：

1. **用例覆盖度**：Coverage 任务只合并 UT、ST 两层，mocked browser E2E 未被度量，且没有任何门禁把已发布的覆盖度作为准入阈值。
2. **CI 稳定性**：真实模型 E2E（L3/L4/L5）依赖外部服务与凭据，偶发失败缺乏系统性的抖动识别、隔离与跟踪机制。
3. **版本 CI 效率**：L5 发布流水线尚无 <5 小时的端到端时长预算约束，大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB、依赖、数据集）在每次运行中反复发生。

相关文件：

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`（L1–L5 主流水线：policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e 等 job）
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`（真实 E2E；`profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入）
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`（L5 发布）
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`（用例目录与 profile 选择）
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`、`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`、`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`（策略与结果汇总）
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`（覆盖度合并与摘要）

## 设计思路

### 1. 用例覆盖度

**基线**——取 `releases/v0.3.0.beta` 线（authoritative，SHA `6d3c49a`）：

| 指标 | 整仓 | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 行 | 73.11%（105840/144777） | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| 分支 | 63.59%（39639/62335） | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| 函数 | 81.43%（7208/8852） | 81.43% | — |

- 行覆盖率最弱的模块：`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`scripts` 63.49%、`artifact-json` 63.16%、`specialist` 68.51%、`gateway` 68.40%。
- 用例：3934 个，UT 覆盖 3694/3806、ST 2/4、E2E 69/124；真实模型 0/16、LLM judge 0/8、external 0/89、legacy 0/42。

**问题**

- 覆盖度只用于展示，没有任何门禁读取；`external` / `real` / `llm` 三类用例恒为 0。

**方案**

1. 门禁取业界健康线，而不是当前的 73%：

| 指标 | 健康线 | 优秀线 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 行覆盖 | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 分支覆盖 | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| 函数覆盖（Node） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 语句覆盖 | ≥80% | — |
| 新增/变更代码（PR diff） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 核心链路（认证、沙箱执行、网关、API 路由） | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| 单包下限 | ≥60% | — |

2. 按上述顺序落地：diff 覆盖立即生效（新代码按健康线走，不阻塞存量），整仓数值以棘轮方式只升不降。

3. 当前差距：行 73.11%（差 6.89pt）、分支 63.59%（差 6.41pt）、函数 81.43%（已达标）。4 个包低于 60% 下限——`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`services/runner` 0%——各自设定提升目标。

4. 用例维度覆盖，而不只是用例数量：profile 是一次运行解析出的门禁档位（`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`），具体选中哪些 tag 组合由 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 定义。目前 16 个真实模型、8 个 LLM judge、89 个 external 用例不被任何 profile 选中，等于永远不跑、永远显示 0；要求每条用例要么被某个 profile 选中，要么在 tag 目录中显式标注「不在范围」，让遗漏在评审阶段就暴露。

5. 用例与模块绑定：tag 目录维护「用例 → 模块」映射，新增模块若没有可执行用例则门禁失败；`planned / executed / passed` 作为与之并列的执行视图。

**永远不会被任何 profile 选中的用例。** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 把每个 profile 定义为五条规则之一（L1/L2 hermetic、L3/L4/L5 real），不符合这些规则的 tag 组合永远不会被执行。以 `main` 目录（359 条）为例，45 条是彻底死用例：

| tag 形态 | 为何无规则命中 | 条数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic 只收 `reviewed`，real 只收 `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | 同上，且没有回到门禁的路径 | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | real 规则硬编码 `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | 五条规则全部要求 `npu:none` | 1 |

另有四类结构性死角，目前恰好没有对应用例：`os:macos` / `os:windows`、非 real e2e 的 `arch:arm64`、`judge:llm` 搭配 `model:none` / `mock`，以及任何缺少 `tier` 标签的用例——release 线那份旧目录没有 tier 维度，按当前策略会全部失配。

还有 131 条显示为 0 但并不属于死用例：61 条 UT 与 70 条 real e2e 实际在跑，只是 `ut` 与 `e2e-real` 两个切片的 catalog 从未上传（`slices` 只登记了 `e2e` 和 `st`），导致执行结果无法归因。

- 处置 45 条：删除或迁移 42 条 `legacy`；为 `quarantined` 补上出口；`st` + `real` 改 tag 为 `e2e` 或标注不在范围；`npu` 单独开档位或声明不支持。
- 在 catalog 校验（`ci:catalog:check`，复用 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 导出的规则并集）中增加可达性检查：用例 tag 若不属于任何 profile，catalog 生成即失败，让死用例在评审阶段暴露，而不是显示 0 数月。

### 2. CI 稳定性提升

- 失败自动归类：产品缺陷 / 环境 / 外部依赖 / 用例抖动（flake）。
- 抖动治理（quarantine）：同一用例近 N 次运行失败率超阈值时自动标记为隔离——它继续运行并记录结果，但失败不再阻断合并，同时自动创建跟踪 issue 派给 owner；连续 N 次通过后自动解除隔离，既不冻结合并队列，也不会让用例悄悄消失。
- 不做统一重试。仅当失败可归因于网络抖动或网关、上游不稳定（连接与读取超时、连接重置、DNS 失败、HTTP 429/5xx、流中断）时才自动重跑；其他失败——包括真实模型用例本身的抖动——如实上报，交由上面的失败归类与 quarantine 处理。重试会标注为基础设施重试，用例维度可看到次数，超出重试预算的持续性网关失败按基础设施故障上报，而不是记为用例失败。
- 探索关闭或调低模型思考模式（thinking / reasoning effort 设为最低档）：真实模型用例的抖动很大程度来自推理路径的随机性，关闭/调低思考模式可收窄输出方差、提升可复现性，同时缩短单用例推理耗时（兼具效率收益）。结论需以 A/B 实验数据支撑：对比开启 vs 关闭（或最低档）两组各 N 次运行的通过率与失败方差，若通过率无可接受退化，则固化为 CI 专用推理配置，仅作用于 L3/L4/L5 journey，不影响产品默认行为。

### 3. 版本 CI 效率提升（<5hr）

- 为 L5 流水线定义端到端时长预算 5 小时，pipeline 内增加各 job 实际耗时 vs 预算的计时看板，超预算自动告警。
- 通过缓存（pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm 已有）、用例分片并行（mocked E2E matrix 已具备，推广到 UT/ST）、release profile 裁剪冗余层级来压缩时长。
- 真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行：L3/L4/L5 关闭思考或把 reasoning effort 调到最低——推理 token 是单个用例的主要开销，这一步直接缩短单用例耗时。与稳定性项共用同一组 A/B 开关，这里以每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对照 5 小时预算衡量，确认通过率无退化后固化。
- 数据下载优化：盘点流水线中的大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB 及其 virtualenv、pnpm / uv 依赖、测试数据集与 fixture、模型与 sidecar 数据、Docker 镜像、二进制基础镜像），逐项消除重复下载——预下载进 `actions/cache`、走内部镜像源 / CDN、与构建步骤并行预取、按 lockfile / 内容寻址命中缓存；下载耗时单独计时并纳入预算看板，缓存命中后的重复运行不应再产生大额下载。
- 输出 L5 耗时基线报告，标注 top-N 耗时 job 与优化建议（含下载耗时占比）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增、不修改产品公共 API；全部为 CI 内部能力。

- 复用现有 CI 内部接口：`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...`（用例选择）、`.ci-results` 结果目录格式、`real-e2e.yml` 的 `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入。
- 新增产物（覆盖度报告、耗时基线报告）统一作为 artifacts 上传，遵循现有 artifact 命名约定（如 `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`）。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `.ci/` 脚本：策略、矩阵、汇总脚本需扩展以输出覆盖度与耗时数据。
- `test/support/tagged`：用例目录需补充覆盖度归属与抖动标记字段。
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`：扩展合并范围与输出格式。
- `release.yml`：L5 预算检查嵌入现有 `workflow_call` 链。
- 不改动产品代码（apps/*、services/*）；模型思考模式配置仅通过 CI / E2E harness 注入，不影响产品默认行为。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **覆盖度**：构造已知覆盖变化的变更，验证 PR 评论与阈值拦截正确触发；验证 E2E 层纳入后报告数值合理。
- **稳定性**：在测试分支制造确定性失败与随机失败，验证分类、quarantine 隔离与自动建单流程；注入网络抖动与网关失败（超时、连接重置、429/5xx、流中断），验证用例被自动重试、重试后通过则记为通过且重试次数可见，而产品缺陷类失败不触发重试；思考模式 A/B 实验两组各跑 N 次，验证关闭/最低档下失败方差收窄且通过率无可接受退化。
- **效率**：以最近 3 次 release 运行作为基线，验证预算看板计时准确，优化后 L5 端到端 <5 小时；验证缓存命中后大额数据下载耗时趋近于零；记录关闭/最低思考强度前后每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对比。
- 上述验证均为 CI 自身行为，属于 L2 可自动化校验范围；不新增真实模型用例（复用现有 L4/L5 journey）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 覆盖度按业界健康线设门禁：整仓行 ≥80%、分支 ≥70%、函数 ≥80%、语句 ≥80%；新代码 diff 覆盖 ≥80%；单包 ≥60%、核心链路 ≥90%。
- [ ] 用例维度覆盖闭环：没有用例落在所有 profile 之外，每个模块都至少映射到一个门禁 profile 实际执行的用例。
- [ ] CI 具备抖动用例自动识别与 quarantine 机制；仅网络抖动 / 网关不稳定导致的失败自动重试，标注为基础设施重试且不适用于产品缺陷；完成模型思考模式（关闭/最低档）A/B 实验并形成结论，可行则固化为 CI 专用推理配置。
- [ ] L5 版本 CI 端到端时长 <5 小时，流水线内有超预算告警；大额数据下载全部纳入缓存/预下载管理，缓存命中后无冗余下载；真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行并记录耗时收益。

## 补充信息

- 本 issue 为工程效能类需求，建议 maintainer 按三个子项拆分任务排期。

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Issue #817 defined four acceptance criteria across three CI engineering capabilities: test coverage gating, CI stability, and release CI efficiency (`<5h`). Three pull requests have since landed on `main`:

- **PR #951** (`2c33bc5017`): migrated 11 previously unscheduled Playwright specs (41 case identities) onto the shared PR plan (`L2` mocked E2E) and removed the `legacy` Playwright project (`status:legacy`, `ci:e2e:legacy`, `test:legacy*`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY`).
- **PR #940** (`360e6b664f`): preserved `reasoning_effort: low` across Evolve and search paths, added bounded upstream transport retries (502/503/504/524 and mid-stream socket resets) for streaming model completions, and configured Nightly model and judge calls to run with `low` effort in `nightly-research` with a 75-minute research-team timeout.
- **PR #971** (`1db615cdd2`): narrowed the active BiomniBench-DA L5 execution set from 50 to 45 cases (64 total real L5 cases), pinned Biomni generator and rubric judge thinking to `enabled` with `low` effort, scaled additive resource baselines by `45/50`, and recovered `da-11-1` when a stream ends cleanly inside truncated tool-call JSON.

### Audit of #817 Acceptance Criteria on Current `main`

Measured against the latest completed `main` CI run [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`) and recent L5 / Release runs:

#### 1. Coverage thresholds and gating
- **1.1 Coverage gate enforcement**: **Not met** — `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` and `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` remain informational only (`Coverage is informational. No minimum percentage is enforced`), and the Coverage job still merges only `ut` and `st` (mocked browser E2E is not measured).
- **1.2 Whole-repo line coverage ≥80%**: **Met** — **80.82%** (`203,344 / 251,596`; Node.js `81.18%`, Python `73.93%`, up from the `73.11%` baseline at `6d3c49a`).
- **1.3 Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**: **Not met** — **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`; Node.js `59.80%`, Python `62.06%`), **10.14 percentage points** below the `70%` target.
- **1.4 Function coverage ≥80%**: **Met (Node.js)** — **80.08%** (`13,142 / 16,411`; Python function coverage is not separately reported).
- **1.5 Statement coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — `summary.json` reports `lines`, `branches`, and `functions` only.
- **1.6 New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — no PR diff coverage calculation, summary comment, or gate check exists in CI.
- **1.7 Per-package coverage floor ≥60%**: **Partially met** — `apps/web` (`62.89%`) and Node `services/runner` (`88.55%`) now exceed `60%`, while `packages/idea-tree` (`45.94%`), `packages/schema` (`57.89%`), and Python `services/runner` (`0%`) remain below `60%`.
- **1.8 Core-path coverage ≥90%**: **Partially met** — `services/api` (`94.84%`), `packages/sandbox-capability` (`100%`), and `packages/model` (`96.48%`) exceed `90%` line coverage, while `services/gateway` (`75.23%`) and `services/runner` (`88.55%`) are below `90%`, and no dedicated core-path gate is enforced.

#### 2. Case-level profile and module coverage
- **2.1 No case outside every profile**: **Partially met** — PR #951 eliminated all 42 `status:legacy` dead cases by moving 41 valid browser identities into the `pr` (`L2`) profile. Remaining cases outside `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` rules are 79 `status:external` UT/ST cases, 1 `status:quarantined` case (`test/literature-review.spec.ts`), 1 `npu:required` case, 1 `category:st + model:real` case, and 6 `os:macos` cases; `ci:catalog:check` does not yet fail on profile-unreachable tags.
- **2.2 Every module mapped to an executing gating case**: **Not implemented** — the tagged catalog does not yet carry an explicit case-to-module ownership mapping or fail when a module has no executing case.

#### 3. CI stability and flake governance
- **3.1 Automated flake identification and quarantine**: **Not implemented** — no rolling failure-rate detector, automatic quarantine transition, or tracking-issue workflow is in place.
- **3.2 Infrastructure-only retries for network/gateway faults**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 implemented bounded transport/stream retries and clean-EOF tool-argument recovery without retrying product defects, but per-case infrastructure retry counts and gateway-outage separation are not yet surfaced in the CI summary.
- **3.3 Thinking-mode (`low` / off) A/B experiment and CI configuration**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 pinned Nightly and Biomni L5 runs to `reasoning_effort: low` without changing product defaults, while a formal multi-run A/B pass-rate and variance comparison report remains open.

#### 4. Release CI efficiency (`<5h`)
- **4.1 L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**: **Not met** — after PR #971 landed, the `main` L5 run [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`l5 · parallel=4 · nightly-research`) ran for **15h 39m** (2026-11-07 14:13Z to 2026-11-08 05:52Z, failed); prior branch L5 runs [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) and [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) took **8h 49m** and **7h 30m**; the latest `Release` workflow run [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) took **25h 01m**.
- **4.2 In-pipeline duration budget tracking and over-budget alerts**: **Not implemented** — no 5-hour budget table or alert check is wired into `release.yml` or `ci.yml`.
- **4.3 Bulk data downloads managed via cache/prefetch with zero redundant downloads on cache hit**: **Not implemented** — bulk downloads across jobs are not yet uniformly cached/prefetched and timed against the budget.
- **4.4 Real-model journeys running at lowest thinking effort with latency gain recorded**: **Partially met** — `low` effort is active for Nightly and Biomni L5, but before/after per-case p50/p95 latency gain reports have not been published.

---

### Scope of Follow-up Work Tracked by This Issue

Based on the audit above, the following four deliverables require continued development:

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70% (Item 1.3)**: raise combined Node.js + Python branch coverage from the current **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`) to **≥70%**, and enforce the threshold in CI.
2. **New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80% (Item 1.6)**: compute diff coverage on pull requests against the merge base and enforce a **≥80%** diff coverage gate on executable changed lines/branches in CI.
3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours (Item 4.1)**: reduce full L5 release pipeline wall-clock duration to **<5 hours**, with per-job budget accounting and over-budget alerts in the pipeline summary.
4. **Cache/prefetch management for all bulk data downloads with zero redundant downloads on cache hit (Item 4.3)**: audit and cache/prefetch all bulk downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm ~1.5 GB runtime and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets and fixtures, model/sidecar assets, and container/base images), record download duration separately, and eliminate repeat bulk downloads when caches hit.

## Design Ideas

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**:
   - Prioritize packages with the largest uncovered branch mass in `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json` (such as `services/api` at `54.79%` branches, `packages/workspace` at `55.72%`, `packages/artifact-manager` at `56.63%`, `services/gateway` at `57.22%`, `services/memory-graph` at `56.95%`, and `apps/web` at `70.73%`).
   - Add targeted unit and system tests for error branches, boundary guards, and fallback paths, and wire the `≥70%` branch threshold into `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` / `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`.

2. **PR diff coverage ≥80%**:
   - Extend `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` (or add a dedicated diff-coverage step in the `Coverage` job) to intersect `git diff <base>...<head>` hunk lines with merged LCOV / JSON coverage records from Node.js (`ut` + `st`) and Python (`coverage.py`).
   - Publish a clear per-file diff coverage table in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and fail the `Coverage` / `merge-gate` check when changed executable lines fall below `80%`.

3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**:
   - Add per-job wall-clock and phase timing (setup/download vs. execution) to the L5 summary and enforce a `<5h` (`18,000s`) end-to-end budget check.
   - Combine shard parallelism tuning, long-tail case timeout/step-budget tightening, and deduplication of overlapping lower-tier work in the release profile so the end-to-end critical path stays under 5 hours.

4. **Bulk data download caching and prefetching**:
   - Inventory every multi-hundred-megabyte download across `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `real-e2e.yml`, and `release.yml` (JiuwenSwarm bundle and Python virtualenvs, Node/pnpm stores, benchmark datasets/fixtures, browser binaries, and Docker layers).
   - Key caches by lockfile/manifest content hashes, warm them once in an upstream setup step or shared cache entry, and log cache-hit status plus download byte/time metrics in each job summary so cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.

## Involved Public APIs

None. All changes are internal to CI workflows, coverage reporting/gating scripts, and test suites; no product HTTP, CLI, or SDK APIs are added or modified.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`: coverage gating, bulk-download cache orchestration, and L5 duration budget reporting.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`, `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`: whole-repo branch coverage gate (`≥70%`) and PR diff coverage calculation/gate (`≥80%`).
- `packages/*`, `services/*`, `apps/*` test suites: branch coverage additions to lift whole-repo branch coverage from `59.86%` to `≥70%`.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Branch coverage ≥70%**: run `pnpm test:shared` with coverage enabled and `node scripts/coverage-report.mjs`; verify merged whole-repo branch coverage is `≥70.00%` and that lowering the threshold or dropping coverage causes the gate script unit tests to fail.
- **PR diff coverage ≥80%**: add unit tests for the diff-coverage calculator covering added, modified, deleted, and non-executable files, plus a synthetic PR diff below and above `80%` to verify both the step summary table and non-zero exit code on failure.
- **L5 <5h and bulk download caching**: verify on consecutive CI / L5 runs that cache-hit jobs report `cache-hit: true` with near-zero download time for JiuwenSwarm, dependencies, and datasets, that the pipeline summary outputs the job timing breakdown against the 5-hour budget, and that the end-to-end L5 run completes in `<5 hours`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Merged whole-repo branch coverage (`Node.js + Python` across `ut` + `st`) reaches **≥70.00%** (up from `59.86%`), and the CI coverage gate fails if whole-repo branch coverage drops below `70%`.
- [ ] Pull request CI computes diff coverage on changed executable lines against the PR base and fails the gate when PR diff coverage is below **80.00%**, with the per-file diff breakdown rendered in the job summary.
- [ ] All bulk data downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm install and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets/fixtures, and runtime assets) are managed through content-addressed cache/prefetch steps, download duration is measured separately, and cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.
- [ ] The L5 release CI pipeline finishes end-to-end in **<5 hours** (`<300 minutes`) and publishes a per-job duration vs. budget summary with automatic over-budget alerting.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

- Parent tracking issue: #817
- Related merged PRs: #940, #951, #971
- Reference CI runs audited:
  - `main` coverage run: [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`)
  - L5 runs: [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`15h 39m`), [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) (`8h 49m`), [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) (`7h 30m`)
  - Release run: [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) (`25h 01m`)

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
### Background

ScienceDiscovery does not have a recognizable product icon.

The browser tab has a title and no favicon. `apps/web/index.html` has no `rel="icon"` in `<head>`, so the product is indistinguishable from a generic page among bookmarks and tabs.

The in-app brand mark is a generic flask outline (`BrandIcon` in `apps/web/src/icons.tsx`) on an accent square. It fills the slot, but it is not a mark for this product, and it does not read at a 16px tab or bookmark size.

The README opens with a text title and a UI animation. It has no product mark.

### Expected

One product icon, the same mark in all of these places:

1. Browser favicon (at least 16×16 and 32×32, legible on both light and dark tab bars).
2. The in-app brand slot (today’s `.brand-mark`), replacing the generic flask outline.
3. The top of the English and Chinese READMEs, as a product mark. It does not replace the existing UI animation.

The mark has to stay recognizable at small sizes. Do not rely on hairline strokes alone. The drawing, colors, and whether it includes a wordmark are not decided here; this issue does not pre-select a design.

### Out of scope

- The icon is not a control that opens settings.
- The product name and copy stay as they are.
- A desktop or installer icon, if one is needed, belongs with [#34](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/34) (a native desktop window). It does not block the favicon and the in-app mark.

### Acceptance

- [ ] After opening the local web app, the browser tab shows the product icon, not the browser’s default page icon.
- [ ] The sidebar brand slot uses the same mark, not the generic flask outline.
- [ ] The English and Chinese READMEs show the same mark at the top, and the existing UI animation remains.
- [ ] The small icon stays legible on a light UI and on a dark system tab bar.
- [ ] The icon ships in the repository (for example an SVG source plus the small favicon sizes). It does not depend on an external URL.

### Environment

Against current `main` of `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`: `apps/web/index.html` has no favicon, and `BrandIcon` is a flask outline.
closed_recent.title: [Feature] Give ScienceDiscovery a recognizable product icon
