closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
## 1. Problem description

When an Artifact version is materialized into a session workspace, the platform records a provenance
revision carrying the attribution: `origin: "system"`, `contentHash`, `artifactVersionIds: [version]`,
`publicationSequence`, `originMeta.kind: "artifact-materialization"`.

That revision is registered with a **wall-clock** `modifiedAt` (`new Date()`), while the file on disk
keeps its real mtime — and when the bytes already exist, the copy step returns early without touching
the file at all. The next workspace listing compares the recorded `modifiedAt` against `stat` and finds
them unequal, so it decides the file changed and appends a **new** revision built by
`reconcileWorkspaceFiles` that carries none of those fields (`origin: "unknown"`, no `contentHash`, no
`publicationSequence`, `artifactVersionIds: []`) — then points `currentRevisionId` at it.

Net effect: a listing refresh reduces the recorded attribution of an unchanged file. The delivered file
is still there and still correct; what is lost is the record of *who produced it and which Artifact
version it is*.

## 2. Minimal reproduction

No data mutation is required to see the mechanism; steps 4-5 are read-only.

    1. In a session, register an Artifact version V whose content bytes already exist at the target
       workspace path (e.g. promote a subagent deliverable that was copied earlier, or re-materialize
       the same version).
    2. Call materializeArtifact / the materialize path so that `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts`
       runs `copyCasToWorkspace({ reuseIdentical: true, ... })` and then
       `recordWorkspaceFileRevision(...)`.
    3. Read the revision row: it has origin="system", a contentHash, artifactVersionIds=[V] and a
       publicationSequence. Its modifiedAt is the clock value taken after the call.
    4. Call anything that lists workspace files — `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/artifacts` reaches
       `readWorkspaceFiles` in `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:106`, which calls
       `store.reconcileWorkspaceFiles(...)` at `:109`. (A run also does this when it emits
       `run.completed`.)
    5. Read the same file's `currentRevisionId` again.

Expected trigger condition: **whenever `reuseIdentical` returns early, or whenever the clock is read
after the write**, the recorded `modifiedAt` cannot equal the file's real mtime, so step 4 always
observes a change.

## 3. Expected vs actual

Expected — either of:
  - the revision that carries the delivery attribution remains the current revision, because a listing
    refresh is not a content change; or
  - if a new revision is appended, it inherits `origin` / `contentHash` / `artifactVersionIds` /
    `publicationSequence` from the revision it supersedes.

Actual — a second revision is appended with only `path`, `size`, `modifiedAt` (from `stat`),
`origin: "unknown"` and `artifactVersionIds: []`, and `record.currentRevisionId` is moved to it.
Consumers that read the current revision — the file listing, `getFileProvenance`, and any audit of
"which run/tool call/artifact version produced this delivered file" — now see an unattributed record.
A listing refresh permanently reduces the recorded attribution of an unchanged file.

## 4. Source location

All line numbers are from `main` = `18fa8353c2e0`.

    a. `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:31-32` — the clock stamp is what breaks the invariant:
           mode: "write", origin: "system", artifactVersionId: version.id,
           contentHash: copied.sha256, size: copied.bytes, modifiedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
       `:34` attaches `originMeta: { kind: "artifact-materialization", ... }`.

    b. `packages/cas/src/workspace-copy.ts:88` — makes the mismatch unconditional for identical bytes:
           if (input.reuseIdentical && existing.size === bytes) { ... return { transferId, bytes, sha256 }; }
       The function returns before the rename/link, so the file's mtime is never refreshed, while
       (a) has just recorded a `modifiedAt` taken after the call.

    c. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:106` and `:109` — the trigger: every file listing runs
       `store.reconcileWorkspaceFiles(...)`. Note `:137-138` in the same file registers with
       `metadata.mtime.toISOString()`, i.e. the correct pattern already exists here.

    d. `services/api/src/store.ts:5167-5168` — the condition that therefore always fires:
           } else if (reconciliationBaseline.get(file.path) === revision.id
             && (revision.modifiedAt !== file.modifiedAt || revision.size !== file.size)) {

    e. `services/api/src/store.ts:5169-5180` — the replacement revision: `artifactVersionIds: []`
       (`:5170`), `origin: "unknown"` (`:5175`), `modifiedAt: file.modifiedAt` (`:5174`), and no
       `contentHash`, no `publicationSequence`, no `runId`/`toolCallId`/`subagentId`/`originMeta`.
       `services/api/src/store.ts:5184` — `record.currentRevisionId = revision.id;` demotes the
       attributed revision to non-current.

    f. Same defect class at `services/api/src/remote-runner.ts:61` —
       `mode: "write", origin: "system", modifiedAt: new Date().toISOString(), size: file.size, contentHash: file.sha256`.

    g. Design-level gap in the vocabulary: `packages/schema/src/session.ts:263-271` enumerates
       `WorkspaceFileOrigin` as agent / mcp-download / remote-compute / subagent / system / tool /
       unknown / upload — there is no promotion or materialization value, and
       `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:376-380` falls back to `"unknown"` for anything it cannot
       classify.

Positive controls inside the same repository (so this is not a global overwrite):

    - `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:386` records `modifiedAt: fileStat.mtime.toISOString()`;
      `services/api/src/subagents/index.ts:174`, `:189` and `:224` likewise use `stat.mtime`. Records
      written through those paths are not demoted.
    - Files written directly by tools keep `origin: "tool"` and a `contentHash` across the same listing
      refreshes (see 5).

## 5. Runtime evidence

Read-only export of all 265 `workspace_file_revisions` rows of the audited instance
(volume `jd-fresh-test_data`, session `2ad3939c…`, run `c48cf34a-810d-4089-b8ca-ae467aa785af`,
executed version pinned by LF-normalized content hash to JD `30178fda77`; `materialize.ts`, `workspace-copy.ts`,
`artifacts/index.ts` and `remote-runner.ts` carry the same blob in SD `807982f0` and, as re-checked this
round, the same lines in live `18fa8353c2e0`).

Verbatim rows for one delivered file (265 revisions exported read-only from `workspace_file_revisions`):

    origin="system"   createdAt=00:41:29.590Z modifiedAt=00:41:29.557Z size=100724
                      contentHash="d0035d0d…" publicationSequence=296 artifactVersionIds=1
                      originMeta.kind="artifact-materialization"
    origin="unknown"  createdAt=00:41:29.603Z modifiedAt=00:41:29.532Z size=100724
                      contentHash=ABSENT publicationSequence=ABSENT artifactVersionIds=0   <== CURRENT

13 ms separate the two registrations. The unknown row's `modifiedAt` (00:41:29.532Z) is the file's real
mtime and is **25 ms earlier** than the `modifiedAt` recorded on the attributed row (00:41:29.557Z),
which is exactly the `new Date()` value from §4a — the discrepancy is arithmetic, not a coincidence.

Population and controls:

    - all 6 delivered files in that run show the chain `['system','unknown']`; current = `unknown`,
      `contentHash` absent, `publicationSequence` absent, `artifactVersionIds` 1 -> 0.
    - control files written by tools (`refs/doi_index.json`, `output/evidence_table.csv`) end their chain
      with `origin="tool"` and `hasHash=true` after the same number of listing refreshes.
    - the attribution existed right up to the promotion: the subagent-private workspace still carried
      6 revisions with `origin="subagent"`, `runId=subagentId`, `toolName="run_shell"`, per-call
      `toolCallId` and `contentHash`, the last at `publicationSequence=886`; the private file record was
      deleted at `01:10:41.794Z` and the promoted copy registered at `01:10:45.339Z`.

What this evidence does NOT prove: it does not show the file content, the Artifact version or the
download path being wrong — the bytes and the artifact record are intact (`contentHash` verified,
registration and read-back both fine). Only the workspace revision's attribution fields are lost.
It also does not measure how often a deployment lists files after promotion; it shows one occurrence
per delivered file in one run, on the delivered population 6/6.

## 6. Impact

    - Every consumer of the current workspace revision: the file listing, `getFileProvenance`, the
      provenance/audit views, and any answer to "which subagent run and which Artifact version produced
      this delivered file".
    - Promotion of Artifact versions into the session workspace (`materializeArtifact`) and remote
      compute deliveries (`remote-runner.ts:61`) — both clock-stamped sites.
    - Deliverables of multi-agent research runs are the visible class: the platform's own attribution for
      a peer-reviewed report degrades to `unknown` while the report itself is untouched, which inverts
      the trust signal for the most-reviewed object in the session.
    - Not affected: files written by tools, by the subagent handoff copy path, or by the recorder path
      (§4 positive controls).
    - JD note (informational, same defect class): the third clock-stamped site in our downstream build is
      `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:510` (workspace transfer commit). Whatever fix
      lands upstream we mirror it; we list it only so the site count is not under-stated.

## 7. Suggested fix direction

Ordered by invasiveness; we have not changed any code.

    (a) In `store.ts:5169-5180`, when the reconcile branch appends a revision, inherit
        `origin`, `contentHash`, `publicationSequence`, `artifactVersionIds` and `originMeta` from the
        revision being superseded. Smallest change, covers every clock-stamped site at once, and cannot
        invent attribution because it only carries forward what was already recorded.

    (b) Prefer a content test over a wall-clock test in `store.ts:5167-5168`: the attributed revision
        already carries `contentHash`, so a listing could treat `size`/digest equality as "no change" and
        skip appending entirely.

    (c) At the write sites (`materialize.ts:32`, `remote-runner.ts:61`), record `stat.mtime` instead of
        `new Date()`, matching `recorder.ts:386` and `subagents/index.ts:174/189/224`. Fixes the instance
        but leaves any future clock-stamped site exposed.

    (d) Add a promotion/materialization value to `WorkspaceFileOrigin`
        (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:263-271`) and stop mapping deliverable classes to `"unknown"` in
        `recorder.ts:376-380`, so the vocabulary can express what these files are.

(a) or (b) is what the observed data argues for: the loss happens in reconcile, not in the write.

## 8. Version note

    - Executed version of the audited instance: pinned by content hash (LF-normalized) to JD `30178fda77`;
      45/45 audited files match that ref, 40 of them also matching SD `807982f0`.
    - Attribution basis: `artifacts/materialize.ts`, `cas/workspace-copy.ts`, `artifacts/index.ts`,
      `remote-runner.ts`, `provenance/recorder.ts` and `runner/readiness.ts` are byte-identical between the
      executed build and SD; `store.ts` differs as a file but the defect lines
      (`:5167-5168`, `:5169-5180`, `:5184` at live main) are present on both sides, and the downstream diff
      hunks lie elsewhere (`:2291`, `:7264+`, `:7307+`, `:7757+`). Hence SD-side framework defect.
    - Re-checked against live `main` = `18fa8353c2e0` on 2026-11-12: all quoted lines still present, and no
      commit on those paths since fixes this (`materialize.ts` and `workspace-copy.ts` last touched by
      `77c6ef3d6` 2026-09-25).
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: A promoted Artifact revision's provenance is silently replaced by an empty origin:"unknown" revision on the next workspace listing

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue. Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 01bed55cb4a442f0b75c584b91b8d861 Branch: dev1/fix/945-desktop-feedback-image-truncation Base: 9871f2dd537a At: 2026-11-06T00:45:51Z ## Summary The desktop shell ships its own copy of the feedback screenshot pipeline, byte-identical to the web one, so the same silent truncation happens there: one multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches only the first 8, the two dropped files disappear, and the dialog says nothing. Web is fixed separately: #942 (fix in PR #943). PR #943's `## Scope` already names this copy and leaves it out: > `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts:116` carries a copy of this function with the same silent cap drop, and its own dialog has the same gap. This change is the `apps/web` face only; the desktop copy is left untouched and needs the same fix, tracked separately. This issue is that separate desktop fix. ## Where it happens (main `9871f2dd`) - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` is the same git blob as the web file: `69a1251` (4981 bytes, sha256 `0b66e24c…` for both). Line 122 is `if (images.length >= FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES) break;` and line 127 returns `{ images }` with no truncation signal. - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx:304-306` — `const result = await prepareFeedbackImages(Array.from(files), images); setImages(result.images); setImageError(result.error);`; `result.error` is `undefined` on this path. - `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx:476` — only `{imageError ?

{fb.images.error[imageError]}

: null}` is rendered, so nothing appears. - The cap is 8 (`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts:40`). It is only stated once the add button is already disabled at the cap (`FeedbackDialog.tsx:447-452` -> `fb.images.limit(FEEDBACK_MAX_IMAGES)`), which never fires for a single over-cap multi-select. - Desktop strings are **not** the web i18n: `apps/desktop/src/text.ts:99` proxies `TEXT` over two dictionaries, and `Text` is `typeof ZH` (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1237`). The image block is `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts:1134-1146` (limit `:1137`) and `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1182-1194` (limit `:1185`). Entries there are function-valued (`limit: (max) => …`), so the new one must be too. ## Steps to reproduce (desktop shell) 1. Open the desktop app's feedback dialog. 2. Click "Upload image" and select 10 PNG/JPEG files in one multi-select. 3. Observe 8 thumbnails and no message; the button then reads "Up to 8 images". 4. Submit; the relayed issue carries 8 images. Expected: a visible notice naming the cap and how many files were dropped, same wording as web: "Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped." Actual: no notice; 2 files vanish. ## Red first (already red on the desktop module) Run through the desktop package's own runner (`apps/desktop/package.json:7` is `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`), against the byte-identical copy of `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` (git blob `69a1251`, sha256 `0b66e24c…`) plus main's `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`, stubbing `createImageBitmap`/canvas/`FileReader`: ``` $ apps/desktop/node_modules/.bin/tsx --test .local/red-desktop/desktop-feedback-images.test.ts not ok 1 - desktop: ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two skipped undefined !== 2 not ok 2 - desktop: two picks under the cap report nothing skipped undefined !== 0 not ok 3 - desktop: one removed then two picked attaches one and reports one skipped undefined !== 1 # pass 0 # fail 3 ``` `images.length` assertions pass; the failing half is exactly the missing truncation signal. Proposed test file `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx`, mirroring the web test in #943: module assertions plus a mounted-dialog assertion (desktop's `react-test-renderer` helper `apps/desktop/tests/support/dom-renderer.ts`) that the hint text appears after an over-cap pick. ## Smallest mergeable slice (Dev-1, desktop face, <= 1 week) 1. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts` — return `skipped: number` next to `images`; count files left when the cap is hit (same shape as PR #943). 2. `apps/desktop/src/feedback/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — hold `skippedImages` in state; render one neutral hint (`className="feedback-hint"`, next to the `preparing` hint at `:475`) when `> 0`, clear it on add/remove/reset. 3. `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` + `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` — add `truncated: (max: number, skipped: number) => string` to the `images` block in both (zh first: `Text = typeof ZH`), same wording as #943. 4. New `apps/desktop/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — the three module assertions above plus the two mounted-dialog directions. No shared-contract or Worker change; web files untouched. ## Acceptance - A1 (must): picking 10 from empty attaches 8 and shows a hint containing "8" and "2" (en) / "8" and "2" (zh). - A2 (must): picking 2 under the cap shows no such hint (negative direction, so a blanket banner does not pass). - A3: with 8 attached, remove one, pick 2 more -> 8 attached and the hint says 1 skipped. - A4: the hint exists in both desktop dictionaries and disappears after a successful submit; wording matches web (#943) so the two shells read the same. ## Dedup - `search/issues` for `desktop feedback`, `feedback-images`, `desktop screenshot`, `desktop attachment`: the only feedback-truncation item is #942 (web, PR #943 open); #879/#880 are the desktop attachment **size unit** surface, unrelated. - No open PR touches any file under `apps/desktop/src/feedback/` or `apps/desktop/src/text/` (checked the desktop PRs whose text matches: #905, #814, #904). - #943's own `## Scope` states the desktop copy is deliberately left out, so this is the tracked follow-up rather than a duplicate. ## Notes - No PR is opened with this issue now: today's new-PR budget is already spent on #941/#943, so the desktop PR queues behind whichever lands on main first. - Opened without labels (our token gets 403 on label writes); triage labels need a maintainer. - Environment: desktop face (`apps/desktop`), no API/base change; base main `9871f2dd537a6f3e3a94a7eb7b5bc67ef717d363`.

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
## 1. Actual behaviour

The Native agent loop emits a usage figure after **every** model turn, and each of those figures is written into the run's persisted record stream. The usage ledger receives **one row per run**, and the token fields of that row are the **last main-agent turn only**.

Measured on one captured session (5 runs, 599 per-turn usage records, 5 ledger rows):

| run | ledger rows | main turns with usage | subagent streams | subagent turns with usage | sum of per-turn input tokens, all streams | input tokens in the ledger row | persisted share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `9ceeb1f9` | 1 | 20 | 5 | 572 | 24,023,894 | 44,952 | 0.1871 % |
| `0673152f` | 1 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 300,115 | 47,387 | 15.7896 % |
| `82036958` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |
| `116b288e` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |
| `de7527c9` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |

Session totals: ledger holds 92,339 input / 12,737 output / 6,592 reasoning / 7,168 cache-read tokens; the same session's streams hold 24,324,009 input / 526,865 output / 404,221 reasoning / 13,340,032 cache-read tokens. **0.3796 % of the input the provider reported for the session is in the ledger.**

Four separate things go wrong, and they compound:

1. **A per-run row carries a per-turn number.** In both runs that have tokens, the row equals one specific turn record byte-for-byte and equals no sum: the matching turn is main turn index 19 of 20 for `9ceeb1f9`, main turn index 6 of 7 for `0673152f` — i.e. the last main turn in each case.
2. **Subagent turns contribute nothing.** `9ceeb1f9` ran 5 children over 572 model turns (5,297,320 + 5,055,291 + 5,267,215 + 5,188,821 + 2,398,037 input tokens) and the ledger has 0 rows for them. 96.62 % of that run's per-turn records belong to children. No `invocationKind` exists for them, and the one `subagent.usage` event per child carries that child's *last* turn, never its sum.
3. **The row's time window and its token figures describe different scopes.** `startedAt`/`finishedAt` come from the prompt manifest (the whole run) while the tokens come from one turn: `9ceeb1f9`'s row spans 2 h 50 min 59 s (02:27:15.507Z → 05:18:14.695Z) and reports 56,382 total tokens, whose turn was recorded 0.753 s before the run closed. Any hours-of-run or cost-per-run figure derived from that row is wrong by construction, not by rounding.
4. **The input to the ledger is not reconstructable from the persisted stream.** No stream file in this session contains a single event of type `model_usage` (0 in `9ceeb1f9` main stream with its 20 model turns; 0 in `0673152f` with 7) even though the ledger value is taken from that channel — see `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` in §3, where the handler returns before publishing. An independent audit therefore cannot recompute the row from what is on disk.

What is *not* claimed here: the three rows with all-null token fields are correct as they stand. Those runs contain no `model.completed` record at all (their main streams hold only `run.queued`, `run.started`, `run.status`, `run.cancelled`/`run.failed`), so `usageStatus: "provider-not-reported"` agrees with the recorded stream. This issue is about turns that ran and were not carried into the ledger, not about inventing numbers for runs that made no model call.

## 2. Expected behaviour

1. The ledger reconciles with the provider. For a run of N main turns plus delegated children, the row set for that run must sum to (or be explicitly reconcilable to) the N + ΣM per-turn figures the provider reported and the engine already recorded.
2. Delegated work is attributable. A subagent's model turns are spend of the same run; they need their own `invocationId` and a kind that distinguishes them from the parent's `task`, so a user can answer "what did the delegation cost" — today the answer is only reachable from CAS blobs.
3. A row's figures must describe the row's scope. If one row per invocation is kept as the shape, its tokens have to be the sum over that invocation's turns with the turn count recorded (the engine already returns `turns`), so the duration window and the token window agree.
4. The channel feeding the ledger stays observable. Either the per-turn `model_usage` figures are persisted, or per-turn rows exist — one of the two must hold, so that a reviewer can recompute a stored figure without reading the internal state pool.
5. `provider-not-reported` keeps its current meaning: unknown is recorded as unknown, never as zero. The same discipline this repository already states for the evolve proxy (`evolution/llm-proxy.ts:273-275`).

## 3. Source code

Paths relative to the repository root; all quoted at main `a773942a` / `bec6399d` (identical, §8).

**The engine produces one figure per turn and keeps only the last.**

- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:286` — `let usage: TUsage | undefined;` declared *outside* the turn loop that starts at `:296` (`for (let turn = 0; turn < this.options.maxModelTurns; turn += 1) {`).
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:334-337` — inside the loop, per turn:
  ```
  if (modelTurn.usage !== undefined) {
    usage = modelTurn.usage;
    this.emit({ type: "model_usage", usage });
  }
  ```
  Reassignment, not accumulation; the same pair repeats in the output-recovery retry at `:367-370`.
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:380-384` (normal completion), `:418-419` (suspended return), `:428-432` (turn-budget return) — every exit ships `...(usage !== undefined ? { usage } : {})`, so `AgentLoopResult.usage` is structurally the last turn's usage. `:428-430` shows the result *does* know the count it does not carry: `turns: this.options.maxModelTurns`.

**The agent wrapper forwards that single figure once.**

- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts:647` `let reportedModelUsage = false;`, `:700` `if (event.type === "model_usage") reportedModelUsage = true;`, `:857-858` re-emits each per-turn event upstream (`case "model_usage": emit({ type: "model_usage", usage: event.usage, usageReported: true });`).
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts:715-717`:
  ```
  const usage = result.usage;
  if (!reportedModelUsage) this.emit({ type: "model_usage", ...(usage ? { usage, usageReported: true } : { usageReported: false }) });
  if (usage) this.emit({ type: "usage", usage });
  ```
  The `type: "usage"` event is the terminal, whole-agent figure — one per agent, and (see next) one turn's worth of tokens.

**The run collector holds one overwritten slot, and that slot is what gets persisted.**

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:1069` `let lastAgentUsage = unreportedModelUsage();` — one variable for the whole run.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2387-2390`:
  ```
  if (event.type === "model_usage") {
    lastAgentUsage = capturedModelUsage(event);
    return;
  }
  ```
  Overwrite per turn, and the early `return` means no `publish(...)` runs for this event type — which is why the persisted stream has 0 `model_usage` records while carrying 20 per-turn usage payloads.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2504` resets the slot to `unreportedModelUsage()` immediately before the run; `:2557` `const taskUsage = lastAgentUsage;`.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2591-2598` (completed), `:2653-2660` (cancelled), `:2700-2707` (failed) — the only three persistence calls on this path, each `invocationKind: "task"`, each passing the same single-slot `usage`. Repo-wide symbol search for `appendModelUsageForManifest` returns three files: its definition, `runs/index.ts` (those call sites), and `services/api/src/http/index.ts:303-306`, which is a re-export list, not a caller. There is no writer in the subagent execution path.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2109-2114` — the child bridge:
  ```
  if (event.type === "usage") {
    subagent.usage = event.usage;
    finalizeMessageStep();
    void emit({ subagentId: subagent.id, type: "subagent.usage", usage: event.usage });
  ```
  A child's whole-run figure becomes one parent-stream event and one field on the subagent record. It is never handed to `appendModelUsageForManifest`, so children cannot appear in the ledger.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3190-3210` — the other direct writer (`invocationKind: "session-naming"`), also `costUsd: null`.

**The record itself has nowhere to put turn granularity.**

- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:27-35` `CapturedModelUsage` (six token fields + `usageStatus`), `:37-47` `unreportedModelUsage()`, `:49-70` `capturedModelUsage(event)` (returns the event's figures verbatim, or the all-null `provider-not-reported` shape).
- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:72-83` — `appendModelUsageForManifest`'s `options` are `attemptIndex / invocationId / invocationKind / manifest / outcome / runId / usage`: no turn index, no turn count.
- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:85-108` — the record built from them, with `costUsd: null` at `:89`, `finishedAt: options.manifest.finishedAt` at `:90`, `startedAt: options.manifest.createdAt` at `:105`. This is exactly the run-window-plus-one-turn mixture described in §1 item 3.
- `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:167-191` — `ModelInvocationUsage` has `invocationId` (`:175`) and `invocationKind` (`:176`) and no `turnId`, no `turnCount`. `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:152-162` — `ModelInvocationKind` is `delegation-track | evolve | paper-vision | review-correction | semantic-review | session-naming | task`: no subagent member, and repo-wide literal search for `delegation-track` returns its declaration only, i.e. no writer uses that kind. The manifests are not a workaround either: `runs/index.ts:2587` (and `:2649`, `:2696`) set `turnId: runId`, so the "turn" identifier in the manifest is the run.
- Read side is faithful to its input: `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:57-71` (`addUsageToBucket`) and `:414-448` (`summarizeModelUsageAnalytics`, which sums `usage.inputTokens` per row) and `:385-412` (`estimateInvocationCost`, per row). Nothing here mis-adds — the turns are simply absent from the input. `ModelUsageBucket.invocationCount` (`packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:198`) counts rows, so a 20-turn run and a 1-turn run both count as 1.

**Per-call rows already exist in this codebase.**

- `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts:126` `handleEvolveCompletion`, `:162` `const startedAt = new Date().toISOString();`, `:233` `const usage = await recordUsage(deps, grant, model, payload, startedAt);`, `:245-278` `recordUsage(...)` → `parseProviderUsage(payload.usage, …)` then one `appendModelInvocationUsage` per proxied completion, keyed `invocationId: \`evolve:${grant.runId}\`` with its own kind and the comment at `:262-263` justifying a separate kind precisely because "a search's spend is not a chat turn". The same argument applies between a parent's turns and a child's, and between turn 1 and turn 20.

## 4. Real run evidence

One captured session on the integration instance (Native executor, `invocationKind: "task"` rows). Sources: the instance data directory's `model-usage/<sessionId>.json`, `run-events/<sessionId>/<runId>/*.jsonl`, and the per-turn payloads resolved through `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/` (the `payloadRef` of each `model.completed` record). Read-only instruments: `rpH7-persisted-vs-perturN.txt`, `rpH22-e6-usage-census.txt`, `rpH24-e6-usage-events.txt` under `runs/JD/TASK-001/artifacts/`. No credentials or host paths are reproduced below.

Ledger contents for the session (`model-usage/bb1d6797-1270-4bb9-a1a3-a464a5bc141e.json`, 5 rows, all `invocationKind: "task"`, all `costUsd: null`, one row per run):

```
run=9ceeb1f9 outcome=completed usageStatus=reported              in=44952 out=11430 reasoning=6282 cacheRead=3584 total=56382
             startedAt=2026-11-11T02:27:15.507Z finishedAt=2026-11-11T05:18:14.695Z manifest=63d20e49
run=82036958 outcome=cancelled  usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=10:29:00.882Z finishedAt=10:32:45.359Z
run=116b288e outcome=cancelled  usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=10:38:39.403Z finishedAt=10:42:15.250Z
run=de7527c9 outcome=failed     usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=11:31:22.799Z finishedAt=11:33:44.840Z
run=0673152f outcome=completed  usageStatus=reported              in=47387 out=1307  reasoning=310  cacheRead=3584 total=48694
             startedAt=2026-11-11T11:51:15.241Z finishedAt=2026-11-11T12:03:34.525Z manifest=c2220e9c
```

Per-turn usage recorded in the streams of the same session, by stream:

```
run 9ceeb1f9
  MAIN     turns_with_usage=20   sum(in=817210  out=39005)  first(turn=0  in=24831 out=81   at=02:27:17)  last(turn=19 in=44952 out=11430 at=05:18:13.942)
  sub a426c709 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5297320 out=126948) last(turn=127 in=32017 out=144  at=03:09:44)
  sub c7d68122 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5188821 out=74992)  last(turn=127 in=44707 out=116  at=04:05:29)
  sub c59905d7 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5267215 out=98987)  last(turn=127 in=39699 out=461  at=04:38:24)
  sub b95116e3 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5055291 out=100647) last(turn=127 in=43520 out=412  at=05:12:26)
  sub ceb12354 turns_with_usage=60   sum(in=2398037 out=75464)  last(turn=59  in=41592 out=9484 at=03:28:28)
  per-turn usage records: 592 (MAIN=20, subagents=572)   sums: in=24023894 out=516043 reasoning=395528 cacheRead=13174272
  MAIN last turn in=44952 out=11430   persisted row in=44952 out=11430   EQUAL=True
  which per-turn records match the persisted row exactly: [('MAIN', 19)]      row == sum over all streams? False

run 0673152f
  MAIN     turns_with_usage=7    sum(in=300115 out=10822)  first(turn=0 in=31442 out=314 at=11:52:38)  last(turn=6 in=47387 out=1307 at=12:03:32)
  (no subagent streams in this run)
  MAIN last turn in=47387 out=1307   persisted row in=47387 out=1307   EQUAL=True
  which per-turn records match the persisted row exactly: [('MAIN', 6)]       row == sum over all streams? False
```

Which channel the ledger's own numbers arrive on, and what the parent stream holds about children (`main.jsonl` event-type census):

```
run 9ceeb1f9 main.jsonl: {"assistant.thinking.delta":309, "assistant.delta":67, "agent.record":60, "tool.started":43,
                          "tool.completed":43, "plan.updated":26, "record:model.completed":20, "subagent.updated":15,
                          "subagent.usage":5, …}
  events of type model_usage: 0        events carrying a usage dict: 5 (all type=subagent.usage)
    in=32017 out=144  -> matches child a426c709 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=41592 out=9484 -> matches child ceb12354 turn 59  (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=44707 out=116  -> matches child c7d68122 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=39699 out=461  -> matches child c59905d7 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=43520 out=412  -> matches child b95116e3 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
run 0673152f main.jsonl: {"record:model.completed":7, "agent.record":21, "tool.started":9, …}
  events of type model_usage: 0        events carrying a usage dict: 0
```

So, in one place each: 20 and 7 per-turn figures exist for the parent and 1 survives; 572 per-turn figures exist for the children and 0 reach the ledger while 5 (their last turns) reach the parent stream; and the ledger's surviving figure never appears in the stream as a `model_usage` event, exactly as `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` predicts.

Control for the "are the nulls wrong?" question: the three null-token runs' main streams contain `run.queued: 1, run.started: 1, run.status: 2` plus `run.cancelled: 1` (or `run.failed: 1`) and 0 `model.completed` records — no turn ran, so `provider-not-reported` is accurate and those rows are not counted as losses anywhere in this report.

## 5. Trigger conditions

- **Always, on the Native agent path.** 5 of 5 runs in the captured session produced exactly one row, and 2 of 2 runs that executed model turns produced a row equal to their last main turn. Any run of more than one turn under-reports.
- **Worst exactly where the platform's value is.** A delegated research run lost 572 of 592 turn records (96.62 %) to the missing subagent rows; the more children and the closer they run to the engine's turn ceiling, the larger the blind spot. (`MAX_MODEL_TURNS = 128` at `native-agent/index.ts:102`, applied at `:656` — four of the five children here hit 128.)
- **Not provider-dependent.** The provider reported usage for every turn in these runs; the loss is between the engine and the writer, not at the wire.
- **Not platform-dependent.** No cited line branches on OS; the only Windows-specific code in the chain is unrelated.
- **Silently distorts anything derived from the ledger** — cost estimates (`estimateInvocationCost` per row, `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:385-412`), per-run spend ranking, and the run-duration pairing in §1 item 3 — because the read side trusts the row set.

## 6. Difference from existing Issues and PRs

- **#103** (closed 2026-09-21, `[Feature] Reuse JiuwenSwarm backend - sub-task: Usage`, labels `help wanted`, `priority/major`, `release/0.3.0`) is a *porting* task: bring the JiuwenSwarm backend's usage capability to this repository. It says nothing about how many rows a Native agent run writes or which turn a row describes, and its subject is the swarm gateway path — where, per the symbol search in §3, there is no ledger writer at all. This draft is about the Native executor's writer, whose whole chain (`runtime-core` → `native-agent` → `runs/index.ts` → `model-usage/index.ts`) post-dates #103's scope. **Not the same request.**
- **#304** (open PR, `fix: parse usage by protocol and keep real E2E accounting non-gating`, created 2026-10-14) changes `.ci/README.md` plus three test files (`packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`, `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts`) and touches no production writer. Its stated principle — missing accounting is diagnostic evidence, not evidence of zero cost — is the same principle §2 item 5 asks this Issue to preserve, and its body explicitly notes that the protocol-aware parser already lives on main in `packages/model/src/usage.ts` (`normalizeUsage`). It resolves *how a reported figure is parsed*, never *how many figures are stored*. **Adjacent, not duplicate.**
- **#783 / #789** (closed) and **#811** (closed PR `fix(model): preserve reasoning token diagnostics`) are arithmetic/diagnostic correctness on a figure that is already in the row: cached-prompt double-charging (fixed at `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:392-398`) and reasoning-token preservation. They assume the row's token fields are the run's true counts. That assumption is what this report measures and finds false for multi-turn and delegated runs.
- **#858 / #861 / #873 / #882 / #912** (closed) and **#509 / #575** (open) concern the usage page's headers, date presets, formatting and entry points — display-layer scoping of the stored rows. Nothing proposes or performs a change to `appendModelUsageForManifest`.
- **#330** (closed, session timeline showing tokens) and **#854 / #550** (closed, subagent panel) consume the per-child `subagent.usage` figure; they establish that the child's *last-turn* number is already user-visible while the ledger holds nothing at all about children. That is the display/record asymmetry §2 item 2 asks to close, not a prior report of it.
- **#963** (closed PR, record judge tokens, session tokens and tool calls on the real-case table) writes a CI artifact in the benchmark pipeline, not `ModelInvocationUsage`.
- Searches run against the live repository index: `usage granularity` → 2 records, neither relevant; `ModelInvocationUsage` → #783, #811; `usage ledger` → #304, #963, #330, #789 among others, none about persistence granularity; `subagent usage` → no record stating that a child's model turns are absent from the usage ledger. No record proposes per-turn or per-model-call rows for the Native agent path.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. **Reconciliation.** For a Native run of N main turns, the stored rows for that `runId` sum to the provider-reported per-turn figures the engine emitted for it (or the difference is an explicit, named state, e.g. `turnsRecorded` vs `turnsTotal`). A test with N ≥ 3 asserts the sum, not the last value.
2. **Children are in the ledger.** A run that delegates to K subagents stores their turn spend with its own `invocationId` and a kind distinguishable from the parent's `task` — either a new `ModelInvocationKind` member or a writer for the already-declared but unused `delegation-track` (`packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:152-162`) — plus the parent linkage that today exists only as `subagentId` on the stream event.
3. **Scope agreement.** Whichever shape is chosen, a row's token fields describe the same scope as its `startedAt`/`finishedAt`. If one row per run is retained, its tokens are the run's sums and the row carries the turn count the engine already returns (`runtime.ts:418`, `:430`).
4. **Recomputable from persisted evidence.** Either `model_usage` figures reach the run's stream (remove the pre-publish `return` at `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` or publish a distinct record) or per-turn rows exist — one of the two, so a reviewer can recompute any stored figure from the record directory alone.
5. **Unknown stays unknown.** A run with zero completed model turns keeps `usageStatus: "provider-not-reported"` with null fields, per §4's control and #304's stated policy; the fix must not materialise zeros.
6. **Derived figures follow.** With rows corrected, `summarizeModelUsageAnalytics` and `estimateInvocationCost` need no change; add a test that a 20-turn delegated run's estimated cost is roughly 20×-plus-children that of a 1-turn run, so a regression to last-turn-only persistence fails loudly.
7. **Docstring parity.** The `ModelInvocationUsage` comment space or the usage page documents what a row means after the change, since "invocation" today silently denotes "run" on one path and "call" on the evolve path.

## 8. Version this draft measured

- SD main while writing: `bec6399dc18afe8885af94080988d5e28538f4b8` (2026-11-11T12:27:01Z). Anchor baseline used for line numbers: `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` (PR #1095 squash, 2026-11-11T11:40:15Z). Compare between them touches three files under `apps/desktop/` only.
- Blob identities (12-hex Git blob prefixes) — identical at both main SHAs *and* identical to the downstream fork the evidence was produced on (`30178fda7…`, read-only `rev-parse HEAD:<path>`):

  | file | blob at main `bec6399d` | blob at main `a773942a` | blob at the fork we run |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts` | `05ab55482858` | `05ab55482858` | `05ab55482858` |
  | `services/api/src/model-usage.ts` | `812d797dafe5` | `812d797dafe5` | `812d797dafe5` |
  | `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts` | `3a88f4fca5d1` | `3a88f4fca5d1` | `3a88f4fca5d1` |
  | `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` | `ad02eef4fe78` | `ad02eef4fe78` | `ad02eef4fe78` |
  | `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts` | `e243aef3821a` | `e243aef3821a` | `e243aef3821a` |
  | `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts` | `16c0bc9490e8` | `16c0bc9490e8` | `16c0bc9490e8` |
  | `packages/model/src/usage.ts` | `40cc9f5d68a1` | `40cc9f5d68a1` | `40cc9f5d68a1` |
  | `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts` | `c447143bc700` | `c447143bc700` | `c447143bc700` |
  | `services/api/src/http/index.ts` | — | — | re-export list at `:303-306` read at `bec6399d` |

  So this is upstream main behaviour, not a downstream fork difference.
- Main source files were read through the GitHub contents API pinned to each `?ref=<sha>` (the local upstream clone used earlier in this round no longer exists on disk); the fork's blobs were read with a read-only `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` / `git show HEAD:<path>`.

## Limitations of this report

- Run evidence is one session (5 runs, 2 of them multi-turn) on a Windows host. The 1-of-N collapse and the missing `model_usage` events were reproduced in both multi-turn runs and follow directly from code with no platform branch, but we have not measured the same shape on Linux or with the JiuwenSwarm executor.
- Per-turn figures were recovered from the `payloadRef` of each persisted `model.completed` record (the agent-state CAS). We verified that the ledger row equals one of those records; we did not verify them against provider invoices, so "what the provider reported" here means "what the provider reported per turn into this pipeline".
- The instance executes the build product of the fork at `30178fda7…`. We proved the *source* blobs for every cited file match main; we did not byte-verify the compiled `dist/` of this cited module against that source.
- `costUsd` is null in every row this writer produces (`model-usage/index.ts:89`, and `runs/index.ts:3194` for the naming path). Cost is an estimate made at read time from pricing tables; the §5 claim that cost inherits the undercount is derived from that code path, not from a usage-page measurement — we did not exercise the analytics UI.
- We report that subagent turns are absent from the ledger. We do not claim a specific row-count target (per-turn vs per-invocation-with-sum-and-count): §2 and §7 state the properties, and leave the shape to the maintainers.
- The 128-turn ceiling that inflated this particular loss (four children cut at 128) is a separate finding with its own draft, and neither draft depends on the other's fix.

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**现象**：在会话里让模型「帮我打开 UniProt 这个 MCP 服务器」，模型发起 `connector.enable` 请求（scope = 本次会话，激活模式 same_run）。界面弹出「启用连接器」卡片，但正文只有一句「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，可用动作只有「关闭」，既没有确认/拒绝，也没有跳转到设置的入口。关闭后该请求被记为拒绝，模型回复「未启用 —— 本次会话中没有打开 UniProt MCP 服务器」，并声明不会再就同一配置需求重新发起请求。

**复现步骤**
1. 新建会话，输入「帮我打开 UniProt 这个 MCP 服务器」
2. 模型调用 configuration 工具的 `connector.enable`（describe → propose）发起启用请求
3. 会话内出现「启用连接器」卡片：正文「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，只有「关闭」按钮
4. 点击「关闭」后卡片变为「启用连接器 · 暂不配置 · 原任务已完成」，模型回复连接器未启用（`sessionEnabled=false`），整个任务中 UniProt 工具均不可用

**代码定位（main，2026-11-11）**
- 卡片正文来自 packages/configuration-ui/src/messages.ts 的 `compact.unavailable`「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」；当 compact 卡片被归为 `unsupported` 时，ConfigurationRequestCard.tsx 中 `collapsedEditor = compact?.unsupported` 为真，编辑器被收起，只留「关闭」。
- 归类逻辑在 apps/desktop/src/app/configuration-presentation.ts 的 `connector.enable` 分支：仅当 `state === "awaiting_confirmation"` 且有 `previewDigest`（即 ready），且 `enabledConnectorIds` 的 before/after 能解析为「精确新增一个 id」时才返回 `{ connectorAddition: true }`，其余一律 `{ unsupported: true }`。
- 对比：apps/web 有专门的会话内连接器卡片（ConversationalConnectorCard.tsx）可以批准；桌面端没有对应实现，而 `unsupported` 兜底文案里的「原版界面」在桌面安装包里并不存在，用户无处可点。

**期望行为**
- 桌面端支持在会话内批准 `connector.enable`（session scope / same_run），至少提供「启用 / 不启用」两个明确动作，并在启用后让本次运行拿到该连接器工具
- 若确实暂不支持，卡片应给出可操作入口（如「前往 设置 → MCP/连接器」），而不是「请用原版界面」；同时应明确提供「拒绝」，避免模型把「关闭卡片」当成用户拒绝并不再重试
- 该能力在桌面端不可用时，不应让模型发起这类请求；至少提示用户只能在设置页手动开启

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- 应用：ScienceDiscovery 桌面版（Windows x64）
- 系统：Windows 11 专业版 25H2（10.0.26200）
- 界面语言：中文
- 场景：会话内让模型启用 UniProt MCP 连接器（connector.enable，session scope，same_run）

### Additional Information

两张截图：
1. 对话中的「启用连接器」卡片：正文「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，右下角只有「关闭」
2. 关闭后的回执「启用连接器 · 暂不配置 · 原任务已完成」，以及模型的结论：未启用，已提交的 connector.enable 请求被拒绝，UniProt 连接器保持 sessionEnabled=false

### Version Information

- 版本：0.3.0 日包（daily build）
- 构建时间：2026-11-11T00:15:34Z（安装目录 resources/version.json 的 builtAt，其中 repoCommit 为 unknown）
- 安装方式：Windows x64 安装包

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Background Description

ScienceDiscovery already has trusted, build-time installed plugins. This issue defines how to evolve that implementation into a clearer, maintainable extension architecture without breaking existing execution, permissions, settings, or historical data.

Current implementation:
- `packages/plugin-sdk` defines manifests, service contracts, configuration, and create/start/dispose lifecycle. Plugin scopes resolve dependencies and clean up failed activation in reverse order.
- Runtime contributions include tools, context factories, state providers, batch policies, and optional result submission.
- Skill, MCP, scheduler, Plan, source connectors, and JSON artifact viewing have plugin entry points.
- Settings inherit across global/project/session scopes; Run composition is frozen at execution start.
- Web extensions have settings, project-view, and artifact-viewer registration points.

Remaining boundaries:
- `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts` and `runtime.ts` explicitly register installed packages and wire their factories. New plugins still require host/build integration.
- Some capabilities reuse Workspace factories; some domain control-plane logic remains in the API host.
- The contribution contract does not allow general replacement of AgentLoop or the harness.
- Native and JiuwenSwarm use different loop/context execution paths. Plugin registration alone does not establish equivalent behavior across backends.
- Plugins are trusted in-process code; manifest permissions do not provide code isolation.

This issue delivers an architecture proposal and implementation breakdown. Dynamic installation, hot reload, and runtime replacement are options to assess, not implementation commitments.

## Design Ideas

1. **Preserve the existing capability model.** Keep domain-owned packages, public exports, explicit Ports, and one authoritative state store. Avoid exposing the whole Store or NativeAgent through a global container.
2. **Separate installation from activation.** Describe the flow as installed package → dependency/service/permission checks → effective scoped settings → frozen Run composition → lifecycle → contributions. Keep installed, available, authorized, and active states distinct.
3. **Reduce duplicate registration.** Evaluate build-time generation of separate API and client catalogs from an installation description. Server factories must not leak into browser bundles. Compare this with retaining explicit registration before selecting an approach.
4. **Define backend capabilities explicitly.** Produce a native/JiuwenSwarm matrix for every contribution type. Unsupported combinations must be rejected or diagnosed explicitly. Main, child, and reviewer agents must use the same frozen selection, with documented role-specific behavior.
5. **Add replaceable contracts only for concrete needs.** Evaluate runtime backend, model, and execution-provider seams. Specify cancellation, events, recovery, tool permissions, and artifact/result submission before proposing a new interface.
6. **Retain Run stability.** Configuration changes affect subsequent Runs. Evaluate draining old instances before disposal; an upgrade must not mix implementations inside a running composition. Define package/API/state-schema versions separately and retain historical read support.
7. **Make conflicts deterministic.** Specify tool-name collision handling, context budget allocation, batch-policy ordering, result-submission ownership, and dependency-disable behavior.

Options to compare:

| Option | Scope | Main tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Strengthen current capability plugins | Catalog consistency, Ports, diagnostics, lifecycle contracts | Lowest migration cost; host integration remains controlled |
| Add replaceable harness contracts | Backend/model/execution seams driven by concrete use cases | More flexibility; requires cross-backend semantic contracts |
| Introduce dynamic distribution | Package resolution, installation, client assets, upgrades and rollback | Largest operational and compatibility cost; untrusted code requires isolation |

Recommended starting direction: strengthen the current mechanism, then add narrowly scoped replacement contracts. Record evidence and alternatives in an architecture decision before choosing dynamic distribution.

## Involved Public APIs

This analysis does not change public APIs. Inventory and assess compatibility for:
- `PluginManifest`, `PluginDefinition`, `PluginInstance`, and `createPluginScope` in `packages/plugin-sdk`.
- `RuntimeContribution` in `packages/plugin-sdk/src/runtime.ts`.
- Plugin settings and scoped Bridge under `/api/projects/:projectId/plugins`, including configuration revisions, query/command authorization, and events.
- Domain package `./plugin`, `./manifest`, and `./web` exports.

Any proposed API change must include consumer impact, versioning, migration, and failure behavior. Distinguish proposed interfaces from contracts already implemented.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Relationship and analysis responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/plugin-sdk` | Manifest, lifecycle, negotiation, services, configuration and Bridge contracts |
| `services/api/src/plugins` | Installation catalog, factory wiring, scoped settings and control plane |
| `services/api/src/native-agent` | Run composition, contribution assembly, lifecycle and backend integration |
| `packages/runtime-core`, `packages/tools` | Loop invariants, tool execution, permissions, cancellation and result ownership |
| `packages/context` | StateView capture, state schema/revision, projection consistency and context budgets |
| `packages/workspace`, capability packages | Remaining factory coupling; domain Ports and ownership; avoid duplicate tool injection |
| JiuwenSwarm integration and adapter | Backend capability parity, event translation, cancellation and recovery boundaries |
| `apps/web/src/plugins` | Current UI registration, authenticated Bridge and server/client import separation |
| `apps/desktop` | Inventory actual client extension needs and current coverage; do not assume Web registration automatically applies |
| Store, CAS, Recorder and provenance | Settings transactions, frozen composition metadata and historical readability |
| Build and architecture checks | Package exports, dependency cycles, distribution completeness and browser-safe entry points |

## Test Design and Test Plan

The following cases are proposed validation requirements for follow-up implementation. They are not claims of tests executed by this analysis. Map each case to existing coverage first, then identify additions.

| Layer / case | Setup or action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit: dependency validation | Missing/disabled dependency, duplicate ID, dependency cycle or incompatible service | Deterministic failure before unsupported contributions execute; useful plugin-specific diagnostic |
| Unit: lifecycle failure | Factory/start throws after earlier instances acquire resources | Created resources released once in reverse order; cleanup failures remain observable |
| Unit: cancellation | Cancel during start or tool execution, then dispose | Cancellation reaches async work; no remaining listeners, timers or child work |
| Unit: configuration | Combine global/project/session overrides, including explicit disable and inheritance | Correct effective settings; invalid fields rejected; existing Run stays unchanged |
| Unit: conflicts | Register duplicate tool names or competing policies/result owners | The documented conflict rule is enforced deterministically |
| Unit: state projection | Change live state after checkpoint capture; supply missing or incompatible state | Context and Recorder use the fixed checkpoint; incompatible state fails explicitly |
| Integration: backend matrix | Exercise each contribution through native and JiuwenSwarm | Supported contributions have observable effects; unsupported combinations produce explicit diagnostics |
| Integration: scope consistency | Start main, child and reviewer agents; change settings mid-Run | All use the frozen selection; only subsequent Runs use new settings |
| Integration: settings writes | Concurrent updates and stale expectedRevision through existing write paths | Existing transaction/CAS behavior preserved; conflicts do not partially apply configuration |
| Integration: package boundaries | Build API/client entries and run dependency checks | No reverse host imports, package cycles, duplicate registration or Node-only imports in browser entries |
| E2E: enable/disable journey | Configure a capability → run → disable → start another Run → open previous output | Disabled capability contributes no new execution; historical Plan/artifacts remain readable |
| E2E: clients | Exercise supported settings/view paths through Web and desktop | Scope and authorization preserved; client support gaps documented rather than silently hidden |
| Upgrade/recovery | Load a historical checkpoint after a plugin/schema change or failed upgrade | Supported migration/read path succeeds; unsupported versions fail clearly without corrupting history |

For implementation follow-ups, select affected UT/ST/E2E suites and run `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and affected builds. Record exact commands, results, and backend evidence. Real model/connector journeys are required only where mocks cannot establish backend or external execution semantics. Documentation-only analysis does not claim runtime validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Publish a source-linked inventory of implemented extension points, registration paths and remaining coupling, including Web/desktop coverage.
- [ ] Publish a native/JiuwenSwarm contribution matrix with evidence, unsupported cases and links to follow-up gaps; coordinate backend findings with #572.
- [ ] Record an architecture decision comparing the three options in migration cost, security, deployment, compatibility and maintenance; explain the chosen scope and rejected alternatives.
- [ ] Define lifecycle ownership, in-flight work handling, conflict rules, settings consistency, Run version freezing and historical state compatibility.
- [ ] Describe one minimal capability integration end to end: package exports, installation, Ports, contributions, UI entry, build and verification.
- [ ] Map the test cases above to existing tests and proposed additions, with observable pass/fail conditions and responsible modules.
- [ ] Break implementation into bounded follow-up issues with dependencies, migration/rollback considerations and validation gates.
- [ ] Review the proposal against existing permission, approval, storage and execution semantics; unresolved decisions have explicit owners and follow-up items.

## Additional Information

- Current architecture: `docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/plugins.md`.
- #572 covers remaining plugin delivery/acceptance for JiuwenSwarm reuse; reuse its findings without duplicating implementation scope.
- Dynamic package installation, plugin marketplaces, untrusted in-process code, and arbitrary live AgentLoop mutation are outside this issue's implementation scope; any future adoption requires a separate reviewed proposal.
